The role
The NMS team at the Construction Research Centre is looking for a Specification Writer to support our Construction Research Centre. The Specification Writer would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
As part of the NMS team, the Specification Writer will contribute to the ongoing development, enhancement, and publication of Canada’s National Master Construction Specification (NMS). a cornerstone resource for architects, engineers, and construction professionals across the country.
The NMS is a comprehensive template system used to develop design and construction specifications for the Canadian built environment, including buildings and infrastructure. It contains more than 17,000 pages of technical content organized into over 850 documents. The NMS is widely adopted by the Government of Canada, as well as provincial, territorial, and broader public‑sector organizations, to support the efficient creation of consistent, high‑quality project specifications.
The incumbent will work closely with NMS technical advisors, English editors, and administrators to ensure the accuracy, consistency, and quality of NMS documents. They will apply expertise in specification writing, building science, and construction documentation to produce and maintain high‑quality master specifications that reflect the latest codes, standards, and industry best practices.
Key Activities:
- Write, edit, and review NMS master specifications for accuracy, clarity, and adherence to NRC’s quality and formatting standards.
- Perform quality assurance reviews.
- Collaborate with technical advisors, English editors, and translators to integrate updates from codes, standards, and research findings.
- Maintain consistency with NMS conventions, including MasterFormat, UniFormat, and SectionFormat.
- Analyze feedback from users, industry partners, and regulatory stakeholders to improve NMS documents.
- Participate in the continuous improvement of workflows, metadata management, and content validation in NMS publication cycles.
- Mentor junior team members on specification writing principles and NMS guidelines.
- Contribute to the development of new documents to address emerging best practices, climate resiliency, and sustainability practices.
- Support publication activities in collaboration with the NMS Specification Administrator and the Production and Marketing (P&M) team.
- Perform data entry of NMS documents into an XML database as required.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Diploma or degree in Architectural/Civil, Building Science Technology, or a related field.
Certification as a Construction Specifications Canada, Registered Specification Writer (RSW), or Certified Construction Contract Administrator (CCCA), Certified Specification Practitioner (CSP); or Construction Specification Institute, Certified Construction Specifier (CCS) or Construction Document Technologist (CDT) would be considered an asset.
An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Significant experience writing, editing, and reviewing construction specifications as part of regular professional duties.
- Demonstrated knowledge of specification formats such as MasterFormat, UniFormat, and SectionFormat.
- Experience coordinating interdisciplinary input from architects, engineers, and other technical specialists.
- Experience preparing and maintaining master construction specifications, would be considered an asset.
- Demonstrated knowledge in construction contract administration, would be considered an asset.
- Experience using digital collaboration tools (e.g., SharePoint, Teamwork) and content management systems for technical publication cycles, would be considered an asset.
- Experience with sustainable design or construction sustainability certification programs (e.g., LEED®, WELL™) would be considered an asset.

Technical competencies

- Ability to identify the impact of changes in standards, codes, technology or industry practices on specifications.
- Broad technical knowledge across architectural and engineering disciplines relevant to building design and construction.
- Working knowledge of contract law principles as they apply to construction procurement and project delivery.
- Strong understanding of specification language, construction terminology, construction law, and English grammar.
- Working knowledge of construction specification writing style, formatting, and classification systems (MasterFormat, SectionFormat, PageFormat, and UniFormat).

JOB OVERVIEW In this role, you will provide expert ecological and environmental guidance to support the planning, design, implementation and monitoring of National Capital Commission (NCC) construction and future development initiatives, ensuring activities and decisions comply with federal, provincial and regional environmental legislation, policies, regulatory requirements and contract documents. You will contribute to the protection and stewardship of natural resources by assessing environmental effects, recommending mitigation strategies, and supporting permitting, compliance and conservation initiatives, while delivering scientific analysis and technical advice. Working collaboratively with internal teams, consultants, contractors and regulators, you will help ensure initiatives are carried out in an environmentally responsible and sustainable manner.
ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS EDUCATION A degree from a recognized post-secondary institution with acceptable specialization in biology, ecology, environmental studies, environmental science or an acceptable combination of education, training and experience.
EXPERIENCE Five (05) to eight (08) years of experience working as a biologist in natural resource management, ecological or biological consulting, environmental impact assessment, applied research, and field work.
KNOWLEDGE • Of conducting ecological studies and field work • Of pre-, syn- and post-construction-phase inspection and monitoring protocols • Of federal and provincial environmental legislation and regulatory frameworks • Of ecological and biological geospatial data analysis tools • Of the NCC and its mandate, mission, policies and role in project oversight in the National Capital Region
ABILITIES • To manage, update, interpret, manipulate and analyze natural resources and environmental data, ecological information, and produce accurate maps, figures and spatial products • To assess on-site environmental issues and environmental effects, analyze field findings, interpret monitoring results, evaluate the feasibility of permit or approval conditions, and determine appropriate implementation strategies. • To investigate, research, analyze and interpret technical and regulatory information to recommend practical and compliant solutions throughout project development and execution.
COMPETENCIES • Demonstrating integrity and respect – Civility and well-being. • Thinking things through – Innovating through analysis and ideas. • Working effectively with others – Relationships and trust building. • Showing initiative and being action-oriented – Getting things done.
CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT • Possess or eligible to obtain Secret security clearance. • Linguistic profile: Bilingual BBB. • Position is in the National Capital Region. The person selected for this position must reside within a commutable distance from the workplace. • The National Capital Commission offers a hybrid and flexible work environment.

Business Improvement Lead
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
About the role
As the Business Improvement Lead, you will play a key, hands-on leadership role in advancing the Bank’s Unclaimed Properties Office’s (UPO) modernization roadmap. Reporting to the Director, Unclaimed Properties Office, you will help drive the implementation of Lean Review recommendations and support modernization, automation, process improvement, and operational excellence initiatives that strengthen UPO’s effectiveness, scalability, and readiness for future growth.
You will work closely with the Project Manager, business leaders, subject matter experts, corporate partners, and vendors to translate opportunities for improvement into practical solutions that deliver measurable and sustainable business outcomes. You will also act as a catalyst for innovation by identifying opportunities to leverage AI, automation, data, and digital tools to improve service delivery, reduce manual effort, and enhance the client experience.
What you will do
In this role, you will lead and support initiatives that improve how UPO works, delivers services, makes decisions, and prepares for future growth. You will help move ideas from concept to implementation while ensuring improvements are practical, sustainable, and aligned with strategic priorities.
More specifically, you will:
- Lead the implementation of priority Lean Review recommendations and operational improvement initiatives.
- Assess current-state processes and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, governance, service delivery, and operational outcomes.
- Apply Lean and continuous improvement methodologies to eliminate waste, reduce rework, simplify processes, and improve the way work gets done.
- Support the develop of future-state process designs, process maps, workflow documentation, standard operating procedures, tools, templates, and guidance materials.
- Identify opportunities to leverage automation, AI, and digital solutions, and develop business cases, requirements, pilots, and implementation recommendations.
- Work with Privacy, Legal, Risk, Data and Digital Services, Information Technology Services, and other enabling functions to assess operational and implementation considerations, identify potential considerations, and develop practical solutions that support successful implementation.
- Support the development of dashboards, reporting requirements, performance measures, and data-informed recommendations.
- Facilitate workshops, working sessions, and stakeholder consultations to support solution design, implementation planning, and business readiness.
- Promote a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, innovation, and operational excellence.
What you need to succeed
You are an experienced business improvement professional who has successfully led process improvement, operational excellence, business transformation, or continuous improvement initiatives. You bring a strong understanding of Lean, continuous improvement, operational excellence, business process improvement, or similar methodologies, and you know how to apply them in a practical way to improve how work gets done.
You are skilled at assessing current-state processes, identifying root causes, mapping workflows, designing future-state solutions, and developing recommendations that are clear, actionable, and aligned with business priorities. You can translate analysis into practical implementation plans, business requirements, briefing materials, and executive-level advice that support sound decision making.
You are also a strong communicator and facilitator who can build trusted relationships with diverse stakeholders and partner groups. You are comfortable influencing outcomes without direct authority, managing multiple priorities, and working through complexity to deliver meaningful and sustainable business improvements.
Nice to have
- Experience implementing Lean Review, operational assessment, or modernization recommendations.
- Experience identifying and implementing automation opportunities, including AI-enabled productivity and automation tools.
- Experience developing performance measurement frameworks, operational dashboards, and management reporting tools.
- Knowledge of data governance, reporting practices, and data-informed decision making.
- A Lean, Six Sigma, Business Analysis, Change Management, or Continuous Improvement certification.
- Experience working in a regulatory, operational, financial services, or public-sector environment.
Your education and experience
This position requires a university degree in business administration, public administration, operations management, technology, or a related field and 6 years of relevant experience leading business improvement, modernization, process design, operational excellence, automation, stakeholder engagement, or implementation initiatives, or an equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional). If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.
What you need to know
- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Reliability Relocation assistance may be provided, if required Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.
Hybrid Work Model
The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.
What you can expect from us This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit A great deal to consider .
- Salaries are based on qualifications and experience and typically range from $111,051 to $130,649 (job grade 17) The Bank offers an incentive for successfully meeting expectations at 7 to 10% of your base salary. The Bank offers additional performance pay (5%) for those who exceed expectations. Exceptional performers who far exceed expectations may be eligible for higher performance pay. Flexible and comprehensive benefits so you can choose the level of health and dental coverage that meets your needs Extra vacation days (up to five each year) that you can purchase to add to your vacation entitlement Option to join the indexed, defined-benefit pension plan after 24 consecutive months of service
We wish to thank all applicants for their interest and effort in applying for this position. Only candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

2459696.text:
The Mint is hiring a Director, Enterprise Data & AI who can thrive in a dynamic and inclusive environment.
Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director, Enterprise Data & AI is responsible for the Royal Canadian Mint’s (Mint) enterprise-wide data, information, architecture, analytics, and artificial intelligence strategy, ensuring data is trusted, secure, and leveraged as a strategic asset and competitive differentiator. This position will play a critical role in business transformation, enabling digital, analytical, architecture, and AI-driven capabilities that support strategic decision-making, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance.
The Director acts as a strategic partner to executive leadership and business stakeholders, ensuring technology investments are aligned with business priorities, risk posture, and architectural standards to become an insight-driven organization.
Your Responsibilities:
- Define and execute the enterprise Data, Analytics, and AI strategy aligned with business priorities.
- Establish data as a trusted enterprise asset to enable analytics, automation, and AI.
- Lead the development of modern data, analytics, and AI/ML capabilities.
- Ensure responsible, secure, and compliant use of data and AI.
- Oversee delivery of data integration, business intelligence, and self-service analytics solutions.
- Provide enterprise architecture leadership, standards, and technology roadmaps.
- Lead technology governance, portfolio management, and investment prioritization.
- Implement effective intake, funding, and performance management processes.
- Drive agile delivery, DevSecOps and CI/CD best practices.
- Ensure consistent, high-quality execution balancing speed, security, and architectural integrity.
- Manage budgets, vendors, and strategic technology investments.
- Build and lead high-performing teams while fostering innovation, accountability, and continuous learning.
This position offers a hybrid work arrangement, requiring on-site presence at our Ottawa location three to five days per week, depending on meeting requirements and other activities.
This selection process may also qualify you for other positions with similar requirements and qualifications.
Qualifications:
Languages Requirements:
Proficiency in both official languages (English / French) is required at the time of hire. If no qualified candidate fully meets the required levels, other candidate language profiles may be considered in accordance with the Mint’s Staffing Policy. The linguistic profile for this position is:
Reading Comprehension : C Advanced
Written Expression : B Intermediate
Oral Proficiency : C Advanced
Education & Designation:
- University degree in related area
Experience:
- Minimum 10 years of experience in data analytics, data modeling, data management, and data architecture
- Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience delivering technology solutions that drive business outcomes.
- Proven experience with enterprise data platforms supporting reporting, analytics, and AI‑driven decision‑making.
- Experience leading the adoption and scaling of AI, including generative and agentic AI, with a focus on business value, governance, and operationalization.
- Experience leading enterprise architecture across data, application, security, AI, and technology domains, including standards and target‑state roadmaps.
- Experience leading cloud, data and AI platforms to ensure scalability, resilience, security, and cost efficiency.
- Experience establishing governance frameworks for data, information, architecture, and AI.
- Experience leading agile delivery and operating model, and DevSecOps best practices.
- Experience managing budgets, strategic investments, vendors and technology contracts.
- Demonstrate ability to build and lead high-performing teams while fostering innovation and continuous improvement.
Additional Qualifications:
- Extensive experience of multifaceted business areas and IT, excellent presentation, negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and communication skills;
- Proven ability to bridge business and technology by translating complex data, architecture, and AI concepts into strategic, actionable insights.
- Strong expertise in modern data and analytics platforms, including Microsoft Fabric, Azure Data Lake, Data Pipelines, Lakehouses, Data Warehouses, SQL Server, and Azure SQL.
- Experience in ERP, manufacturing, finance, supply chain and e-commerce is highly desirable
Why the Mint?
At the Mint, you will collaborate with a diverse group of people and be a part of an iconic Canadian organization. Your safety and wellbeing are our top priority. We offer outstanding pay and total rewards for you and your family and you will be supported to continuously learn throughout your career.
The Mint is committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We value diversity and aim to provide an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment, selection and onboarding process to ensure that each candidate is treated respectfully. In accordance with the Employment Equity Act, you are invited to voluntarily self-identify with one or more of the four employment equity groups (women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities and members of visible minorities) by sending your application to the confidential email, EE@mint.ca that is accessed only by the Human Resources section.
If you need accommodation at any point in the application or interview process, please let us know. We are committed to being an inclusive employer. For a confidential inquiry, simply email us directly at EE@mint.ca to make arrangements.
What to Expect:
In order to be considered for an interview, please clearly demonstrate on your application how you meet the language, education and experience qualifications. The additional qualifications may be assessed through interviews, exams, reference checks, etc.
Selected candidates will be required to complete a background check facilitated by the Mint in order to obtain a security clearance.
Ready to mint your career? Please forward your resume to careers@mint.ca by September 20, 2026. We look forward to receiving your application!

The Senate plays a unique role in shaping our country’s democracy. As members of the upper house of Parliament, senators examine legislation, study public policy, champion causes and conduct interparliamentary diplomacy.

About the Supervision Department The payments landscape in Canada and globally is evolving rapidly, driven by technological advancements that are introducing innovative ways for consumers and businesses to make payments. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), the Bank of Canada is responsible for registering retail payment service providers (PSPs) that perform retail payment activities, maintaining a public registry of PSPs, and supervising PSPs’ compliance with operational risk management, fund safeguarding and reporting requirements.
The Bank assesses whether PSPs are managing risks effectively, identifies areas for improvement, and promotes compliance through a range of supervisory, compliance and enforcement tools. These positions will support the ongoing implementation and continuous improvement of the Retail Payments Supervisory Framework.
What you will do As a Supervisor within Retail Payments Supervision, you will contribute to fulfilling the Bank’s regulatory mandate by supporting work across one or more areas of Registration, Risk Supervision and Enforcement. You will apply supervisory judgment, strong analysis and sound recommendations to help implement the Bank’s legislative and regulatory authorities under the RPAA.
Depending on the area of focus, you may assess registration applications and scope questions, evaluate PSPs’ operational risk and fund safeguarding practices, review PSP reporting and incidents, investigate potential non-compliance, or support the use of appropriate supervisory, compliance and enforcement tools. You will also contribute to policies, procedures, guidance, training materials and process improvements that strengthen the Bank’s approach to supervising PSPs.
- Apply technical expertise and knowledge of supervisory concepts, principles, practices and methodologies aligned to the Bank’s Supervisory Framework.

Did you know? In 2017, the Bank of Canada opened a new Bank of Canada Museum where visitors learn about the work that the Bank does to support the economic well-being of Canadians and explore Canada’s National Currency Collection. Our Museum is both a traditional museum and an interpretive centre. As a public outreach arm of the Bank’s Communications Department, the Museum’s mission is to clarify for Canadians the key functions of the Bank of Canada.
In addition, through the National Currency Collection the Museum interprets our monetary heritage, both Canadian and international. This position will support the Visitor Services team by delivering onsite and virtual programs as well as assisting with the development of educational programs and resources for schools which is a key initiative of the Museum.
Are you are interested in contributing to the Museum’s mission to help Canadians understand the economy, our economic heritage and the work of the Bank of Canada?
What you will do Under the supervision of the Manager, Visitor Services, you help plan, coordinate, implement and deliver front-line services and programs to visitors. In addition, you promote a better understanding of and appreciation for the Museum’s themes as well as the Bank of Canada’s mandate and functions.
More specifically, you will:
- offer high-quality service by delivering educational programs onsite and online, coordinating the daily operation of the Museum, answering questions about all aspects of the Museum and the functions of the Bank, etc.
- develop, deliver, and provide ongoing training for the VS Team; training focused on best practices for both in-person and virtual program delivery of Museum Educational programs
- interpret the history and themes set out for the Museum and communicate them to the public through a variety of activities (guided visits, school programs, exhibitions, workshops, interactive games, etc.)
- provide support to the Museum and the Bank’s social media teams by monitoring trends, scheduling posts, contributing to content creation and liaising with colleagues to identify links between museum initiatives and other public communication priorities of the Bank of Canada.
- contribute to the evaluation of visitors’ experience by gathering statistics and working on various short-term assignments, e.g., surveying visitors, evaluating Museum programs and services, and supporting Museum operations
- assign daily tasks to the Museum Guides, including scheduling, special projects, and ensuring high-quality service in all areas of the Museum
- provide input into the recruitment and performance evaluation of the Museum’s interpretive staff, as well as in the planning, preparation and implementation of training programs in support of the management of the Museum
What you need to succeed We are looking for an effective communicator, self-starter, and team player to join our Visitor Services team. You must be organized, and able to plan necessary resources to take steps to achieve objectives. Your problem-solving skills, adaptability and flexibility make you an ideal candidate for this role. We are also looking for someone with strong communication skills, presentation techniques and creativity when interpreting the work of the Bank of Canada to the public (virtually, through social media content and in person).
T his position requires availability on weekends and holidays and may be asked to work occasional evening shifts for special events.
Nice-to-have
- Knowledge of the Bank of Canada, economics, the retail sector, and museology
- Experience as a supervisor, including program delivery
- Knowledge of best practices for social media content creation
Your education and experience This position requires a post-secondary degree or diploma in a related field (e.g., education, public history, Museum education & interpretation studies, museum studies, communications, marketing) and a minimum of one year of work experience coordinating services to the public and a minimum of two years of relevant programming experience (in person and virtual) in a museum or public setting. Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. Did you know?
The Currency Department helps ensure that Canadians continue to have confidence in, and access to, bank notes. Within Currency Policy and Research (CPR), we conduct research and policy analysis on cash use, payment behaviour, payment and cash system developments, financial inclusion and other issues affecting the future role of cash in Canada.
Our work combines survey design, applied microeconomic analysis, policy development, stakeholder engagement and publishable research to provide evidence-based advice to Bank management and external partners. This work supports flagship initiatives including the Methods-of-Payment Survey (MOP), the Cost of Payments Study and broader research on cash usage and payment choice in Canada.
What you will do
Reporting to the Assistant Director, Currency Policy and Research, you will contribute to the Bank's research and policy work relating to cash, payments and consumer payment behaviour.
Specifically, you will:
- Lead and conduct empirical research on cash use, payment choice, consumer behaviour and payment-system developments in Canada.
- Own key research workstreams for the Bank’s Methods-of-Payment Survey program, including survey design, data strategy, analysis, estimation and dissemination of findings to support evidence-based advice on cash use and payment behaviour.
- Analyze household, survey and other microdata using advanced quantitative and econometric techniques.
- Support the Cost of Payments Study, including research design, data collection initiatives, analysis and estimation work.
- Produce high-quality reports, briefing notes, presentations and policy recommendations for senior management.
- Translate research findings into operational and policy advice related to currency, cash accessibility and payment-system developments.
- Prepare research papers and contribute to the publication and dissemination of Bank research.
- Present findings to internal and external audiences, including conferences, workshops and stakeholder forums.
- Collaborate with researchers, analysts, survey specialists, external research firms and academic partners.
- Provide guidance and mentorship to junior staff and research assistants.
- Respond to requests for analysis and advice from senior management and internal partners.
What you need to succeed
To succeed in this role, you will bring significant experience conducting applied economic research, including analyzing survey data or microdata and applying econometric and statistical methods to policy or research questions. You will be comfortable translating complex data and research findings into clear, high-quality analytical products for senior decision makers.
You will also have strong quantitative and econometric skills, along with proficiency using statistical software and data-analysis tools. Strong writing, presentation and communication skills will be important, as you will be expected to explain complex analytical findings clearly to a range of audiences.
The ideal candidate will demonstrate sound judgment, analytical thinking and initiative, while working collaboratively and building strong relationships across multidisciplinary teams. You will be results-oriented and able to influence through clear, evidence-based communication.
Nice-to-have
A combination of one or more of the following would be considered an asset:
- Research experience in payments, cash demand, consumer finance, financial inclusion or payment-system developments.
- Experience designing and managing surveys.
- Experience working with large-scale administrative, transactional or payments-related datasets.
- Experience using agentic AI to complete research projects.
- Publication record in peer-reviewed or practitioner-oriented journals.
- Experience working with external stakeholders, academics or market-research firms.
Your education and experience
The position requires a PhD in Economics, Econometrics, Finance, or a related quantitative discipline or a master’s degree with four years of relevant experience.

We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. Although the position language requirement is English or French essential, we do encourage everyone to improve their second language proficiency for future career growth and to contribute towards fostering a bilingual environment.

Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2025 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
Canada’s crop production is being increasingly challenged by climate change, more prevalent weather extremes, and emerging disease threats. Designing transformative computer vision and machine learning systems to boost efficiencies and design resilient crops is critical to our agriculture industry. Automated vision analysis of crop roots and the rhizosphere presents a unique opportunity to increase the genetic gains and adaptability of Canada’s field crops. At the NRC’s Aquatic and Crop Resource Development (ACRD) research centre, we are investing in technologies to image and analyze crop root and shoot systems, increasing the use of machine learning and generative AI solutions, and expanding our digital capabilities to develop innovative tools for crop improvement and agricultural productivity. We invite you to join our team to take crop phenomics to the next level and be an integral member contributing to making Canada’s crops more resilient. Interacting with colleagues across ACRD and collaborating nationally and internationally, the successful candidate would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
As a Computer Vision specialist on the Integrated Omics and Climate Resilience Team at ACRD, you will play a key role in helping position the NRC as leaders in digital research for Canada. Your responsibilities include the delivery of software support for the design, development, and implementation of computer code which enables automated analyses of crop images. This would include supporting ACRD efforts for implementing best practices and new tools for data management. The successful candidate is also expected to mentor and lead Computer Systems administrators, Technical Officers, and Research Officers colleagues and students for accomplishment of projects focused on Computer Vision and Machine Learning.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
M.Sc. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Candidates with a B.Sc. and at least 2 years of relevant experience in developing computer vision or machine learning algorithms will also be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Significant experience* in computer vision approaches with proven track-record of developing algorithms, documentation, and production-quality software code for image analysis. Experience*** with biological or agricultural images is an asset.
- Strong proficiency** in Python and experience*** with C++ for performance‑critical computer vision applications.
- Experience*** in computational geometry, 3D representations and related data structures.
- Experience*** developing and training deep learning models for computer vision, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), vision transformers, and foundation models.
- Experience*** mentoring junior developers, engineers, or students in machine learning or computer vision methods and software development best practices.
- Experience*** in parallel processing (e.g., across GPUs) and multi-threaded application design is preferred.
- Experience*** with transfer learning techniques to leverage pre-trained models, including large foundation models, will be considered an asset .
* Significant experience is defined as 3+ years of directly relevant experience, with demonstrated application across multiple projects. ** Strong proficiency is defined as 3+ years of experience, with demonstrated ability to independently develop, debug, and maintain code across multiple projects. *** Experience is defined as 2+ years of hands-on experience, with demonstrated application in one or more projects.

English

Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Knowledge of classical computer-vision methods including pre-processing, segmentation, object detection and classification including foundational theory and familiarity with OpenCV or similar frameworks.
- Knowledge of 3D reconstruction techniques and generation of 3D representations such as point clouds or meshes.
- Understanding of deep learning methods for computer vision and their application to image analysis.
- Proficiency in training dataset preparation, including preprocessing, augmentation, and annotation, and familiarity with self-supervised or representation learning approaches.
- Proficiency in modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
- Familiarity with model evaluation, validation, and performance metrics for computer vision tasks.
- Ability to use version control systems (e.g., Git) and workflow or pipeline tools to support reproducible machine learning experiments and data processing (e.g., Snakemake, MLflow, or similar).
- Practical knowledge of open-source frameworks for federated learning will be considered an asset .

2460886.text:
The Canadian Air Transport Security Authority (CATSA) has 1 (one) exciting fixed-term opportunity up to July 14, 2028 within the Technology branch at the CATSA HQ.
This position represents an opportunity for career-driven individuals seeking a position within an organization that inspires growth and promotes excellence to make a difference and contribute to CATSA’s unique culture as it strives to excel in air transport security.
Why is CATSA a great fit for you?
CATSA is a world leader in aviation security, mandated to protect the public by delivering security screening operations at 89 designated airports across Canada. As a Crown corporation, CATSA is accountable to Parliament through the Minister of Transport.
We champion innovation and creativity and offer a welcoming and inclusive workplace where employees can be their true selves and take pride in being part of a mission that matters.
If you are a motivated professional seeking a position within a multifunctional and collaborative environment and you are looking for the next great adventure, CATSA is the place for you!
Summary of responsibilities:
The Advisor, Logistics is responsible for providing logistical oversight in the development and maintenance of procurement plans and strategies for securing the delivery and relocation of screening equipment and associated equipment to airports across Canada. The incumbent is also responsible for performing contract management functions, including procurement, invoice validation and resolution, budget tracking and reporting. The Advisor, Logistics performs all other duties and responsibilities related to the position as required.
Key Tasks and Responsibilities:
- Leads, plans, and executes all aspects of the delivery and relocation of screening and associated equipment to airports, including negotiation, motivating, coordinating and liaising with project teams, suppliers, shippers, movers, and airport authorities.
- Prepares procurement requisitions and purchase orders (PO’s) for equipment and Logistics requirements; tracks and confirms receipt and completion of PO’s.
- Performs detailed reviews and audits of invoices to validate that goods and services were delivered as per the contract terms and resolves any invoice and payment disputes and queries.
What you need to succeed To qualify for the position, you must have:
- Graduation from a recognized college or university with a specialization in business, material/supply chain management or another speciality relevant to the duties of the position.
- A minimum of five years of experience in the areas of supply chain management, logistics, deployment, warehousing, and/or contract management.
- Experience managing concurrent equipment deliveries to multiple sites on an on-going basis.
- Experience overseeing and motivating Contractors and Airport stakeholders to insure timely support of project objectives.
- Experience providing input and analysis to support the budget forecasting process.
- Experience planning and delivering tasks and projects.
- Experience reconciling invoices for payment while ensuring accordance to contract terms and conditions.
- Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices related to general procurement and deployment planning and coordination.
This position is best suited to individuals with the following skills and abilities:
- Client service orientated with strong interpersonal skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a team environment to achieve corporate, departmental and branch goals.
- Highly organized with the ability to prioritize, set schedules, meet deadlines, handle multiple projects/activities and competing demands, and deliver results in a changing work environment.
- Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment.
- Ability to clearly articulate point of view to various audiences, both orally and in writing.
- Ability to liaise effectively, and coordinate efforts and interests with multiple internal and external stakeholders.
- Ability to negotiate, influence and engage with stakeholders in a tactful and cooperative manner.
- Ability to multi-task and set priorities with close attention to details, accuracy, quality and completeness.
- Ability to analyze situations and propose solutions in time-sensitive situations.
Valuable skills include:
- Knowledge of the aviation industry.
- Knowledge of CATSA's mandate and priorities, as well as an awareness of relevant legislation impacting CATSA.
- Experience working in a technology environment.
- Knowledge of transportation principles and methods for moving equipment or goods by air, rail, sea, or road, including the relative costs and benefits.
- Knowledge of project management tools and methodologies.
Specific work requirements:
- Ability to travel as required
- Language Profile: English Essential;
- Ability to obtain and maintain a Reliability security clearance;

If you feel you are the ideal candidate for this position, please click on the following link to submit your application before September 23, 2026 by 11:59pm EST.

Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
We are looking for Computer Support Specialists to support our Chief Information Officer Branch (CIOB). The Computer Support Specialist would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
As a Computer Support Specialist, you will work as a Field Support Team member within the NRC-Client Service Centre (NRC-CSC), providing clients with IT support services for distributed computers, mobile, and audio-visual equipment in Research Centres/Branches/IRAP of NRC. Some Research Centres may require support for servers and networking appliances. You will source, implement, and troubleshoot the hardware and software services provided to the clients.
In addition, you will assist IT team members in improving general operating efficiency; create, edit and maintain documentation; maintain software; provide IT support to computer, users; and utilizing desktop and management tools. There are skills that are more specific to research environments and others to corporate environments.

Education
College diploma in Computer Science or related field.
Bachelor degree in Computer Science from a recognized University considered an asset.

For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Experience providing desktop and technical support to users both locally and remotely (including problem analysis and resolution) in a Windows based environment including support of MS Office products, TCP/IP etc.
- Experience using a Service management application to manage events, incidents and service request, asset management and finally to document knowledge.
- Significant* experience in supporting Microsoft desktop operating systems in Windows 10 and 11, including imaging software.
- Significant* experience installing, configuring and maintaining the desktop hardware, software and peripherals.
- Experience installing and supporting Linux & Mac OS, would be an asset but not required.
- Experience supporting Servers/VM, would be an asset but not required.
- Experience supporting Networking equipment, would be an asset but not required

Reliability Status

Language requirements
Bilingual Imperative BBB/BBB
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests

Technical competencies

- Ability to use reasoning and problem-solving skills for troubleshooting of IT devices.

View all competency profiles

2460943.text:
Selection process number: 2090-CMN-26-OC-045
Your place at the Museum
We value diversity and believe we benefit from working in a place where everyone feels included and where the unique qualities and strengths inherent in a diverse workforce are combined. We welcome applications from persons who may identify as a member of one or more other equity seeking groups (for e.g. women, visible minorities, Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+, religious or cultural minority).
You have a place at the Museum!
About the position
As a growing public collection of over one million preserved specimens of plants, lichens and algae, the National Herbarium of Canada safeguards a significant part of the physical evidence through which our nation’s natural history and future are understood. Within this incredible “botanical library”, the Botany Specimen Technician works closely with the Botany Curator, Assistant Collection Manager, and Indigenous Technician, and a vibrant community of research staff and associates, visitors, volunteers, and interns. Together, the team builds, preserves, and shares the collection as productively as possible.
Focusing specifically on specimen processing and digitization, the Botany Specimen Technician contributes to a wide array of projects related to vascular plants, bryophytes, lichens, and algae. They prepare new specimens for the collection, make meticulous repairs to fragile objects, and receive / prepare / document specimen shipments. To advance collection digitization, they also capture and manage large volumes of specimen images and data. The Botany Specimen Technician communicates widely in the Botany and broader Research and Collections teams at the CMN, working effectively both independently and in a variety of teams.
Working at the museum means:
- Contributing to an engaging mission as well as exciting projects and challenges
- An inclusive, friendly and safe work environment
- A competitive salary established by collective agreements
- Access to federal public service group insurance and pension plans
Eligibility criteria
This position is open to all employees of the Canadian Museum of Nature and any members of the public who meet the qualifications below. Candidates must be legally entitled to work in Canada.
Education and training
Completion of a post-secondary degree or diploma in Biological Sciences, Museum Studies, or a related field.
Language requirements
English or French is essential
Experience
- Minimum one year experience in activities related to Botany (plants, lichens and/or algae) collection development, care and/or management
- Experience working with specialized database software to enter, upgrade and manipulate a high volume of natural history collection data and images
- Experience with capturing digital specimen images for database records.
- Experience in secure handling of fragile, valuable objects, and dangerous goods
- Experience in providing high-quality service to both external and internal clients
- Experience in mentoring and working with junior team members (like students).
Interested? APPLY!
The Canadian Museum of Nature is committed to inclusive and barrier-free selection processes and work environments. If you are invited to participate in the selection process, we encourage you to advise us of any accommodation you may require. This information will be treated as confidential.
The Statement of Qualifications, providing greater detail about the skills, knowledge and aptitudes needed for this role, can be obtained by contacting the Museum at competition@nature.ca.
All candidates must submit a cover letter and curriculum vitae outlining how their experience and training meet the requirements listed above.
Send your application by filling in the application form page where you can upload your cover letter, curriculum vitae and any other required documents.
CLOSING DATE : September 24th, 2026

The role
Help bring research to life and drive your career forward with the National Research Council of Canada (NRC), Canada's largest research and technology organization.
We are looking for a Research Associate (RA), to join our Thermometry and Radiometry Team within the Metrology Research Centre. The Metrology Research Centre is committed to fostering innovation through high-precision measurement science and advancements in metrology. The RA would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The RA will join a team of experts performing original research and development, advancing the field of metrology in quantum network metrology and quantum sensing.
Using your understanding of physical principles and your hands-on skills, you will work with our team to develop, research and establish capabilities in quantum sensing and metrology. You will contribute to one or more of the following projects: sensing with atomic and molecular optical systems; precision timimg and synchronization of quantum network nodes; ultra-low temperature thermometry
Working with other members of the team, The RA will:
- Design, participate in, and execute experiments in quantum optics, quantum networks, and atomic and molecular optical physics;
- Work in metrology labs with other research and technical team members to support research activities;
- Acquire and analyze data;
- Report and disseminate results.

Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
A doctoral degree in electrical engineering, optics, physics, engineering physics or a closely related field.
A Master’s degree in engineering physics, engineering (electrical, mechanical, other), or in physics, along with relevant experience may also be considered.
As part of the RA Program you must have received your PhD or Masters within the last five years or you expect to receive the degree within the next six months.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Hands-on experience in a scientific lab setting and using a variety of laboratory test equipment;
- Experience working with quantum optics and/or atomic and molecular physics;
- Experience working with optical components and systems;
- Experience working with vacuum systems;
- Experience in general programming and computer interfacing and control of instruments by computer;
- Experience collecting and analysing data; and dissemination of results.
Experience in the following are assets:
- Python;
- Metrology;
- Laser cooling and atom trapping
- Atomic clocks
- Operating and performing experiments with dilution refrigerators
Condition of employment
Reliability Status
For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Solid knowledge of laboratory measurement devices;
- Extensive knowledge of physical principles;
- Advanced knowledge of quantum optics and/or atomic and molecular physics;
- Solid experience with laboratory vacuum systems;
- Solid knowledge of programming languages for computer control of experimental apparatus and data acquisition;
- Solid knowledge of programming languages and techniques for data analysis;
- Excellent written and oral communication skills;
- Demonstrated ability to conduct experimental research in relevant areas; and
- Ability to write high quality research articles, technical reports, and to communicate research findings to partners and clients.
Behavioural competencies
- Research - Creative thinking (Level 3)
- Research - Results orientation (Level 2)

Working closely with counterparts across the federal research funding agencies and Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, you will build partnerships, foster collaboration and advance a coordinated approach to promoting Canadian research excellence and supporting government priorities.
As a member of the leadership team, you will help shape the future direction of communications and engagement at NSERC, leading change, inspiring innovation and creating meaningful connections between science, research and Canadians.

Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), the Bank of Canada is responsible for registering retail payment service providers (PSPs) that perform retail payment activities, maintaining a public registry of PSPs, and ensuring PSPs’ compliance with operational risk management, fund safeguarding and reporting requirements.
The Bank assesses whether PSPs are managing risks effectively, identifies areas for improvement, and promotes compliance through a range of supervisory, compliance and enforcement tools. These positions will support the ongoing implementation and continuous improvement of the Retail Payments Supervisory Framework.
What you will do As an Analyst within Retail Payments Supervision, you will contribute to fulfilling the Bank’s regulatory mandate by supporting work across one or more areas of Registration, Risk Supervision and Enforcement. You will conduct analysis and support the development of sound recommendations to help fulfil the Bank’s legislative and regulatory authorities under the RPAA.
Depending on the area of focus, you may assess registration applications and scope questions, support the evaluation of PSPs’ operational risk management and fund safeguarding practices, review PSP reporting and incidents, investigate potential non-compliance, or support the use of appropriate supervisory and enforcement tools. As an analyst, you will:
- Analyze issues relating to the Bank’s supervision of PSPs
- Contribute to business documentation, operational policies, procedures, guidance, training materials, and continuous improvement initiatives
- Collaborate with colleagues and internal or external partners to support registration, supervision, compliance and enforcement activities
- Contribute to the development of recommendations to support decision making

You will join a collaborative, forward-looking team modernizing the Bank's enterprise database services. You will also have access to the Bank's learning and development resources, including relevant certifications, labs and career development opportunities.
About the position
This role is intended for senior database professionals who combine strong enterprise Oracle and SQL Server administration expertise with demonstrated cloud platform and migration experience. You will support critical production database environments while helping lead the Bank's continued modernization toward Azure-based database services.
This is not an entry point into cloud technologies. You must have practical experience implementing, administering or migrating production database workloads in the cloud and be prepared to apply that experience immediately. You will help guide migration activities, technical decisions and the evolution of the Bank's Database-as-a-Service (DBaaS) platform.
This is a hybrid database administration and cloud modernization role. It combines the administration and operational support of enterprise Oracle and SQL Server environments with cloud migration, automation and platform development responsibilities. You will work across on-premises and Azure-based database services as the Bank transitions toward a standardized DBaaS model.
The platform portfolio includes:
- Azure SQL Managed Instance, the primary migration platform Azure Database for PostgreSQL, a strategic growth platform Oracle Database@Azure, used for targeted exception scenarios
What you will do
In this role, you will administer and support critical enterprise databases while helping deliver the Bank's cloud migration and DBaaS objectives. More specifically, you will:
Database Administration and Production Operations
- Administer and support enterprise Oracle and SQL Server database environments, including availability, performance, capacity, backup, recovery, patching and security. Diagnose and resolve complex database performance, reliability and availability issues. Support SQL Server Always On Availability Groups and Oracle technologies such as RAC and Data Guard. Participate in incident response, problem management, root-cause analysis and the on-call rotation.
Cloud Migration and Hybrid Operations
- Assess, plan and execute migrations from on-premises SQL Server and Oracle environments to Azure database platforms. Develop migration, testing, cutover, validation, rollback and post-migration support approaches. Work with platform and application teams to address dependencies, compatibility, performance and operational readiness across hybrid architectures. Help guide technical decisions and drive adoption of standardized database services for new and existing applications.
Cloud Platform Development and Automation
- Help design, implement and evolve Azure-based database services, including Azure SQL Managed Instance, Azure Database for PostgreSQL and Oracle Database@Azure. Provision, scale, patch and decommission databases using automation, infrastructure as code, scripts, pipelines or templated deployments. Develop and maintain automation for provisioning, monitoring, backup and recovery workflows. Define and apply platform standards, guardrails and onboarding patterns for application teams.
Security, Resilience and Governance
- Implement high availability and disaster recovery patterns aligned with enterprise requirements. Apply requirements for identity and access management, encryption, auditing, data protection, backup and recovery. Implement monitoring, alerting and performance baselines to maintain reliability. Contribute to architecture deliverables, governance processes and continuous service improvement.
What you need to succeed
You bring deep enterprise database administration expertise and demonstrated experience working with production cloud database platforms and migrations. You can operate critical Oracle and SQL Server environments, lead or significantly contribute to complex cloud migrations, and help develop secure, reliable and scalable database services. You are a self-starter and strong collaborator who can work independently and influence decisions across technical teams.
In addition, you have:
- Significant hands-on experience administering enterprise Oracle and SQL Server databases in production environments. Demonstrated hands-on experience implementing, administering or migrating production workloads on cloud database platforms such as Azure SQL Managed Instance and/or Oracle Database@Azure. Proven experience executing or leading production database migrations from on-premises environments to cloud platforms, including assessment, planning, testing, cutover, rollback and post-migration support. Experience designing and operating high availability and disaster recovery solutions, including SQL Server Always On Availability Groups and Oracle RAC and/or Data Guard. Experience developing or maintaining database automation using scripts, infrastructure as code, pipelines or templated deployments. Strong knowledge of performance tuning, monitoring, backup, recovery, security, data protection and production incident resolution. Experience improving operational efficiency through automation, standardization and reusable service patterns. The ability to guide technical decisions, collaborate across infrastructure, cloud, security and application teams, and support application onboarding to shared database services.
Nice to have
- Experience with Oracle Exadata or particularly complex enterprise SQL Server deployments. Familiarity with enterprise governance, security and compliance frameworks. Knowledge of monitoring, logging and observability tools for cloud platforms. Relevant certifications, such as Azure and/or Oracle data, database or architecture certifications.
Your education and experience
Your combined education and work experience demonstrate that you have the competencies and skills for the position. We are ideally seeking candidates with relevant education in computer science or a related field and five or more years of relevant experience in database technologies and cloud platforms.

Job Description
Reporting to the Director General, Library and Research Services, the Senior Director, Branches and Parliamentary Outreach, provides strategic leadership for a diverse portfolio of services that are essential to the Library of Parliament’s mandate. This includes library branch services, reference and intake services, news and current awareness products, parliamentary learning and outreach initiatives, and the Parliament of Canada Information Service.
As a member of the senior leadership team, you will shape the future of service delivery by driving modernization, fostering innovation and ensuring that the Library continues to provide timely, trusted and client-focused services. You will lead a team of managers, librarians and specialized professionals, championing a culture of excellence, collaboration, inclusion and continuous improvement.
The incumbent performs the following duties:
Strategic Leadership
- Develop and implement strategies that advance the Library’s mandate and priorities.
- Provide direction for the delivery of high-quality services and programs.
- Promote excellence and results across a broad portfolio.
Innovation and Modernization
- Lead transformational initiatives that modernize services, processes and technologies.
- Enhance accessibility and the client experience.
- Foster innovation and continuous improvement.
Build Strategic Partnerships
- Cultivate strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
- Represent the division and the Library on committees, working groups and collaborative initiatives.
- Advance organizational goals through effective consultation and partnership.
Please consult the executive brief for more information on the role of Senior Director, Branches and Parliamentary Outreach, at the Library of Parliament.

Education :

Experience :
- Significant experience leading multidisciplinary teams delivering a library function, including responsibility for operational planning, workforce management and performance management.
- Experience providing strategic advice and recommendations to senior executives.
- Experience building and maintaining relationships with senior stakeholders and partners.
- Experience developing and implementing strategic and operational plans.
- Experience leading organizational change, transformation or modernization initiatives.
- Significant experience leading client-focused programs, services or operations.
* Significant experience is defined as the depth and breadth of experience normally associated with having performed a broad range of various complex related activities.

- Knowledge of Canada’s parliamentary system and parliamentary institutions.
- Knowledge of strategic and operational planning, governance, performance measurement and risk management.
- Knowledge of leadership and people management practices.
- Knowledge of trends, challenges, best practices and emerging technologies related to library, information and client service delivery.
- Knowledge of change management and organizational transformation principles.

- Adaptability
- Client Focus
- Embracing Diversity
- Exemplifying Integrity
- Thinking Strategically
- Inspiring Others
- Decision Making
- Partnering
- Planning and Organizing
- Visioning and Alignment
- Leading Change
Asset Criteria :
- Experience leading library branch operations or reference services.
- Experience overseeing client-facing information or outreach programs.

Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2025 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
This position supports applied research in structural full-scale testing, component testing, and material testing related to air vehicle development, certification, and life extension. Testing is conducted on a wide range of articles, from simple coupons and components to rotorcraft and full-scale aircraft.
As an Aircraft Structural Technician in the SMPL Structural Integrity Test Facility, you will play a hands-on role in all practical phases of physical testing, from test setup through to teardown. Working independently and as part of a team, you will support the installation and assembly of test articles and rigs, setup and calibration of control and data acquisition systems, test operations, inspections, and data collection.
Following required training and competency verification, you will be responsible for confirming and certifying that test articles, aircraft components, and test setups are correctly configured, assembled, and functioning as required at key stages of testing, including test start, inspection pauses, restarts, and test completion. You will work from engineering orders, drawings, procedures, and specifications, and contribute to the preparation of technical instructions, parts breakdowns, and illustration packages that support safe, high-quality testing.
NRC Aerospace provides technical and research services, as well as access to state-of-the-art facilities, to help Canadian businesses grow and to support other government departments in priority areas such as Royal Canadian Air Force fleet airworthiness and research and technology development.
This position will support applied research in the areas of structural full-scale testing, component testing and material testing as it applies to air vehicle development, certification and life extension. Tests are carried out on a wide range of test articles ranging from simple coupons to rotorcraft to multimillion dollar aircraft.
In this role, you be participating in all practical phases of structural and other physical testing, from test set up to test dear-down in the SMPL Structural Integrity Test Facility. After verifications of competency and relevant training, you will work independently and in teams on assigned testing tasks such as installation, assembly, control and data acquisition system calibration and setup, test operations and data collection. Part of your responsibilities is to certify to the Project Manager through signature that test rig and article assembly have been performed properly and that functionality has been confirmed at test start, inspection pauses and test completion.
We are looking for an Aircraft Structural Technician to to support our NRC Aerospace Structures, Materials and Performance Labortoary (SMPL) Structural Integrity Team.
This position will support applied research in the areas of structural full scale testing, component testing and material testing as it applies to air vehicle development, certification and life extension. Tests are carried out on a wide range of test articles ranging from simple coupons to rotorcraft to multimillion dollar aircraft.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Certification and extensive experience (7+ years) as an Aircraft Maintenance Engineer (AME) or Canadian Forces Aviation Systems Technician with expertise in aircraft metallic and composite structures, control surface removal and installation and metal working.
AME-M or AME-S licenses would be considered an asset.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Extensive* experience working on airframe structures, aircraft flight control surface removal, installation and rigging. Preference will be given to those with Royal Canadian Air Force experience;
- Extensive experience working with pertinent specifications, civilian technical maintenance manuals and / or Canadian Forces Technical Orders;
- Experience with machine shop equipment, practices and quality control techniques;
- Significant experience of visual, close visual and borescope inspections;
- Significant experience in calibration techniques;
- Experience working accurately from mechanical drawings, with an understanding of precision alignment and fitting of components; and
- Experience operating overhead cranes, safe hoisting and materiel movement and aircraft maintenance stands.
The following may be considered as an asset:
- Experience working with composites;
- Demonstrated experience of the operation and calibration of MTS servo hydraulic load frames;
- Hands on experience in test control principles, full-scale structural test techniques and in the operation of a direct digital full-scale control and data acquisition systems including the maintenance of mechanical and servo hydraulic sub-systems.
*Extensive refers to a minimum of 7 years of relevant work experience.
Condition of employment
Secret clearance
A thorough security clearance process will be applied.
For a Secret Clearance, verification of background information over a period of 10 years is required. Individuals must have lived in Canada for a sufficient period of time to enable the security screening process.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Knowledge of mechanical testing and test data collection for both static and fatigue testing;
- Knowledge of hydraulic systems including actuators, servo valves, and pumps;
- Ability to work with machine shop equipment and other fabrication equipment used in fabrication and assembly processes;
- Knowledge of technical orders, service manuals and pertinent specifications;
- Knowledge of NDT techniques including eddy current and Ultrasonic inspection specific to aero applications; and
- Advanced knowledge of aircraft fasteners, their applications and installation requirements.
Assets:
- Knowledge of the operation and calibration of MTS servo hydraulic load frames;
- Knowledge of test control principles, full-scale structural test techniques and in the operation of a direct digital full-scale control and data acquisition systems including the maintenance of mechanical and servo hydraulic sub-systems;
- Knowledge of structural repair, hole cold working techniques used in aero applications;
- AME-M or AME-S license ratings.
Behavioural competencies
- Research Technician/Technologist - Communication (Level 2)
- Research Technician/Technologist - Creative thinking (Level 2)
- Research Technician/Technologist - Initiative (Level 2)
- Research Technician/Technologist - Results orientation (Level 2)
- Research Technician/Technologist - Teamwork (Level 2)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile: Research Technician/Technologist
View all competency profiles
Compensation
From $83,435 to $107,838 per annum.
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
Notes
- In 2025, the NRC was chosen as one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, a National Capital Region Top Employer and Forbes Canada’s Best Employer.
- Relocation assistance will be determined in accordance with the NRC's directives.
- A pre-qualified list may be established for similar positions for a one-year period.
- Ability to work at heights is a requirement.
- Occasional national and international travel may be required.
- Occasional overtime may be required.
- Ability to work in conditions found in an ordinary laboratory environment with some (minimal) exposure to hazardous materials or chemicals such as adhesives and cleaning agents. Independently work in such environments in a safe manner, with a working-level tolerance to a typical test environment with enhanced noise levels, heat and reduced air quality.
- Preference will be given to Canadian Citizens and Permanent Residents of Canada. Please include citizenship information in your application.
- The incumbent must adhere to safe workplace practices at all times.
- We thank all those who apply, however only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.
