About the role
Join the Enterprise Architecture and Artificial Intelligence team, in the Advisor, Solutions Architect position.
We are seeking a highly skilled Advisor in Solution Architecture, experienced with Microsoft Dynamics 365 (D365), who thrives in complex enterprise environments and enjoys solving challenging business and technical problems. This role requires an individual who can seamlessly transition between strategic architecture, technical leadership, and hands-on troubleshooting.
Our D365 ecosystem supports multiple business-critical processes and integrates with numerous enterprise applications, cloud services, and external platforms. The ideal candidate will possess deep D365 expertise, strong integration knowledge, and the ability to diagnose and resolve issues across the entire technology stack.
This is not a pure architect role. We are looking for someone who is equally comfortable designing solutions, reviewing architecture, configuring D365, analyzing logs, troubleshooting integrations, and working directly with development and operations teams to resolve production issues.
What you'll do:
- Act as a primary Microsoft Dynamics 365 (D365) technical expert, providing architectural leadership and direction for initiatives and platform enhancements.
- Lead solution design decisions, ensuring alignment with business requirements while balancing scalability, security, maintainability, and governance.
- Enforce D365 best practices, governance standards, and Microsoft-recommended architectures and patterns.
- Design, support, monitor, and continuously improve integrations between D365 and enterprise systems to maximize reliability and performance.
- Troubleshoot and resolve complex integration issues involving APIs, middleware, ETL processes, messaging platforms, cloud services, and data synchronization through root cause analysis.
- Collaborate with infrastructure, application, security, business, and vendor teams to address cross-platform challenges and deliver scalable technical solutions.
- Provide hands-on technical delivery, including D365 configuration, workflow optimization, system design, implementation, testing, deployments, production support, and incident resolution.
- Review code and technical solutions, maintain architecture and operational documentation, mentor technical teams, and communicate complex concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
What you should have:
- At least 7+ years of hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 and 10+ years delivering enterprise applications and integration solutions.
- A deep expertise in one or more D365 platforms, including Customer Engagement (Sales, Customer Service, Marketing), Finance & Operations, and Customer Insights.
- A strong knowledge of the Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power Automate, and Dataverse.
- A proven experience designing and implementing enterprise integration architectures and patterns.
- A strong proficiency with REST and SOAP APIs and enterprise integration technologies.
- An experience with Azure Integration Services, Azure Logic Apps, Service Bus, and event-driven architectures.
- An expertise in data integration, synchronization, and troubleshooting distributed systems and complex production environments.
- A solid understanding of security, authentication, authorization, enterprise architecture principles, and experience working in Agile and DevOps environments.
It would be great if you also had:
- Microsoft Dynamics 365 certifications.
- Azure Architect or Azure Integration certifications.
- Experience with enterprise middleware platforms.
- Experience supporting highly integrated and mission-critical business platforms.
- Knowledge of data architecture, analytics, and reporting solutions.

About the position
Stream 1: Refugee Protection Division (RPD)
The RPD is the largest of four divisions within the IRB, Canada's largest independent administrative tribunal. The RPD is a fast-paced, innovative, and engaging work environment, where Members are expected to deliver a high number of decisions pertaining to refugee claimants.
RPD Members determine whether refugee protection claims made in Canada are well-founded or not, delivering their decisions orally and in writing, with claimants or other parties present. Other duties include vacating or ceasing refugee status, for example, in cases where misrepresentations or changes in circumstances are later discovered.
Important note
RPD Members are exposed to difficult written narratives and oral testimony, including narratives of violence, trauma, sexual assault, crime, genocide, torture, and political persecution. RPD Members must be able to maintain composure and navigate these areas to obtain the necessary evidence on which they must base their decisions in a high-volume environment.
Lead refugee determination hearings
RPD Members prepare for and preside over refugee claim hearings, then issue decisions respecting refugee claims. Most RPD hearings are held on a virtual platform, though some occur in person at IRB premises.
RPD Members conduct hearings with claimants present. Legal counsel, witnesses, and other parties or observers are often also present. RPD proceedings and decisions are recorded. RPD Members’ decisions are subject to higher reviewing bodies, including the Federal Court. Consequently, RPD Members must maintain a very high standard of oral and written communication, which must be concise, focused and legally-sound and can be easily understood.
RPD Members work independently, composing and revising their decisions with limited administrative support.
RPD Members use effective questioning techniques to obtain important information in the refugee claims before them. The depth, breadth, and focus of questions will vary from case to case. RPD Members must be active listeners and must be able to spontaneously adjust lines of questioning as hearings progress. Often, this involves making complex and difficult credibility assessments as evidence unfolds. RPD Members are expected to remain calm and to manage the hearing so that it is meaningful, effective, procedurally-fair and completed on time.
RPD Members must promote procedural fairness and natural justice principles, which includes remaining neutral and open-minded in hearings and decision-making.
Analyze evidence and write decisions
RPD Members must deliver clear, concise, and cogent decisions that clearly explain to claimants the reasons for the results of their claims, whether positive or negative. Decisions will almost invariably include an analysis of complex events, including the RPD Member’s findings respecting a claim’s general credibility, and the application of relevant legislation, case law and policy guidelines to the facts of each case. Some decisions are simple and short while others can be very legally-complex.
To be successful, RPD Members must not only have a thorough understanding of refugee case law, administrative law principles, relevant legislation, policy instruments, and the rules of natural justice, they must also be able to swiftly apply their understanding during the hearings (often in situations where there is incomplete information), and in rendering decisions.
RPD Members are expected to uphold the highest standards of ethics as their comportment and decisions influence the public’s confidence and trust in the IRB and in the integrity of Canada’s refugee and immigration system. RPD Members must adhere to the Code of Conduct for Members of the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada.
RPD Members are also expected to complete cases in a timely manner and to be flexible with unpredictable scheduling, caseload, and case types.
Please note that for bilingual positions, RPD Members must be able to work effectively in English AND in French, including rendering oral decisions in both official languages.
Stream 2: Immigration Division (ID)
The ID is one of four divisions of the IRB. ID Members conduct detention reviews and admissibility hearings. Unlike the IRB’s other three divisions, ID Members’s workload is composed entirely of cases referred to it by the Canada Border Services Agency.
ID members require similar competencies to those expected of members in other divisions, yet the nature of ID Members’ work can be especially challenging.
Notably, expectations include but are not limited to:
Rendering well-reasoned decisions orally at the conclusion of each hearing, with very limited scope – given the statutory time limits and high-volume caseload – to reserve and render decisions in writing later.
Conducting hearings in a high security or correctional environment with significant background noise and rudimentary facilities or by videoconference or teleconference with hearing participants in multiple locations, or in person.
Managing voluminous files and exhibits, primarily in the form of a digital file.
Dealing professionally and compassionately with individuals who are suffering from mental illness or addictions, and who may not understand the nature of the proceedings.
Presiding at hearings with significant media interest.
Presiding over cases involving individuals who may have engaged in serious criminality, crimes against humanity, or acts of terrorism.
The ID is a high-volume tribunal and ID Members are expected to keep pace with their workload, meet tight deadlines, and render a high number of quality decisions.
ID detention reviews are considered an essential service with statutory time-limits that must be met. This requires ID Members to be flexible and, in some cases, work outside regular business hours.
Please note that for bilingual positions, ID Members must be able to work effectively in English AND in French, including rendering oral decisions in both official languages.
Work environment
At the IRB, inclusion is part of how we work every day. We aim to build a workplace where people feel respected, supported, and able to succeed. The work we do has a lasting impact on people and communities across Canada. To do it well, we rely on diverse perspectives and experiences that reflect the country we serve today and in the future. We are committed to creating an environment where employees can grow, contribute, and make a difference. If you’re looking for meaningful work in an inclusive organization, we encourage you to apply.

The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) is an independent agency of the Government of Canada, dedicated to fostering public trust and confidence in Canada's financial system by rigorously regulating and supervising over 400 federally regulated financial institutions (FRFIs) and 1200 federally regulated pension plans (FRPPs). OSFI has offices located in 4 major cities across Canada: Ottawa, Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver. Safeguarding Canada’s Financial Future: Through diligent regulation and supervision of FRFIs and FRPPs, we ensure that these entities operate soundly and securely. Our proactive approach to risk management and early intervention safeguards the interests of depositors, policyholders, pension plan members, and beneficiaries. We remain committed to fostering public confidence and supporting the competitive and resilient nature of Canada's financial landscape. Our Mandate: Our mandate is to ensure the stability and integrity of Canada's financial system. We achieve this by: Maintaining Financial Soundness: Ensuring that FRFIs and FRPPs remain in sound financial condition. Safeguarding Against Threats: Ensuring that FRFIs protect themselves against threats to their integrity and security, including foreign interference. Proactive Intervention: Acting swiftly when issues arise, requiring FRFIs and FRPPs to implement necessary corrective measures without delay. Risk Management: Continuously monitoring and evaluating risks, promoting sound risk management practices among FRFIs and FRPPs. Our Approach: In fulfilling our mandate, we adopt a balanced approach: For FRFIs: We protect the rights and interests of depositors, policyholders, and financial institution creditors. At the same time, we recognize the need for FRFIs to compete effectively and take reasonable risks. For FRPPs: We safeguard the rights and interests of pension plan members, former members, and entitled beneficiaries. Join Us: Be part of a system that ensures financial stability and security for all Canadians. Learn more about our work and how you can contribute to a stronger Canadian financial future. Who we are
This position falls within a directorate that provides common services to two funding agencies: the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC) and the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC).
At the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC), we bring together the research community, as well as the public, private and not-for-profit sectors, in contributing knowledge, talent and expertise to build a better future for Canada and the world. SSHRC is seeking talented professionals passionate about Canadian research and the value it brings to society.
The Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) is Canada’s largest funder of science and engineering. A career at NSERC means supporting the visionaries, explorers and innovators who are searching for the scientific and technical breakthroughs that will advance knowledge, improve the lives of Canadians and transform the world for the better.
Visit our career page at SSHRC or NSERC to learn more about why you should join our agency.

Leadership and direction in the delivery of performance measurement, evaluation and review services including the provision of strategic and authoritative advice to senior management of the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC)‘s, Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC)’s and Inter-Agency programs and other external stakeholders to optimize the effective and sound evaluation, assessment, and analysis of the performance of NSERC’s, SSHRC’s and Inter-Agency programs and associated policies.

- Foreign Credential Validation against Canadian Standards

- Experience supervising or managing human resources.
- Extensive 1 experience analyzing data, synthesizing evaluation findings and presenting results to senior management.
- Experience evaluating research or research related activities, and/or grants and contribution programs would be an asset .
1 Extensive is equivalent to five (5) or more years of experience.
Knowledge
- Knowledge of program evaluation theory and practices, including federal government performance measurement and evaluation policies/standards.
- Knowledge of evaluation methods and approaches, including qualitative and quantitative analysis techniques.
- Knowledge of project management principles.
- Knowledge of the post-secondary research funding environment, the research process and the transfer of research results to the user sector would be an asset .
Competencies
- Client service and delivery oriented.
- Analytical thinking (analysis and problem-solving).

The role
We are looking for an early-to-mid-career Technical and Policy Advisor on Construction Codes to support our Construction Research Centre. The Technical and Policy Advisor on Construction Codes would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
Successful candidates will work in the directorate for Codes Canada, a group that is responsible for supporting Canada’s Construction Code Development system. The development system is governed by an intergovernmental federal-provincial-territorial partnership. The team manages relationships with other federal departments, provincial and territorial governments and industry, standards, and other organizations within the construction sector.
Technical and Policy Advisors on Construction Codes support the deputy-minister-level Canadian Table for Harmonized Construction Codes Policy, the Canadian Board for Harmonized Construction Codes and the Advisory Council for Harmonized Construction Codes. Technical and Policy Advisors will support these groups in the development of policy considerations and advice on topics related to building design, construction and operation through regulation.
Codes Canada is in need of advisors with technical and policy backgrounds who are strong consensus-builders and who can:
- support executive-level code system committees with high quality advice
- develop high quality executive-level briefing materials
- work directly and liaise with technical content experts
- develop and present strategic and regulatory policy options
- work collaboratively with federal, provincial and territorial colleagues
- maintain strong relationships with industry organizations, and
- contribute to multi-jurisdictional, multi-stakeholder, and multidisciplinary initiatives in support of the development of model codes including initiatives involving NRC research.
Construction Codes are the interface between policy, regulation, and research. Successful candidates will develop and maintain an understanding of building construction, regulation, and economics involved in the application of technology to design and construction

The role
We are looking for a Research Officer, Building Acoustics to support our Construction Research Centre. The Research Officer, Building Acoustics would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The primary responsibility of the Research Officer (RO) is to support the goals of NRC and the Research Centre through research of and the development and application of advanced technologies. The RO works in a team environment with researchers and technical experts in world-class facilities. Activities include designing and making measurements for research projects, project management, and providing service to NRC clients. The RO provides input into the overall direction and research priorities for the program area within the context of the Research Centre business plan.
As part of a multidisciplinary team developing and deploying technical solutions for construction sector clients, the incumbent will support and conduct research activities dealing with the control of sound transmission in multi-unit buildings. Research activities focus on characterizing the acoustic performance of multi-unit construction, relating this performance to key construction details, modifying the design details to achieve enhanced performance for airborne and impact sound insulation.
Transferring research findings to industry and stakeholders is also an important responsibility of this position
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
PhD in a relevant field of Engineering such as Acoustic, Architectural, Civil, Mechanical or Electrical.
A Master’s degree in a relevant field of Engineering combined with relevant experience may be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Experience in designing and conducting research activities dealing with the evaluation and control of sound transmission in buildings.
- Experience in experimental design and analysis including data collection and analysis, overseeing data production, and ensuring data quality.
- Experience using measurement systems and analysis techniques to characterize sound fields and sound transmission.
- Experience in identification of research requirements, proposal writing, project management, and reporting through written documentation, presentations and publishing.
- Experience working with standards, specifications, or building codes dealing with acoustical performance of buildings would be an asset.

English

- Knowledge of measurement instrumentation and methods to characterize direct and flanking transmission in buildings for airborne and impact sound. For example:
- Measurement of STC rating Measurement of IIC rating
- Solid knowledge of acoustical signal analysis.
- Ability to design and use electro-acoustic instrumentation systems to measure, control, and characterize sound fields in buildings.

The role
We are looking for a Construction Project Coordinator to support our Real Property Planning and Management Branch. The incumbent would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity. The successful candidate will be exposed to a wide variety of buildings, including offices, laboratories and special use facilities (such as cleanrooms and wind tunnels) that offer an interesting work experience. As a Construction Project Coordinator, you will represent the NRC, the building owner on the construction site and will be expected to be the eyes and ears and spokesperson for the Construction Project Manager who holds overall responsibility for the project. The Construction Project Coordinator is expected to coordinate multiple projects and contracts simultaneously while ensuring that work is completed according to the tender documents and that industry best practices and all safety and building codes are respected. Due to the fast-paced working environment, the Construction Project Coordinator will need to have strong communication skills and must have experience working with contractors, consultants, clients. The projects range from renovations, restorations and alterations of NRC buildings and facilities to new construction and involve all construction trades and disciplines including civil, structural, architectural, mechanical and electrical. The project values can range from tens of thousands of dollars to millions of dollars depending on the complexity and size of the project being completed.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
College diploma in Architectural, Civil, Electrical, Mechanical Engineering or Structural Engineering Technology. A relevant trade license would also be considered. An equivalent combination of education and experience may also be considered. A certificate in construction management would be considered an asset.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Significant* and recent* experience coordinating construction projects in the commercial or industrial building industry.
- Significant* experience coordinating and reviewing the on-site activities of contractors on multi-trade projects.
- Significant* experience interpreting and managing construction contracts ensuring conformance to tender documents and compliance with contractual due diligence.
- Experience developing and reviewing site-specific construction safety plans.
* Significant experience is defined as two (2) to six (6) years of experience. ** Recent experience is defined as experience acquired within the last five (5) years. The following experience criteria would be considered as an asset:
- Experience coordinating construction contracts within the Federal Government environment.
Condition of employment
- Must be able to possess and retain the physical capabilities to perform the position which include but may not be limited to: crouching, bending, twisting, walking, climbing stairs and ladders, and ability to hear to diagnose mechanical troubles.
- Must possess and retain a valid Ontario Class G Driver’s Licence or a valid Quebec Class 5 Driver’s License.
- Reliability Status
For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests

Technical competencies
- Ability to read and interpret construction drawings and specifications as well as compare them to as-built details.
- Knowledge of construction practices and techniques particularly of the architectural, civil, mechanical and electrical trades.
- Knowledge of federal, provincial and/or local regulatory requirements including building and construction codes.
- Knowledge of Occupational Health and Safety Act for construction projects including safety standards and practices.
- Knowledge in the interpretation and management of construction contracts.
- Ability to coordinate the work of contractors for construction projects such as building additions, renovations, equipment installation and commissioning.

Assistant Director, Endpoint Management
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
In addition to the position being staffed, this competition may be used to fill similar opportunities (Regular or Term) that become available at the same job grade. If you’re interested in this type of role, we encourage you to apply.
Did you know? The Bank of Canada is modernizing its digital workplace through a cloud-first approach to endpoint management. As Assistant Director, Endpoint Management, you will help shape the future of how employees work by leading the evolution of device management, virtual workspaces, endpoint security, automation and digital employee experience. You'll lead a high-performing team responsible for keeping thousands of devices secure, resilient and productive, while advancing innovative technologies that support the Bank's mission.
What you will do As Assistant Director, Endpoint Management, you will lead a team responsible for the full lifecycle management of the Bank's endpoint environment, including laptops, mobile devices, virtual desktops and endpoint services.
In this role, you will:
- Provide leadership, coaching and development opportunities to build a high-performing and engaged team.
- Establish operational priorities and align team objectives with departmental and corporate goals.
- Oversee the reliability, security and continuous improvement of endpoint management platforms and services.
- Lead strategic initiatives that modernize endpoint management through cloud-first technologies, automation and self-service capabilities.
- Drive improvements in endpoint security, compliance, vulnerability management and operational resilience.
- Manage operational planning, resource allocation, budgets and technology investments.
- Build strong partnerships with internal clients and stakeholders to deliver high-quality services and solutions.
- Monitor service performance, identify improvement opportunities and implement corrective actions where required.
- Foster a positive, collaborative and inclusive work environment that supports employee growth and innovation.
What you need to succeed You demonstrate strong leadership, communication and relationship-building skills, along with experience leading operational technology teams in a complex enterprise environment.
You also have experience with:
- Modern endpoint management platforms, including Microsoft Intune, Windows Autopilot, Windows 365, Azure Virtual Desktop and Microsoft Configuration Manager (SCCM).
- Endpoint security, patch management, compliance management and vulnerability remediation.
- Cloud-first identity and device management, including Microsoft Entra ID, Conditional Access and mobile device management.
- Leading technology modernization initiatives and large-scale endpoint transformation projects.
- Using operational data and automation to improve service delivery and user experience.
- Strategic planning, operational management and continuous service improvement.
Nice to have The following would be considered assets:
- Experience with Patch My PC, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Qualys, Splunk, Sysmon and ServiceNow integrations.
- Experience implementing or supporting Windows 365 Cloud PC and Azure Virtual Desktop environments.
- Experience with PowerShell, Microsoft Graph API, Power BI and workflow automation.
- Knowledge of zero-touch provisioning, endpoint analytics and AI-enabled operational support.
- Experience supporting Microsoft Copilot, Security Copilot or related AI-enabled workplace technologies.
Your education and experience The position requires a university degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business Administration or another related field, or a college diploma in Information Technology, and 8 to 15 years of progressively responsible experience in endpoint management and technology operations, including experience managing teams and supporting modern endpoint technologies; an equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Innovative Mindset We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement T he Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional). If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.
What you need to know
- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents
- Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Secret
- Relocation assistance may be provided, if required
- Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.
Hybrid Work Model The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.
What you can expect from us This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit A great deal to consider .
- Salaries are based on qualifications and experience and typically range from $153,721 to $180,848 (job grade 19)
- The Bank offers an incentive for successfully meeting expectations at 7 to 10% of your base salary. The Bank offers additional performance pay (5%) for those who exceed expectations. Exceptional performers who far exceed expectations may be eligible for higher performance pay.
- Flexible and comprehensive benefits so you can choose the level of health, dental disability and life and/or accident insurance coverage that meets your needs
- Extra vacation days (up to five each year) that you can purchase to add to your vacation entitlement
- Indexed, defined-benefit pension
We wish to thank all applicants for their interest and effort in applying for this position. Only candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director, Enterprise Data & AI is responsible for the Royal Canadian Mint’s (Mint) enterprise-wide data, information, architecture, analytics, and artificial intelligence strategy, ensuring data is trusted, secure, and leveraged as a strategic asset and competitive differentiator. This position will play a critical role in business transformation, enabling digital, analytical, architecture, and AI-driven capabilities that support strategic decision-making, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance.
The Director acts as a strategic partner to executive leadership and business stakeholders, ensuring technology investments are aligned with business priorities, risk posture, and architectural standards to become an insight-driven organization.

Languages Requirements:

- University degree in related area
Experience:
- Minimum 10 years of experience in data analytics, data modeling, data management, and data architecture

- Proven experience with enterprise data platforms supporting reporting, analytics, and AI‑driven decision‑making.

Additional Qualifications:
- Extensive experience of multifaceted business areas and IT, excellent presentation, negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and communication skills;
- Proven ability to bridge business and technology by translating complex data, architecture, and AI concepts into strategic, actionable insights.

Why the Mint?
At the Mint, you will collaborate with a diverse group of people and be a part of an iconic Canadian organization. Your safety and wellbeing are our top priority. We offer outstanding pay and total rewards for you and your family and you will be supported to continuously learn throughout your career.
The Mint is committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We value diversity and aim to provide an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment, selection and onboarding process to ensure that each candidate is treated respectfully. In accordance with the Employment Equity Act, you are invited to voluntarily self-identify with one or more of the four employment equity groups (women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities and members of visible minorities) by sending your application to the confidential email, EE@mint.ca that is accessed only by the Human Resources section.

Ready to mint your career? Please forward your resume to careers@mint.ca by September 20, 2026. We look forward to receiving your application!

Company Description
The Library of Parliament is a non-partisan organization that provides a unique and stimulating work environment. We are led by our guiding principles of agility, collaboration, excellence, impartiality, and inclusion. For more information about the Library and what we offer, visit Employment opportunities at the Library of Parliament .
Job Description
Reporting to the Senior Manager, Data Analysis and Visualization, the Statistical Officer provides non-partisan statistical services, data analysis and data visualization to support the work of Parliament.
The incumbent performs the following duties:
- responds to statistical and data-related requests from parliamentarians and their staff;
- assists other Library employees in supporting the work of parliamentary committees;
- contributes to the development of research publications
- develops, maintains and updates data-related products and services.
- provides statistical, data analysis and data visualization support across the Library of Parliament.
Qualifications
Education :
- A bachelor’s degree in statistics, economics, data science, or a related field, OR
- An equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Experience :
- Experience working with large and complex datasets from multiple sources and covering different time periods.
- Experience using advanced Microsoft Excel features and functions.
- Experience using statistical software or programming languages, (e.g., R, Python), to conduct quantitative analysis and develop data visualizations.
Knowledge :
- Knowledge of statistical and quantitative analysis methods, data analysis, and data visualization.
- Knowledge of a wide range of tools and technologies relevant to statistical analysis, data analysis, and data visualization.
- Knowledge of authoritative Canadian and international data sources, including official statistical sources.
- Knowledge of current and emerging Canadian public policy issues and their potential implications for the work of Parliament.
Competencies :
- Adaptability
- Client Focus
- Embracing Diversity
- Exemplifying Integrity
- Attention to Detail
- Research
- Teamwork
- Analytical Thinking
- Communication
- Organizational Awareness
Asset Criteria :
- Experience building, cleaning, transforming and updating datasets for interactive dashboards, visualizations and maps.
- Experience using Statistics Canada’s Social Policy Simulation Database and Model (SPSD/M).
- Experience applying Gender-Based Analysis Plus (GBA Plus) and analyzing disaggregated data to identify differences, trends, and disparities across population groups.
- Experience developing high-quality data visualizations, including charts and tables, to effectively communicate analytical findings.
Conditions of Employment :
- A successful pre-employment security screening.
- A second-language evaluation (Bilingual staffing – imperative): CBC/CBC.
Second language self-assessment test: To help you decide if you should apply to a bilingual position, an optional self-assessment of your written expression and reading comprehension in your second official language is available for you to take before completing your application. Try out the self-assessment tests for written expression and reading comprehension.
For more information on language requirements, see the language requirements for candidates .
Additional Information
Please include a cover letter with your application describing how you meet the education and experience requirements of the position. Applications without a cover letter may not be considered . Please combine your cover letter and CV into a single document or upload your cover letter on the second page of the application form.
The Library of Parliament welcomes all candidates to apply and encourages applications from Indigenous persons, racialized persons, 2SLGBTQIA+ persons and persons with disabilities for this position.
We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace by providing a barrier-free staffing process. If you have an accommodation request or require material in an accessible format, please contact us at LOPCareers-CarrieresBDP@parl.gc.ca .
Education and experience requirements will be used to determine which candidates will be asked to participate in the next stage of the selection process.

Senior Human Resources Advisor
This competition may have a hiring priority for Indigenous people, Black people, racialized people, Deaf people, people with disabilities, women, or members of 2SLGBTQI+ and gender diverse communities . Candidates belonging to these equity deserving groups who wish to be considered must self-identify. This initiative is in support of the Council’s employment equity and diversity goals.
About the Role
Under the direct supervision of the Manager, Human Resources, the Senior Human Resources Advisor serves as a trusted advisor that, through the building and nurturing of credible, collaborative, value-driven relationships, provides consultative and advisory services to support, guide and enable management and staff on a full range of talent management matters, including the interpretation and application of the collective agreement/terms and conditions of employment, related legislations as well as policies, procedures, guidelines and employment related issues. The Advisor serves as the first point of contact for labour/employee relations issues and supports the grievance process, investigations, and implementation of disciplinary actions, as required. The incumbent participates in labour-management meetings and supports preparation for bargaining, as needed.
The Advisor is the primary liaison and point of contact between People and Organizational Culture and the rest of the organization and contributes to achieving functional and organizational results. While the role supports specific divisions/sections, the Advisor brings a Council-wide perspective—contributing to, promoting and delivering strategies, programs, initiatives, policies, procedures and best practices that advance Council’s strategic human resources plan and objectives. The incumbent pivots seamlessly demonstrates agility between strategic orientation, operational delivery, and the development of creative solutions to meet the evolving needs of Council’s talent management.
The Advisor also assists in defining, capturing, tracking and reporting talent management analytics. The incumbent contributes to continuous improvement initiatives, provides presentations to various audiences, prepares reports on matters related to talent management and performs other related duties.
Education
An undergraduate degree in human resources or a related field or an equivalent combination of education, training and relevant professional experience related to the responsibilities of the position. Possession of a recognized professional designation in human resources (e.g., CHRP, CHRI, CPHR) is considered an important asset.

Why join us
You will join an innovative and collaborative team helping shape the future of IT security at Canada’s central bank. You will have opportunities to exercise judgement, work with enterprise cyber security tools, deepen your knowledge across assurance domains, and grow through the Bank’s learning and development programs.
About the position
Join the Cyber Security Assurance team and help connect people, information and assurance activities in a way that supports clear decisions and effective follow-through. In this role, you will help make cyber assurance information easier to understand, monitor and act on across teams.
You will work closely with ITS portfolios to anticipate demand, align assurance activities with portfolio roadmaps, strengthen risk monitoring, coordinate follow-up on outstanding items, and communicate results to a broad range of stakeholders. This role is well suited to a dynamic communicator who enjoys building partnerships, working with data, and bringing structure to complex, cross-functional work.
Candidates with transferable strengths in communication, analysis, stakeholder engagement, project coordination or risk management are encouraged to apply. Cyber experience is valuable, but curiosity, sound judgement, attention to detail and a strong desire to learn are equally important.
What you will do
- Build trusted partnerships with ITS and business portfolios to understand priorities, project roadmaps and readiness for cyber assurance activities.
- Maintain and improve assurance and risk dashboards, KPIs, KRIs and reporting views that communicate the status of assurance activities, documented remediation updates and portfolio follow-up.
- Monitor the quality, consistency, timeliness and completeness of risk data, identify gaps, trends or overdue items, and coordinate follow-up with ITS portfolios and accountable stakeholders.
- Track decisions, action items, dependencies and remediation commitments to help ensure portfolio updates are current, clear and ready for governance or executive reporting.
- Prepare clear reports, presentations, briefing materials and awareness communications for operational teams, risk stakeholders, cyber colleagues and governance forums.
- Explain how risk assessment processes, cyber testing, vulnerability management, and third-party risk activities support and connect to the ITS project lifecycle.
- Support recurring portfolio reviews and governance discussions by helping clarify priorities, roles, responsibilities, decisions, action items and escalation paths.
- Maintain risk records, exceptions, remediation updates, follow-up notes and supporting evidence in ServiceNow IRM and related assurance tools, ensuring information remains current and ready for reporting.
- Support continuous improvement of tools and practices for planning, risk management, monitoring, reporting and governance across assurance activities.
- Maintain long-term relationships with internal and external stakeholders while contributing to a collaborative, learning-focused team environment.
What you need to succeed
You are an effective and adaptable communicator who can make complex information clear, relevant and actionable for different audiences. You combine analytical thinking, attention to detail and strong relationship skills, and you are comfortable bringing structure to evolving information, competing priorities and cross-functional work.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear briefings, reports, presentations, dashboards and awareness materials for a range of technical and non-technical audiences.
- Ability to build productive relationships, influence without direct authority, and follow up effectively with portfolio teams, project teams and risk stakeholders.
- Experience working with data to monitor status, identify trends, flag gaps or overdue items, support decisions and communicate an evidence-based story.
- Understanding of risk assessment and risk management concepts, including monitoring, reporting, remediation tracking, escalation and follow-up.
- Strong organizational, coordination and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing demands, track commitments, maintain accurate information and drive timely follow-up with appropriate independence.
- Knowledge of the IT project lifecycle and how governance, risk and assurance activities support delivery.
- A collaborative mindset, sound judgement, curiosity, attention to detail and a commitment to learning and continuous improvement.
Nice to have
- Experience in cyber security, technology risk, operational risk, assurance, audit, governance or a related field.
- Experience building dashboards, KPIs, KRIs or management reporting using risk, performance or portfolio data.
- Experience with ServiceNow IRM, GRC or other workflow, reporting or risk management tools.
- Experience in project coordination, portfolio support or working directly with project managers and technology delivery teams.
Your education and experience
Your combined education and work experience demonstrate that you have the competencies and skills required for the position. We are ideally seeking candidates with a degree or diploma in a relevant discipline, such as computer science, information systems, cyber security, risk management, business, communications or data analytics, together with three or more years of relevant experience. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional). If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.
What you need to know
- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Secret There will be no relocation assistance provided Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.

The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.

The role
We are looking for a MAPLE Systems Engineer to join the Aerospace Research Centre and support the development, modification, integration, certification, and operation of the NRC’s MAPLE — M edium-long Range A ircraft PL atform for E nvironmental Research Aircraft Development Project. The successful candidate would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
Reporting to the MAPLE Development Project Technical Lead, the successful candidate will contribute to technically complex projects involving aircraft modifications, scientific instrumentation integration, airborne measurement systems, and research capability development. The position combines hands-on technical work with independent technical review, systems integration, and stakeholder coordination responsibilities.
The incumbent will support the MAPLE Project Team in ensuring the technical integrity of project deliverables and may be assigned responsibility for specific technical work packages, studies, integration activities, or engineering investigations. Working within a multidisciplinary environment, the MAPLE Systems Engineer will collaborate with researchers, engineers, flight operations personnel, maintenance specialists, contractors, aircraft original equipment manufacturers, and regulatory authorities to develop and implement safe, effective, and scientifically robust airborne research capabilities.
The successful candidate will be expected to contribute directly to technical work while also providing critical assessment and independent review of engineering analyses, designs, certification documentation, and contractor deliverables.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
A Master’s degree from a recognized university in aerospace, mechanical, electrical, systems engineering, or another discipline relevant to research aircraft systems, airborne science infrastructure design and certification, or aircraft modification programs.
A PhD in a field directly related to aircraft systems, aircraft modifications, airborne instrumentation, computational modelling, aerospace engineering, atmospheric measurements, flight sciences, or a related discipline would be considered an asset.
Registration as a Professional Engineer in Canada would be an asset.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Experience supporting aircraft modifications, aircraft systems integration, or aerospace engineering projects;
- Experience with scientific instrumentation, airborne measurement systems, or research infrastructure development;
- Experience conducting engineering analysis, modelling, simulation, or technical substantiation activities;
- Experience conducting independent review of engineering designs, technical analyses, or contractor deliverables;
- Experience interacting with contractors, aircraft manufacturers, research organizations, or regulatory authorities; and
- Experience supporting airworthiness, certification, safety assessment, or regulatory compliance activities.
The following would be considered assets:
- Experience with computational fluid dynamics, aerodynamic modelling, flow-field characterization, or sensor placement studies;
- Experience working with Transport Canada, FAA, EASA, military airworthiness authorities, or equivalent regulatory organizations.
Condition of employment
- Reliability Status
For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
- Candidates will be required to work on and around aircraft, scientific instrumentation, test facilities, laboratories, and aircraft hangars;
- Candidates will be required to wear personal protective equipment and participate in integration, testing, and troubleshooting activities in operational environments;
- Must be able to travel across Canada and/or internationally;
- Must be able to fly as aircrew on-board experimental aircraft and be able to access system locations (i.e., confined and/or high places) on aircraft; and
- Must be able to possess and retain the physical capabilities to perform the position which include but may not be limited to: crouching, bending, twisting, walking, climbing stairs & ladders, ability to hear to diagnose technical and operational problems.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Solid knowledge of aircraft systems, aircraft modification processes, systems integration, or aerospace engineering principles;
- Knowledge of electrical, mechanical, or systems engineering principles and their application in project environments;
- Ability to develop, review, and assess engineering requirements, specifications, technical reports, design documentation, certification documentation, and contractor deliverables;
- Ability to analyze and troubleshoot technical issues and support integration, verification, validation, and testing activities;
- Basic understanding of scientific instrumentation, airborne measurement systems, data acquisition systems, and research infrastructure;
- Familiarity with project planning, scheduling, risk tracking, coordination processes, and multidisciplinary technical work packages;
- Ability to translate technical objectives into actionable tasks and deliverables aligned with project scope, schedule, and project goals;
- Knowledge of airworthiness, certification, safety assessment, or regulatory compliance processes would be considered an asset; and
- Knowledge of computational fluid dynamics, aerodynamic modelling, flow-field characterization, or sensor placement studies would be considered an asset.
Behavioural competencies
- Research - Self-knowing and self-development (Level 2)
- Research - Communication (Level 2)
- Research - Teamwork (Level 2)
- Research - Results orientation (Level 2)
- Research - Creative thinking (Level 2)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile: Research
View all competency profiles
Compensation
The intent of this hiring action is to staff this position at the RCO-2/RCO-3 level, which is an intermediate-career level position with a salary range of $83,985 to $139,608 .
NOTE: Please note that the full RO/RCO salary scale has five levels. Salary determination will be based on a review of the candidate’s expertise, outcomes and impacts of their previous work experience relative to the requirements of the level. As such, the initial salary could be within another level of the RO/RCO salary scale (i.e. above or below the intended level for this position).
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.

The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. Interested in launching your career through a rotation? We are seeking an early-career economist to join the Rotation Program in the Canadian Economic Analysis (CEA) department. This structured program offers a broad experience across CEA while allowing you to contribute from the outset to high-impact analysis that informs monetary policy. Through the rotation, you will learn how economists at the Bank assess economic conditions in Canada, develop the economic outlook, and provide timely advice to support monetary policy decisions. Depending on your placement, you could assess and forecast key economic developments, contribute to staff economic projections or work with economists and researchers on rigorous, policy-relevant research that advances the understanding of the Canadian economy and contributes to the broader economics literature. You could also help develop the data, models, and analytical tools used across the department. You will turn complex economic information into clear briefings, research, and analytical products for senior management and Governing Council. After completing the rotation, you will be placed permanently in one division, where you can build on the expertise and relationships developed through the program.
What you will do
In this role, you will prepare and deliver insightful briefings to senior management and transform complex economic data into clear, actionable insights. Your analysis will help inform decisions that affect Canada’s economy. You will contribute to the Bank’s publications, including staff analytical papers and major reports like the Monetary Policy Report.
You will have opportunities to spend time on professional development. Whether it’s learning new software or exploring recent economic theories, continuous learning is a part of the role. As an economist in the Canadian Economic Analysis (CEA) department, you will conduct economic analysis and research that support the Bank’s assessment of the Canadian economy and inform monetary policy advice.
Examples of analytical work include:
- Designing new models and tools to monitor and forecast economic conditions
- Contributing to staff economic projections using large-scale macroeconomic models
- Analyzing information gathered through business and consumer surveys, regional outreach, and consultations to identify emerging economic trends and assess risks to the Canadian economic outlook
- Assessing the implications of major structural changes in the Canadian economy, such as demographic shifts, for growth, productivity, inflation, and the conduct of monetary policy
- Collaborating with economists and researchers on rigorous, longer-term research that advances the understanding of the Canadian economy and contributes to the broader economics literature
- E xamining fundamental questions in monetary economics, including the design of Canada’s monetary policy framework
What you need to succeed You have the ability to initiate and carry out rigorous research and analytical projects, and to use data and quantitative methods, including econometrics and time-series analysis, to develop evidence-based policy advice. You bring strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate alternatives and develop innovative solutions.
You demonstrate a high degree of intellectual curiosity and a commitment to continuous learning and self-development. You proactively identify emerging opportunities and translate them into forward-looking model development plans.
You collaborate effectively across teams and contribute to shared objectives. You are able to manage multiple projects, prioritize tasks, and ensure timely completion. You also have strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly to varied audiences.
Nice-to-have
- Proficiency in programming with tools like Python, R, Stata, SQL, MATLAB, EViews, etc.
- Experience applying AI tools and methodologies to economic analysis, modelling, data processing, coding, and policy-relevant research
- Familiarity with Canadian data sources and concepts

The role
We are looking for a vibrant and dynamic Junior Researcher to support our High Temperature Materials team within the Aerospace Research Centre. The Junior Researcher would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect, and Creativity.
The primary responsibility of the Junior Researcher is to develop and apply, in collaboration with internal and external partners, predictive models including machine learning (ML), materials thermodynamics, etc. for high-throughput identification and screening of advanced materials for gas turbine engine applications. The Junior Researcher will be expected to think critically and creatively develop innovative solutions and approaches using modern ML methods and identify opportunities to adopt this technology into various research projects within the High Temperature Materials team. The Junior Researcher is also be expected to contribute to design, synthesis, processing, and characterization of the microstructures and thermal-mechanical properties of advanced high-temperature materials. The Junior Researcher works in a team environment with researchers and technical experts in world-class facilities. Activities also include the development of proposals for new research initiatives, project management, and providing service to NRC clients. The Junior Researcher provides input into the overall direction and research priorities for the program area within the context of the Portfolio business plan.
You will collaborate directly with senior personnel, other project managers and external clients.This position will appeal to a person who is well organized, who is detail-oriented, and who enjoys working as part of a multidisciplinary team to deliver excellent service.
If you’re that person, then this may be the perfect role for you!
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
M.A.Sc. or Ph.D. in materials science, aerospace engineering, or a related field with a focus on high temperature materials and application of digital tools such as machine learning for accelerated materials discovery and phase/property prediction.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Demonstrated experience in the research and development of advanced materials, particularly those used as high temperature materials in gas turbine engine applications;

- Demonstrated experience in applying machine learning algorithms and techniques to materials science problems, including supervised and unsupervised learning, deep learning, and reinforcement learning;
- Experience with data preprocessing, model evaluation, handling large datasets, including data collection, cleaning, storage, and management;
- Experience with integration of computational results with machine learning models to predict material properties and behavior;
- Experience in statistical analysis and data visualization to interpret and communicate findings effectively; and
- Experience working with interdisciplinary teams, including materials scientists, engineers, data scientists, and industry stakeholders.

- Experience in business development, marketing activities, and/or the development of partnerships and collaborations;

The role
We are looking for a Senior Power Electronics Researcher to support our e-Auto Challenge Program hosted by the Automotive and Surface Transportation (AST) Research Centre. The successful candidate would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The e Auto Challenge Program aims to strengthen the competitiveness of Canadian auto industry on the world stage by accelerating and de-risking novel Canadian Zero Emissions Vehicle (ZEV) solutions innovation. Specifically, this initiative focuses on advancing, integrating and deploying advanced power electronics technologies for inverter, converter, and controller applications to enable higher power density, more efficiency, reliable and lower cost traction drives, battery systems, and charging infrastructures.
The Senior Power Electronics Researcher is a technical leader who will play a key role in shaping and delivering the Power Electronics theme for the e-Auto Challenge program, bridging advanced research with product ready solutions in collaboration with multidisciplinary teams across industry, academia and government to achieve technical excellence and commercial success.
This position calls for a visionary researcher with demonstrated expertise in automotive power electronics development, system integration and validation for industrial applications.
The activities in support of program area objectives may include:
- Research and Development: Conduct cutting-edge research in advanced power electronics technologies for inverter, converter, and controller applications related to zero-emission vehicles (ZEV).
- Experimental Design and Execution: Design and execute novel experiments to assess feasibility of cyber-physical systems, introduce or improve instrumentation and data collection, and validate applications for machine learning.
- Technology Assessment: Evaluate emerging technologies, instrumentation devices and other tools related to power electronics for electric vehicles applications.
- Collaboration: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support interdisciplinary research projects.
- Documentation and Reporting: Prepare technical reports, presentations, and publications for internal and external stakeholders.
- Intellectual Property (IP): Contribute to the development and protection of IP through invention disclosures, patent applications, and technology transfer activities.
- Continuous Learning: Stay current to trends in metal additive manufacturing through conferences and professional development activities.
- Client Engagement: Support the business development function as a scientific discipline leader. Assist in identifying client requirements and prepare technical scope of project proposals.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, or a field relevant to the position. A Master’s Degree in Engineering combined with experience in research or technology development relevant to the position may also be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Extensive** and recent*** experience in the design, architecture and implementation of high power, high efficiency inverter, converter or controller topologies using Silicon carbide (SiC) and Gallium Nitride (GaN) technologies.
- Significant* experience in systems-level electrical, mechanical, and thermal interfaces optimization to meet performance, cost, and manufacturability targets.
- Significant* experience in switching behavior, losses, and electromagnetic interference mitigation strategies for high frequency operation.
- Significant* experience in developing compact, thermally robust packaging solutions for high-voltage automotive environments.
- Significant* experience in design-for-reliability, design-for-manufacturing, and cost optimization practices.
- Significant* experience leading and delivering research projects.
The following experience criterion would be considered an asset:
- Experience working in an industrial research and development (R&D), product development and/or product deployment environment within the automotive, clean tech or defence sector.
* Significant experience is defined as experience of three (3) to six (6) years. ** Extensive experience is defined as experience of at least seven (7) years. *** Recent experience is defined as experience acquired within the last two (2) years.
Condition of employment
Reliability Status For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Expert knowledge in the design of power converters and multi-level inverters for electric vehicle (EV) powertrain and charging systems.
- Expert knowledge of SiC and GaN devices multi-physics application for high power-density design.
- Solid knowledge of high-voltage design, insulation coordination, dielectric materials, creepage/clearance, and partial discharge phenomena.
- Solid knowledge of electromagnetic compatibility, electromagnetic interference mitigation, and automotive electromagnetic compatibility standards compliance.
- Solid knowledge of motor control integration, drivetrain efficiency, and system-level architecture of EV powertrains.
- Knowledge of project management principles and practices.
Behavioural competencies
- Research - Communication (Level 2)
- Research - Creative thinking (Level 3)
- Research - Partnering (Level 2)
- Research - Results orientation (Level 3)
- Research - Teamwork (Level 2)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile: Research .
View all competency profiles
Compensation
The intent of this hiring action is to staff this position at the AsRO/AcRO level, which is an early-career level position with a salary range of $83,985 to $139,608 .
NOTE: Please note that the full RO/RCO salary scale has five levels. Salary determination will be based on a review of the candidate’s expertise, outcomes and impacts of their previous work experience relative to the requirements of the level. As such, the initial salary could be within another level of the RO/RCO salary scale (i.e. above or below the intended level for this position).
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.

As a Communications Analyst, you will read or listen to foreign language material, determine its relevance and importance as well as produce translations and draft reports based on the intelligence value in the material, to generate leads for investigations.
Under the direction of a Team Leader, you will be responsible for assessing, identifying oral and written communications, collaborate with counterparts and stakeholders, and provide advice to management.
