Required coursework may be completed at the college (e.g., CÉGEP), undergraduate, or graduate level. Applicants must meet all three of the following:
- Microeconomics & Macroeconomics: at least one half-year course in Microeconomics and at least one half-year course in Macroeconomics (or one full-year course covering both); and
- Additional Economics: at least two additional half-year courses or one full-year course in economics**; and
- Statistics/Methods: at least one half-year course in statistics, quantitative analysis, or research methods.
* " Recently” is defined as having obtained the qualifying degree in 2024, 2025 or 2026. Applicants who have not yet graduated may also apply if all required coursework will be completed by June 1, 2027 and the qualifying degree will be obtained no later than June 1, 2028.
** Courses used to meet the Additional Economics requirement should have substantial economics content reflected in the course title, course code, or official course description. The course title does not need to include the word "Economics". About the role
Join the Accounting Operations and Procurement team, in the Team Leader, Cash Management position. In this role, you will lead and manage a team responsible for cash receipt application, collections, account reconciliations, and the reporting of banking transactions. You will provide guidance to clients on financial operating requirements and processes, helping them navigate complex financial matters and enabling informed business decisions. You will develop a deep understanding of business operations through analysis, collaboration, and stakeholder engagement, allowing you to identify financial needs, build trusted relationships, and deliver valuable business insights. As a subject matter expert, you will lead process improvement initiatives to optimize accounting and statutory reporting processes while supporting ongoing transformation and modernization efforts across the organization.
What you'll do:
- Lead and manage a team responsible for cash receipts, cash applications, collections, account reconciliations, banking transactions, and related financial reporting activities.
- Oversee the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of accounting records, reconciliations, and financial reports, ensuring compliance with accounting standards, policies, and regulatory requirements.
- Analyze complex financial information, identify trends, risks, and opportunities, and provide recommendations that support sound business decision-making.
- Provide guidance to clients on financial operations, accounting processes, budgeting considerations, and financial controls.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with internal stakeholders and business leaders, developing a deep understanding of operational needs to deliver value-added financial insights and solutions.
- Lead continuous improvement initiatives by identifying process inefficiencies, implementing innovative solutions, and optimizing accounting, reporting, and operational processes.
- Monitor the effectiveness of accounting policies, systems, and internal controls, identifying control gaps and recommending corrective actions to strengthen financial governance.
- Support audits and financial oversight activities by ensuring the timely preparation of reports, analyses, explanations, and supporting documentation.
- Develop, coach, and empower team members by setting clear expectations, providing ongoing feedback, fostering accountability, and promoting an inclusive and high-performing work environment.
What you should have:
- An undergraduate degree in a related field such as accounting, finance, business administration, economics, or commerce.
- A minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience in accounting with a minimum of 1 year of supervisory/ project leadership experience. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
- Extensive knowledge of accounting principles, financial statements, and applicable financial, legislative, and regulatory requirements.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to gather and synthesize complex information and develop practical, well-supported recommendations.
- Experience with financial systems and software applications, combined with advanced computer skills and a strong aptitude for leveraging technology to support business objectives.
- A demonstrated success leading teams, providing coaching and feedback, and fostering a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing work environment.
- A proven experience driving process improvements, increasing operational efficiencies, and implementing solutions that support evolving business needs.
- Exceptional relationship-building, communication, and client service skills, with the ability to influence, negotiate, and effectively engage stakeholders at all levels of an organization.
It would be great if you also had:
- An MBA.
- A professional accounting designation (CPA).
- Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Financial Operations (ERP Software.
- A Six Sigma certification.

Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.

What you will do Reporting to the Deputy Managing Director, Corporate Services, you will provide leadership for the Bank's Facilities Services function, ensuring the safe, reliable and efficient operation of the Bank's physical infrastructure and workplaces. You will oversee a multi-million-dollar portfolio of operations, maintenance, capital investments and service delivery programs that support the Bank's critical operations and employees across Canada.
As a member of the Corporate Services leadership team, you will play a key role in advancing operational excellence, organizational resilience, employee experience, sustainability objectives and long-term stewardship of the Bank's physical assets.
In addition, you will:

- Lead medium- and long-term planning for facilities services, including operational priorities, lifecycle management, workplace strategies, policies and investment planning.
- Manage budgets, work plans, performance measures and service levels, ensuring effective stewardship of resources and alignment with corporate priorities.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with internal stakeholders, service providers and external partners to deliver facilities services that meet evolving business needs.
What you need to succeed You are a strategic thinker and an experienced leader who can balance long-term planning with operational excellence.
Y ou have:
- Significant leadership experience in facilities management, workplace services, property management, engineering, building operations, real estate, or a related field.
- Experience leading large and complex operational portfolios, including multi-million-dollar operating and capital budgets.
- Strong business acumen and the ability to align facilities investments and services with organizational priorities.
- Demonstrated success leading high-performing teams and developing a culture of engagement, accountability, and collaboration.
- People leadership with a proven ability to build, inspire, and develop high-performing teams while fostering a culture of trust, accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
- Exceptional relationship management and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Experience managing external service providers and complex contractual relationships.
- Experience applying risk management, governance, performance measurement, and continuous improvement practices.
- A client-focused mindset and a commitment to service excellence.
Nice-to-have
- Experience overseeing critical infrastructure or mission-critical facilities.
- Experience working in a highly regulated or public-sector environment.
Your education and experience This position requires a bachelor’s degree in engineering, architecture, facilities management, business administration, project management, real estate, or a related discipline and a minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in facilities management, property management, engineering, building operations, infrastructure management, workplace services, or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Innovative Mindset We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement T he Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional). If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.
What you need to know
- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents

Company Description
The House of Commons Administration delivers outstanding services to Members of Parliament and their employees in support of parliamentary democracy. Our success is made possible by our talented and dedicated workforce. We leverage diversity in all its forms and recognize that everyone has valuable contributions to make and the potential for individual growth. If you dream of joining an organization that is small enough for you to be noticed, but big enough to provide you with a meaningful career, then we want to hear from you!
Job Description
The House of Commons Parliamentary Precinct Operations is currently looking to staff the Cabinetmaker position.
As a Cabinetmaker, you will use your expertise in woodworking to construct, repair, and restore furniture both in the shop and on site, delivering specialized services throughout the Parliamentary Precinct. You will play an important role in conserving and restoring heritage pieces, building custom furniture, and repairing furniture, woodwork, and architectural millwork. A key aspect of this position is your ability to perform wood carving and decorative restoration work, including the reproduction, repair, and restoration of carved details on heritage furniture and architectural features while preserving their historical integrity. You will also provide specialized woodworking services to Members of Parliament, House Administration, and the Library of Parliament, and contribute to special projects and events as required. To succeed in this role, you bring demonstrated experience in wood carving, along with the craftsmanship, attention to detail, and commitment needed to preserve historically significant assets in accordance with heritage conservation standards.
This position requires extensive physical efforts and therefore, the candidates must successfully pass a pre-placement medical / physical fitness assessment.
Top Reasons to Join the Trade Services team:
By joining this team, you'll work directly with heritage and antique workpieces, equipped with a diverse range of tools and materials that will allow you to challenge yourself and thrive in your tasks. You'll be part of a collaborative, supportive team where creativity and camaraderie are celebrated. This role goes beyond traditional woodworking - it's an opportunity to work on historically significant elements. In our family-like atmosphere, you'll have the opportunity to fully express your creativity while mastering a specialized trade. Employment at Parliament opens doors for professional advancement and skill enhancement, fostering a deep sense of pride and accomplishment as a valued member of our workforce.
- Training and development opportunities.
- Work-life balance /35-hour workweek
- 4 weeks’ vacation (minimum)
Qualifications
Education :
- Post-secondary education in woodworking and a recognized cabinetmaking certification obtained through an apprenticeship program, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience;
- Specialized knowledge, training, and technical expertise in wood carving.
Experiences :
- Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with clients, colleagues, and stakeholders;
- Experience in woodworking and cabinetmaking, including the application of both contemporary and heritage restoration techniques;
- Experience performing wood carving and restoration work;
- Experience in the use of various equipment and tools;
- Experience applying occupational health and safety standards, practices, and procedures in a workshop environment.
Additional Information
We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace by providing a barrier-free recruitment and selection process. If you have an accommodation request, require material in an accessible format, or need additional support with the application process, please contact Recruitment and Selection Services at HOCCareers-CarrieresCDC@parl.gc.ca .
Each bilingual position is assigned a linguistic profile that identifies the level of second language proficiency for reading comprehension, written expression and oral interaction required. We are a collaborative and diverse team within ITS with the mission to carry out the roadmap of an effective regulatory IT platform to meet the requirements of the Bank of Canada’s role in supervising payment service providers (PSPs) . We are also beginning work on two new mandates: Stable Coin and Consumer-driven Banking .
Lead by the Director of the Retail Payments Supervision portfolio, you will join a dynamic and highly skilled team working together to design, develop, and support our regulatory IT platform built on the Power Platform.
Further, you will have the full support of your leader and teammates to enhance your skills, experiment, and further your career through our customizable Learning & Development programs across various domains (IT, Programming, Architecture, Analytics, etc.) and relevant certifications.
What you will do As a Developer, you will be responsible for developing new features and maintaining existing components for the Bank’s RPS regulatory IT platform using the Microsoft technology stack, comprised of Power Pages (Portal), Model Driven Apps, Custom PCF controls, SharePoint, Power Automate Flows, Azure services (Function Apps, APIM) and multiple system integrations.
More specifically, you will:
- Contribute to the development of the Power Platform application and peripheral technologies
- Analyze, design and implement enhancements to meet business requirements
- Maintain collaborative relationships with internal clients and external counterparts
- Perform technical and root-cause analysis on issues and make recommendations for correction
- Create working procedures and documentation on solutions and populate knowledge databases, testing plans and results
- Apply a continuous improvement mindset, by identifying innovative ways of doing or providing services to our clients; changing or reconfiguring approaches to improve efficiency and capacity

- Experience developing within Dynamics 365 and Power Platform or other CRM systems
- Experience building custom APIs and Plug-ins
- Proven experience with C# programming language and .NET Framework
- Proven experience with web portal development in a Microsoft or equivalent environment
- Experience developing and maintaining HTML5, CSS, JavaScript web portal applications
- Experience working with business analysts or user experience (UX) designers to creatively translate business requirements and designs into interactive web portal functionality
- Experience and understanding of source control systems, including advanced branching and merging techniques

- Experience with Liquid or equivalent templating engine
- Experience in writing programming scripts using PowerShell

We are ideally seeking candidates with a relevant degree/diploma and 3+ years of relevant experience for the job grade 15 role and 5+ years of experience for the job grade 16 role.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.

Although the position language requirement is English or French essential, we do encourage everyone to improve their second language proficiency for future career growth and to contribute towards fostering a bilingual environment.

2469350.text:
The Parliamentary Budget Office (PBO) is an independent and non-partisan entity providing stimulating and rewarding work. We offer competitive salaries, excellent benefits, and learning opportunities to support professional and career development.
The Parliamentary Budget Officer is an Officer of Parliament mandated to support Parliament by providing economic and financial analysis that supports the quality of parliamentary debate and promotes greater budget transparency and accountability. Before and during general elections, the PBO's mandate also includes estimating the cost of election proposals at the request of political parties or independent members. The PBO's mandate is set out in the Parliament of Canada Act , and employment at the PBO is governed by the Parliamentary Employment and Staff Relations Act (PESRA) . The PBO is independent of the executive branch of government.
The PBO is supported by a dynamic team of highly specialized analysts and advisors. We are currently searching for candidates to support our work as an Economic/Financial Analyst .
The Economic/Financial Analyst conducts analysis that informs exceptional advice on economic and financial matters for the Parliamentary Budget Officer, Parliament, and Canadians.
UNIVERSITY / POST-UNIVERSITY RECRUITMENT 26-PB-14
Economic/Financial Analyst
Indeterminate, Determinate, Interchange
Multiple positions available
Note: This selection process may also be used to establish a pool of prequalified candidates that could be used to staff determinate and indeterminate positions at the PBO that require similar knowledge or competencies.
BAN-01 ($75,825 - $98,000) leading to the target level of BAN-03 BAN-02 ($92,633 - $119,718) leading to the target level of BAN-03 *The target level of BAN-03 has a salary range of $100,999 to $131,623.
Open to: Canadian citizens and permanent residents who are legally able to work in Canada. Consideration will be given to applicants with a valid work permit at the time of appointment for determinate employment only. The validity of the work permit must be for a period of no less than one (1) year from the date of appointment.
Work Location: Ottawa, Ontario
Closing date: November 30, 2026 – 12:00 PM Eastern Standard Time
ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS
Education:
The candidate must:
- successfully complete their Master's degree or PhD in Economics, Finance or in a similar field from a recognized university by December 1, 2027; OR
- have obtained recently (after January 1, 2025) a Master's degree or PhD in Economics, Finance or in a similar field from a recognized university.
Knowledge, Abilities and Competencies:
- Knowledge of financial, economic or quantitative analysis methodologies
- Knowledge of the PBO's activities in the parliamentary context
- Ability to research, consider and analyse economic or financial data and information
- Ability to communicate effectively in writing
- Ability to communicate effectively orally
- Adaptability
- Teamwork and collaboration
- Professionalism
Various Language Requirements:
- English or French essential
- Bilingual Imperative: Reading comprehension: Intermediate level (B) or Superior level (C) Written expression: Intermediate level (B) Oral interaction: Intermediate level (B) or Superior level (C)
Operational Requirements:
- Occasional overtime and variable hours on short notice may be required.
- Travel to various locations within or outside of the National Capital Region may be required.
- Willingness and ability to be present in the workplace a minimum of 4 days per week.
Condition of Employment:
- Successful pre-employment enhanced reliability security screening
ASSET QUALIFICATIONS
Work Experience (Not Essential):
Relevant work experience in economic/financial analysis, OR economic/fiscal forecasting, OR policy costing in:
- a central agency in the Government of Canada; or
- a federal or provincial/territorial department; or
- an independent fiscal institution (in Canada or abroad); or
- private sector; or
- academia; or
- civil society
will be considered an asset.
Additional Information – please read carefully :
- You must include a cover letter with your CV, indicating how you meet the education criteria of the position and how you could help fulfill our mandate. The cover letter must also indicate whether you have relevant work experience that could be considered an asset.
- You must include a copy of your bachelor's and master's transcripts with your application (unofficial copies are accepted at this stage of the process).
- In your cover letter, you must confirm that you are a Canadian citizen, a permanent resident or the holder of a valid work permit.
- If you are currently employed in the federal public service or by a parliamentary entity, please identify your employment status, substantive group and level, and current second language evaluation results in your application.
- Depending on the number of applications, a top-down selection will most likely be used at the screening stage of the process.
- Employment at the BAN-02 level will only be considered for holders of a PhD in economics, finance or a related field from a recognized university.
- Progression to the target BAN-03 level is based on a combination of performance evaluation and merit assessment.
- Satisfactory references and proof of education are essential conditions of employment.
- We are committed to providing an inclusive and barrier-free work environment. If you need accommodation during any phase of the evaluation process, please use the contact information below.
- The PBO can provide new employees with relocation assistance of up to $3,000 CAD (up to $6,000 CAD if accompanied by dependants).
Please reference Staffing Process 26-PB-14 when emailing your CV, cover letter, and bachelor's and master's transcripts to pbohr@parl.gc.ca .

The Royal Canadian Mint (the Mint) is hiring Executive Assistant, who can thrive in a dynamic and inclusive environment.
Reporting to the VP, Human Resources, and supporting the VP, Legal & Corporate Affairs, the Executive Assistant is responsible for delivering all administrative tasks related to both Vice-Presidents’ responsibilities, objectives and priorities. The ideal candidate will have experience managing an extensive range of executive and administrative tasks of a sensitive and confidential nature and will be capable of working independently, with little supervision. The candidate is organized and capable of handling and resolving the administrative difficulties inherent in supporting a diversified team and fast-paced environment.
Your Responsibilities:
Your Responsibilities as Executive Assistant to both the VP, Human Resources and the VP, Legal & Corporate Affairs :
- Manage each VP’s agenda to maximize efficient use of time and ensure priorities, accountabilities and objectives are met.
- Monitor, screen, redirect and respond to correspondence and communications through each VP’s office, including communications from direct reports, Mint executives, Board members and the Office of the President & CEO, as appropriate.
- Draft, edit and proofread correspondence, reports, presentations and other documentation, often of a sensitive or confidential nature, for executive, Board and other meetings as required.
- Manage the planning, preparation and logistics for meetings chaired by the VPs and act as a focal point to facilitate the exchange of information.
- Manage travel arrangements, verify travel claims for accuracy and complete expense reports for the VPs.
- Support the VPs and their direct reports in coordinating special projects, events and administrative processes.
Unique responsibilities by VP:
- VP, Human Resources: Maintain the divisional operating budget, submit expenditures for approval, reconcile monthly financial reports and create requests to purchase goods and services.
- VP, Legal & Corporate Affairs: Provide administrative support for Board of Directors’ meetings, VP town halls and the filing and processing of various documents.
This position offers a hybrid work arrangement, requiring on-site presence at our Ottawa location three to five days per week, depending on meeting requirements and other activities.
This selection process may also qualify you for other positions with similar requirements and qualifications.
Qualifications:
Languages Requirements:
Proficiency in both official languages (English & French) is required at the time of hire. The linguistic profile for this position is:
- Reading Comprehension: C Advanced
- Written Expression: B Intermediate
- Oral Proficiency: C Advanced
If no qualified candidate fully meets the linguistic profile of the position, other bilingual profiles may be considered, in accordance with the Mint’s Staffing policy.
Education & Designation:

The role
We are seeking an instrumentation scientist or engineer who will play a lead role in the development of new astronomical instrumentation based on fiber optic and photonic chip technologies. The Instrumentation Scientist would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect, and Creativity. The successful candidate will participate in the TESERACT project, a CubeSat mission that will demonstrate a novel type of spectroscopy in space. As a Research Associate in our team, you will contribute to the instrumentation effort based on our photonic integral field unit (IFU) architecture through fiber-coupling, alignment, integration, on-sky and in-lab characterization. The long-term objective is a multi-object spectral characterization instrument for biosignature detection on Earth-like exoplanets, with applications in Earth observation. The work shifts from bulk optics to chip-scale photonic processing, improving size, weight, power, cost, stability, and scalability while maintaining high resolution. Key technical areas include:
- Integral field unit (IFU) and integral field spectroscopy feed design and integration
- Fiber-coupling, microlens arrays, and beam-remapping optics
- Optical design, alignment, and integration of instrument front-ends
- Photonic device and sub-system characterization at visible and near-infrared wavelengths
- On-sky commissioning and validation on ground-based telescopes
You will collaborate with researchers from NRC’s Quantum and Nanotechnologies Research Center, the University of Toronto, and Queen's University Belfast, with travel to collaborator sites.

- design or characterization of photonic chip technologies.
The following may be considered as assets:
- Experience working in an astronomical instrumentation development team.
- Experience using or developing optical spectrographs, integral field units (IFUs) or adaptive optic systems.
- Experience with CubeSat or small satellite payloads and space systems engineering.
- Experience working with lasers, scientific cameras / optical detectors.
- Experience working with photonic integrated circuits.
Significant experience: 2 to 6 years of related experience

English

- Expertise in optical component and system design using simulation tools such as Zemax, OpticStudio, Code V, or similar.
- Expertise developing optical instrumentation or devices.
- Ability to analyze complex data sets and statistical analysis.
- Knowledge of computer-instrument interfacing and developing software for data acquisition and instrument control.

About the Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre
We are Canada's gateway to the stars. At the Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre, we maintain and operate Canada's largest and most powerful observatories and represent the country in some of the world's leading astronomy initiatives. We are astronomy and astrophysics experts, conducting cutting-edge research, operating Canada's national observatories, providing extensive data management and analysis tools through our Canadian Astronomy Data Centre, supporting activities at international observatories and developing advanced astronomical instruments with industrial partners. More…
About DAO
The Dominion Astrophysical Observatory (DAO) offers capabilities in optical imaging, spectroscopy and spectropolarimetry, and currently operates two research telescopes: the 1.8-metre Plaskett Telescope and the 1.2-metre telescope, which features the high resolution McKellar spectrograph. The DAO conducts technology research and development associated with instrumentation, facility design and construction projects of the domestic, international and future telescopes they support. The Observatory has been designated a national historic site because of its important role in establishing Canada's international scientific reputation in astronomy. Over the decades, these telescopes have contributed significantly to our understanding of the rotation, size and mass of the Milky Way, and of the rarefied interstellar medium between the stars. Recent projects include orbital determination of comets and asteroids, spectroscopy of magnetic stars, and ongoing studies of distant quasars and galaxies. More..

Position Status: Temporary Full Time
Position Type: Hybrid

Salary: Our salaries generally range from $ 73555.31 to $ 91944.14 and are based on qualifications and experience.
About CMHC
The work you do and the work we do together matters. We come to work every day with a common purpose: to contribute to a well-functioning housing system.
At CMHC, we hold ourselves accountable for our results and support our colleagues in their achievements. We thrive on collaboration, connecting across CMHC and involving the right people to get our work done. Our leadership style is guided by trust , where our leaders favour an adaptive approach based on the needs of their teams.
Join us and be part of a team that's committed to making a real difference and be part of something meaningful.
Our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion
We're committed to advancing employment equity and fostering an inclusive workplace. To reflect the diversity of Canada’s population, we encourage applications from women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQI+ individuals, veterans, and racialized peoples. We also welcome applications from all individuals eligible to work in Canada.
We are also committed to advancing reconciliation with Indigenous Peoples and supporting the meaningful inclusion of First Nations, Inuit, and Métis voices and priorities. While this position is hybrid requiring some in-office presence, a work from home arrangement may be considered for First Nations candidates on reserve or Indigenous candidates that reside further than 125KM from a CMHC office.
Learn more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion
What’s in it for you
We’ve got the purpose, the people and the perks you need for a fulfilling career. Here’s the comprehensive and generous benefits you get when you’re a contract employee:
- Accrued vacation.
- Annual individual performance bonus.
- Support towards your personal and professional growth with training, mentorship and more.
- While positions at CMHC require some in-office presence, alternative work arrangements may be considered for Indigenous candidates.
About the role
Join the Agreement Management team, in the Bilingual Senior Officer, Operations position. In this role, you will manage long-term housing agreements concluded between CMHC and our indigenous and non-indigenous clients, including co-operative organizations, non-profit organizations and First Nations. You will be responsible for supporting and providing excellent client service to help achieve corporate objectives.
This is a temporary position of a duration of 12 months.
What you'll do:
- Undertake a variety of analysis and monitoring activities to ensure compliance and viability of housing projects receiving CMHC funding.
- Analyze financial statements, budgets and conduct other activities to identify issues, potential problems and/or emerging trends in the housing portfolio.
- Work with our various business lines on the sustainability of the housing portfolio and the creation of new units.
- Provide support and recommend alternative solutions in line with our risk appetite to clients and stakeholders, including the communication of key decisions and the interpretation of policies.
- Responsible for operational activities related to payment of subsidies, administration of loans and default management.
- Maintain quality relationships with clients to understand their needs and objectives and explore opportunities to further housing outcomes.
- Prepare a variety of reports, memorandums and communications to support decision making and a positive client experience.

- A post-secondary education in business administration or commerce, with a specialization in accounting, finance or property management, and/or a minimum of five years of equivalent relevant experience.
- An understanding of audited financial statements and ability to assess their viability.
- The ability to interpret program guidelines and policies to maximize flexibility in their implementation.
- Strong analytical, problem solving and decision-making skills.
- An ability to persuade, influence and/or negotiate with others to gain acceptance of proposals or plans.
- Demonstrated organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple concurrent priorities and tight deadlines with an emphasis on producing quality results.
- Strong oral and written communication skills in both official languages.

- A Chartered Professional Accountant designation.
- A demonstrated experience working with different types of client such as : Indigenous clients and/or non-profit and co-operative organizations.

- The knowledge of mortgage financing and social housing programs.

Selection process number: 2090-CMN-26-OC-062
Your place at the Museum
We value diversity and believe we benefit from working in a place where everyone feels included and where the unique qualities and strengths inherent in a diverse workforce are combined. We welcome applications from persons who may identify as a member of one or more other equity seeking groups (for e.g. women, visible minorities, Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+, religious or cultural minority).
You have a place at the Museum!
About the position
The Human Resources Advisor works as part of a collaborative HR team providing practical, hands-on advice and support to managers and employees across the Museum. The Advisor serves a diverse internal client base, from researchers and scientific professionals to employees working in collections, exhibitions, public-facing operations and corporate services. This requires the ability to understand different operational realities, build effective working relationships and provide responsive, client-focused HR service.
The role has a strong focus on staffing and recruitment, with the Advisor supporting managers throughout the recruitment and selection process, from identifying staffing needs and launching processes to screening applications, coordinating and participating in assessments and interviews, and supporting selection and hiring activities. The Advisor also contributes to a variety of HR programs and initiatives, including employee recognition, accessibility, diversity and inclusion, policies and procedures, reporting, data analysis and process improvement.
This is a fast-paced and varied role where several files and priorities are managed at the same time and needs can change quickly. The Advisor works closely with other members of the HR team, responding to day-to-day requests and helping managers navigate HR questions and situations. Strong organization, sound judgment, initiative and the ability to identify practical solutions are important to successfully balance immediate client needs with ongoing projects and priorities.
Service is an important part of the role. The Advisor is expected to be responsive, approachable and solutions-oriented, while providing accurate and appropriate HR guidance.
Working at the museum means:
- Contributing to an engaging mission as well as exciting projects and challenges
- An inclusive, friendly and safe work environment
- A competitive salary established by collective agreements
- Access to federal public service group insurance and pension plans

This position is open to all Employees of the Canadian Museum of Nature and any members of the public who meet the qualifications below. *Candidates must be legally entitled to work in Canada.
Education and training:
Completion of a post-secondary degree, diploma or certificate in human resources management, business administration, industrial/labour relations, OR an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
Language requirements:
English and French are essential Bilingual non- imperative : CBC/CBC
Experience:
- 2–3 years of experience providing human resources advice, guidance and operational support to managers and employees.
- 2 years of experience coordinating staffing and recruitment processes at the local and national levels, including preparing or reviewing staffing documentation, screening applications, coordinating assessments and interviews, participation in interviews and supporting selection committees.
- Experience researching and analyzing human resources issues, trends, practices, organizational needs or data, and providing recommendations to support planning and decision-making.
- Experience coordinating or contributing to human resources projects and initiatives, including planning activities, collaborating with stakeholders, monitoring progress and supporting implementation.
- Experience applying equity, diversity, inclusion and accessibility principles and practices within human resources programs, processes or initiatives.
- Experience managing multiple priorities, projects and staffing processes simultaneously in a fast-paced environment, including competing and time-sensitive deadlines.
- Experience using software applications, with advanced knowledge of Excel and Word, including using data to support HR reporting, analysis and decision-making.
Interested? APPLY!

Job Description
The House of Commons’ Digital Services and Real Property is currently looking to staff the Security Systems Technician position. This position is full time on site five (5) days per week.
As a Security Systems Technician, you will work in a product-centric environment as part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary team responsible for maintaining, enhancing, and installing electronic physical security and connected systems across the Parliamentary Precinct. Your work will support a wide range of technologies, including video, audio, security, control, and other integrated building systems.
You will provide Tier 1 and Tier 2 client support, responding to service requests, performing preventative maintenance, and resolving urgent technical issues to ensure systems remain reliable and operational. You will also contribute to the implementation, testing, documentation, and ongoing support of enterprise-level building and security solutions
In this role, you will work closely with partners such as the Senate, the House of Commons’ Sergeant-at-Arms, and the Parliamentary Protective Service, supporting both day-to-day operations and large-scale renovation projects, including work in heritage buildings. You will follow established standards and best practices while contributing to continuous improvement of systems and support processes
This role requires flexibility to work outside regular hours, including evenings, weekends, shifts, and on-call as system support, maintenance and upgrades are often performed outside of business operations.
Top Reasons to Join the Physical Security Systems Team: You will work at the heart of Canadian democracy, supporting systems that help keep Parliament safe and operational. This role offers meaningful, hands-on technical work in a complex and high-profile environment. You will be part of a collaborative and inclusive team that values learning, professionalism, and shared success.

- 4 weeks’ vacation (minimum)

Education :
- A post secondary degree or diploma in Engineering Technician or related field or an acceptable combination of education and or relevant experience and training.
Experiences:
- Minimum of three (3) years of experience providing technical support and problem-solving for a wide range of integrated, enterprise-level electronic security systems and equipment, including diagnosing and resolving technical issues;
- Experience performing preventative and corrective maintenance on electronic security systems, such as perimeter intrusion detection, access control video management and analytics systems, and high-density videowall displays;
- Minimum of two (2) years of experience implementing and administering of enterprise-level physical security platforms such as Genetec, Milestone, Lenel, or Software House;
- Knowledge of common communication protocols and security hardware standards, such as OSDP, RS485, ONVIF, and SIP, as well as various credential and card formats;
- Ability to read and interpret electrical and architectural drawings, security elevations, and system schematics, as well as generating technical plans and diagrams to document system modifications or new installations;
- Experience supporting small to medium sized security installation projects, including defining requirements, reviewing proposals, coordinating with other trades, commissioning, and as-builts;
- Experience providing high-level client service, including managing service requests through an incident tracking system while maintaining clear status updates, and completing detailed documentation for resolution and closeout.
Assets:
- Experience maintaining and troubleshooting physical security-related Internet of Things (IoT) systems and network-connected environmental sensors;
- Experience developing and delivering informal training sessions for non-technical users and clients;
- Experience managing the Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) process for specialized security components and maintaining critical spare parts inventories;

- Certification and/or manufacture training in configuring and programming security systems and related equipment (e.g., Lenel, Genetec, Milestone, TRAKA, Bosch, Jupiter, Raritan);

Company Description
The Library of Parliament is a non-partisan organization that provides a unique and stimulating work environment. We are led by our guiding principles of agility, collaboration, excellence, impartiality, and inclusion. For more information about the Library and what we offer, visit Employment opportunities at the Library of Parliament .
Job Description
The Information Management Technician is responsible for managing the technical configuration of the Information Management Modules within the Electronic Document and Records Management System (EDRMS) which manage the information resources lifecycle; provides significant technical support to clients (i.e., Library staff and managers from all service areas) related to the management of electronic information resources; develops and delivers technical training sessions to clients and recommends technical solutions.
The incumbent performs the following duties:
- Participates in the development and use of institutional repositories, particularly EDRMS by managing the Records Management module within the Electronic Document and Records Management System (EDRMS) and developing business processes to facilitate the capture, control, maintenance, and disposition of information resources and IM metadata.
- Provides significant technical support to clients (i.e., Library staff and managers from all service areas) related to the management of electronic information resources.
- Develops and delivers technical training, develops supporting documentation, and provides support to users by providing them with advice, demonstrations, and instructions to ensure optimal and effective use of information management tools and repositories, such as EDRMS and Microsoft 365.
- Conducts IM lifecycle management activities for electronic information resources within EDRMS (transfer, migration, reorganization, disposition, …) in all the Library’s electronic environments (Production, Development, and Test) to ensure compliance with the Information Management Policy.
- Performs tests on new product upgrades (Modules/Features and Functionalities) and conducts User Acceptance Testing and documents test results in order to ensure successful implementation of product upgrade.
Qualifications
Education :
- Post-secondary education in a field relevant to the position, such as information systems, management information systems, or computer science, or an acceptable combination of education, training and relevant experience.
Experience :
- A minimum of three (3) years of experience working with systems used for the management of electronic documents and records
- Experience conducting system testing activities, including developing test cases, executing test plans, and documenting results
- Experience providing technical guidance and support to end users within an Electronic Document and Records Management System (EDRMS)
- Experience participating in projects or collaborating with stakeholders regarding the management of electronic documents and records
- Experience working with Microsoft 365 products (e.g., OneDrive, MS Teams, SharePoint)
- Experience working with tools such as OpenText Content Server 22 (GCdocs)
Knowledge :
- Knowledge of legislation, policies, guidelines, and standards relevant to information management
- Knowledge of principles, techniques and experience with complex systems used for the management of electronic Information Resources (such as an EDRMS) is required to support and participate in the implementation and effective use of information management tools, processes and practices within the system
Competencies :
- Adaptability
- Client Focus
- Embracing Diversity
- Exemplifying Integrity
- Information and Knowledge Resource Management
- Quality Focus
- Attention to Detail
- Initiative
- Teamwork
- Planning and Organizing
Asset Criteria :
- Experience implementing digital multimedia asset management systems and workflows
Conditions of Employment :
- A successful pre-employment security screening.
- A second-language evaluation (Bilingual staffing – Imperative): CBC/CBC.
Second language self-assessment test:
To help you decide if you should apply to a bilingual position, an optional self-assessment of your written expression and reading comprehension in your second official language is available for you to take before completing your application.
Try out the self-assessment tests for written expression and reading comprehension. For more information on language requirements, see the language requirements for candidates . https://www.canada.ca/en/public-service-commission/jobs/services/gc-jobs/language-requirements-candidates.html
Additional Information
Please include a cover letter with your application describing how you meet the education and experience requirements of the position. Applications without a cover letter may not be considered . Please combine your cover letter and CV into a single document or upload your cover letter on the second page of the application form.
The Library of Parliament welcomes all candidates to apply and encourages applications from Indigenous persons, racialized persons, 2SLGBTQIA+ persons and persons with disabilities for this position.
We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace by providing a barrier-free staffing process. If you have an accommodation request or require material in an accessible format, please contact us at LOPCareers-CarrieresBDP@parl.gc.ca .
Education and experience requirements will be used to determine which candidates will be asked to participate in the next stage of the selection process.
This selection process may include a second-language evaluation, a written exam, and an interview. The interview will consist of behavioural, situational and knowledge-based questions. Candidates will be required to pass each stage in order to move to the next stage of the selection process.
Qualified candidates from this selection process may be considered for determinate or indeterminate positions at the Library of Parliament that require similar knowledge and/or competencies.
Satisfactory references and proof of education are essential conditions of appointment.
Travel and relocation expenses are the responsibility of the candidates.

2470895.text:
The Mint is hiring a Logistics Coordinator who can thrive in a dynamic and inclusive environment.
Reporting to the Senior Manager, Logistics Operations & Strategy, the Logistics Coordinator is responsible for ensuring the safe, efficient, and accurate shipment and receipt of goods for the Mint. This role supports daily transportation, documentation, and customs compliance processes while maintaining close collaboration with internal teams and external logistics providers. The Logistics Coordinator uses established systems (e.g., ERP) to manage data and performance metrics, helping to achieve on-time delivery and cost effectiveness for customer orders and maintain robust security and regulatory compliance.
Your Responsibilities:
- Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders, identifying their needs and defining priorities in order to create effective logistical plans and ensuring aligned implementations.
- Plan and organize the transportation of goods including selecting the most cost-effective and efficient transportation modes, coordinating with carriers and optimizing routes to minimize transit times.
- Prepare and validate shipping documents (e.g., bills of lading, customs forms, certificates of origin) in line with internal and external requirements.
- Communicate daily with carriers, freight forwarders and armoured car providers to confirm bookings, resolve exceptions quickly, and support the Mint’s on-time delivery and cost targets.
- Accurately enter shipment data and inventory updates in the ERP system (e.g., D365 or similar), maintaining up-to-date, error-free records.
- Support customs clearance activities by preparing necessary documentation, liaising with customs brokers and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations.
- Work closely with internal partners (e.g., Production, Finance, Sales, Security) to ensure all steps in the end-to-end logistics process are completed on schedule for on-time delivery to customers.
- Support safe and efficient warehouse operations by assisting with best practices, resolving carrier and transportation issues, and ensuring alignment with logistics goals.
- Follow all safety, security and dangerous goods handling protocols in daily logistics work.
- Continuously track and analyze key logistics metrics (such as on-time delivery, costs, and carrier service levels) to identify and recommend opportunities that enhance efficiency and improve service and financial performance.
This position offers a hybrid work arrangement, requiring on-site presence at our Winnipeg location three to five days per week, depending on meeting requirements and other activities.
Due to the nature of the role, the successful candidate must be available to work outside normal business hours, as required, to respond to emergency issues and ensure timely resolution.
Qualifications:
Language Requirements:
- Proficiency in English is essential. Bilingualism is considered an asset.
Education & Designation:
- Post-secondary diploma or degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, Transportation, or a related field. A combination of other relevant education, related work experience, or accreditation may be considered.
Experience:
- Minimum 3-5 years of experience in logistics, transportation, supply chain operations, or a related coordination role
- Experience coordinating domestic and international shipments, including customs documentation and cross-border transportation.
- Experience working with transportation providers, freight forwarders, customs brokers, and third-party logistics providers (3PLs).
- Experience preparing and validating shipping and export documentation.
- Experience using ERP systems (e.g., Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP, or similar) for shipment processing, inventory management, and data entry.
- Experience in a highly regulated, manufacturing, security-sensitive, or precious metals environment is considered an asset.
Additional Qualifications:
Skills and Abilities:
- Strong planning, organization, and coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a manufacturing environment.

Defence Industrial Strategy
The NRC has an important role within the Government of Canada's Defence Industrial Strategy , accelerating research and innovation, and helping Canadian businesses develop leading-edge technologies for civilian and military use.
With expertise across fields such as transportation, quantum science, medical countermeasures and advanced manufacturing, the NRC is hiring to drive the development of national sovereign defence capabilities. The following role will support the NRC’s contributions to defence priorities.
The role
We are looking for a Thermal Imaging Specialist to join our Aerospace Research Centre and support the on-going innovative research in thermal imaging aboard NRC aircrafts, including drones. You would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity. The Aerospace Research Centre is looking to expand its capability in full scale aircraft autonomy. As part of this growth, the successful candidate will take a leading role in evaluating data from sensor payloads on NRC aircrafts. In this role, the candidate will collaborate closely with specialists in Earth observation / Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance, (ISR), to extract meaningful information from thermal imaging. The successful candidate will conduct applied research and technical investigations under the direction of Research Officers, including interpreting thermal data, documenting methods and results, and contributing to scientific publications, technical reports, and client deliverables. A key focus of this role is the need to assess the quality of thermal sensors and extract meaningful data that will be used to advanced mission system capabilities including dual defence/civilian applications. This includes:
- Thermal imager selection, calibration, performance and validation;
- Thermal imager operation and configuration.
- Georeferencing of thermal imagery from airborne platforms;
- Extraction of meaningful information from thermal imagery
- Correction of thermal imagery based upon well-developed material, optical and atmospheric principles
- Supporting the integration of thermal imagers with other electro optical systems;
The role will support both relative detection tasks and quantitative thermal measurement applications, with an emphasis on determining the level of calibration, correction, and validation required for each mission. The role will also guide the establishment and optimization of facilities and competencies to advance autonomous flight innovation and foster Canadian commercialization opportunities. The candidate will coordinate closely with the team to ensure effective resource sharing, maximize the impact of new activities, and achieve a “force multiplication” effect through collaboration. This role will also be critical to identify and address gaps, ensuring alignment with client requirements and supporting technology readiness for operational deployment.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
A Master’s Degree from a recognized university specializing in Engineering, Applied Physics or Geophysics with a strong relationship to Thermal Imaging, or a M. Sc. in a discipline related to / focused on remote sensing.
A bachelor’s degree in the same fields may also be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Hands-on experience configuring thermal imagers
- Practical experience with thermal data collected as part of an airborne campaign (piloted or drone platforms).
- Experience evaluating calibrations of thermal imaging sensors
- Experience developing data processing pipelines for thermal imaging output.
- Experience developing optical and/or atmospheric correction processes.
- Experience developing signal analysis methods to extract high quality thermal imaging data.
- Experience participating in applied research, including contributing to technical reports and scientific publications.
Assets
- Experience with hyperspectral thermal imaging;
- Experience with autonomous or semi autonomous aircraft platforms.
Condition of employment
Secret Clearance A thorough security clearance process will be applied. For a Secret Clearance, verification of background information over a period of 10 years is required. Individuals must have lived in Canada for a sufficient period of time to enable the security screening process.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Knowledge of thermal imaging requirements including radiance, emissivity, and atmospheric dependencies.
- Knowledge of airborne data acquisition parameters (flight and environmental) for acquiring thermal imaging.
- Knowledge of thermal sensors, including short-wave infrared (SWIR), mid-wave infrared (MWIR), and/or long-wave infrared (LWIR) imagers.
- Ability to develop a data processing pipeline for thermal imagery analysis.
- Knowledge of geo-rectification of imagery based on Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) input – e.g. as derived from an on-board Inertial Navigation System (INS)
Behavioural competencies
- Technology extension - Results orientation (Level 2)
- Technology extension - Teamwork (Level 2)
- Technology extension - Conceptual and analytical ability (Level 2)
- Technology extension - Client focus (Level 2)
- Technology extension - Communication (Level 2)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile: Technology Extension
View all competency profiles
Compensation
The intent of this hiring action is to staff this position at the RCO-1,2 or 3 level, which is a junior to intermediate-career level position with a salary range of $64,739 to $139,608 . NOTE: Please note that the full RO/RCO salary scale has five levels. Salary determination will be based on a review of the candidate’s expertise, outcomes and impacts of their previous work experience relative to the requirements of the level. As such, the initial salary could be within another level of the RO/RCO salary scale (i.e. above or below the intended level for this position). NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
​
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2025 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.

As a workplace, the Senate is composed of dynamic people representing our nation’s diverse talents, backgrounds and perspectives. The Senate of Canada is seeking an experienced security leader to direct a multidisciplinary team that helps protect the people, information, assets and operations that supports parliamentary work of senators. As the Senate’s chief security officer, the Director, Corporate Security will set the direction for the corporate security programs and deliver responsive, reliable and non-partisan services to senators and staff. You will establish clear priorities, align resources with operational requirements, and foster a respectful, inclusive, service-oriented and accountable workplace where employees are supported in developing their skills and contributing to the Directorate’s success. You will also provide oversight and expert advice on security requirements for Senate facilities and infrastructure projects undertaken as part of the Parliament of Canada’s Long Term Vision and Plan. What you will do We are currently seeking a Solution Architect to join the Financial Market & Banking Operations (FMBO) Portfolio in the Information Technology Services (ITS) Department.
Reporting to the Assistant Director, Banking Operations you will work closely with Scrum Teams to lead the development of Banking Operation technical solution architectures for various projects within the Portfolio. You are accountable for creating architectures for the development and integration of business and information systems to enable streamlined application interfaces, improved application redundancy, efficient distribution of data and improve service reliability in support of business objectives. You ensure that the integration of services, data flow and infrastructure architectures meet evolving business and operational requirements as well as standards for reliability, scalability and availability.
As a member of the Bank of Canada ITS architecture community, you will also work alongside other Solutions Architects and the information technology community to help review and critique other initiative solutions to ensure they are closely aligned with the Bank’s road maps and best practices.
More specifically you will :
- Lead the design and delivery of secure, scalable, and cloud-enabled solution architectures across all phases of the project lifecycle.
- Serve as the technical authority for architecture initiatives, providing strategic direction, governance, and oversight of solution design and implementation.
- Identify technical risks, security vulnerabilities, and architectural challenges, and define appropriate mitigation strategies.
- Assess current-state environments to identify modernization, simplification, and cloud migration opportunities.
- Define and promote architecture standards, technology roadmaps, and best practices, including the evaluation and selection of platforms, tools, and infrastructure components.
- Research emerging technologies and industry trends, recommending innovative solutions that enhance operational efficiency, security, and business outcomes.
- Provide expert guidance in the resolution of complex application, infrastructure, and operational issues.
- Drive operational excellence through automation, infrastructure-as-code, and the adoption of DevSecOps practices and tooling.
- Design, implement, and continuously improve CI/CD pipelines leveraging Azure DevOps, GitHub Advanced Security, and Nexus to support secure code integration, automated testing, vulnerability management, and deployment automation.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate security, compliance, and reliability requirements into solution architecture and software delivery processes.
What you need to succeed As an experienced Solutions Architect, you are a self-starter with the ability to quickly grasp the essence of complex issues. You are an effective communicator, able to clearly convey key points, organize content, and write in a style appropriate to the audience and purpose of the document and presentation. You can quickly grasp the essence of a complex issue and communicate key points. You are self-motivated and independent, requiring little supervision and with the ability to function effectively as part of a team. You will contribute towards creating positive team dynamics by engaging in productive and respectful conversations, dealing with conflict in a timely way, helping team members who may be struggling and having a positive attitude towards the team's goals.
Nice-to-have
- exposure to diverse work environments, with a broad understanding of multiple business sectors, hardware and software technologies and IT security
- recognized IT industry certification such as TOGAF, Zachman, ITIL and project-management certification
- knowledge of: CI/CD tools such as GitHub, Nexus, Jenkins, Tekton, Argo CD, Azure Container Registry, and Azure DevOps[MK1.1] Cloud Environment and implementation Leading vendor platforms, such as RedHat, Cisco, Oracle, Microsoft and IBM Enterprise Java applications
Your education and experience This position requires a bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or a related discipline, along with a minimum of five years of experience in a solutions architect role within organizations of 200 or more employees utilizing various high-availability solutions, is required. Additionally, candidates should have at least five years of relevant hands-on experience with the Bank’s Infrastructure or Cyber Platforms. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.

Although the position language requirement is English or French essential, we do encourage everyone to improve their second language proficiency for future career growth and to contribute towards fostering a bilingual environment.

Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. The role
We are looking for a Site Operations Coordinator to support our Real Property Planning and Management Branch. The successful candidate would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity. As part of the Real Property Planning and Management (RPPM) Branch Operations and Maintenance unit, the Site Operations Coordinator is responsible for planning, contracting and coordinating the delivery of building services and general maintenance requirements within the building. The Site Operations Coordinator evaluates the performance of various building equipment and systems, troubleshoots problems and malfunctions, and proposes technical solutions. The Site Operations Coordinator is also responsible to coordinate aspects of the security, environmental and safety and health requirements within the buildings in support of programs and business operations. The Site Operations Coordinator will report to a Site Operations Manager. The position does not have direct supervisory responsibilities but does oversee and manage services provided by third party service providers.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
College diploma in a related technological or technical field such as architectural, electrical or mechanical. A combination of a trade certification (Electrician, HVAC, Millwright, and Plumber) with the relevant experience would be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Experience in the coordination of activities related to building service delivery, maintenance, infrastructure support, property management.
- Experience in performance analysis and preventive maintenance of mechanical and electrical systems.
- Experience in coordinating the on-site activities of contractors on multi-trade projects.
- Experience reviewing plans, drawings, prepare preliminary sketches and estimates for renovations or modifications.
- Experience with the application of the related federal and provincial building codes, standards, acts, legislation and regulations.
- Experience in the coordination of construction projects (under 100k).
The following listed experience would be considered as an asset:
- Experience supporting specialized research facilities and laboratories.
- Experience working with various computer programs such as AutoCad, SAP Plant Maintenance and material management systems.
- Experience coordinating construction contracts in the Federal Government environment.
Condition of employment
Reliability Status
For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
Language requirements
French
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Ability to create and maintain a safe and healthy environment in compliance with Occupational Health & Safety regulations and legislation as well as construction safety standards and practices.
- Knowledge of building automation systems (BAS) and electromechanical components, including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), electrical, and plumbing systems.
- Knowledge of practices and procedures, equipment maintenance, and technical issues in various trades such as electrical, architectural, mechanical, and telecommunications.
- Ability to coordinate and supervise technical interventions and the work of construction contractors, particularly during projects involving additions, renovations, equipment installation, and commissioning.
- Ability to interpret technical plans and drawings, and to prepare sketches and preliminary estimates for renovation or modification projects.
- Knowledge of project management principles.

Special Posting Considerations:
The intent of this process is to fill positions within the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC). The results of this selection process may be used to staff similar term or indeterminate positions with various language requirements within NSERC and the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC). This selection process will establish a pool of qualified candidates.
IMPORTANT NOTE: When applying, candidates will be asked to clearly demonstrate how they meet the Education and Experience factors listed in the Statement of Qualifications below. A separate cover letter is not required.
Who we are
The Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) is Canada’s largest funder of science and engineering. A career at NSERC means supporting the visionaries, explorers and innovators who are searching for the scientific and technical breakthroughs that will advance knowledge, improve the lives of Canadians and transform the world for the better.
Visit our career page at NSERC to learn more about why you should join our agency.
What you will do
The Program Officer (PO) is responsible for the delivery of funding opportunities and for representing and promoting the agency within the scientific/research community. The PO ensures the integrity and quality of peer review processes and takes part in the planning and monitoring of the program operations. The PO serves as the external facing authority for aspects related to program delivery, directly responding to internal and external queries. The PO provides policy and procedural direction to peer review committees, external reviewers, applicants, and others in the scientific/research community. Provides analysis and advice to management on program and policy related issues. The position may involve supervision of a Program Assistant, including providing guidance and training, monitoring workload and performance, and contributing to performance management activities.
What you need to succeed
Education
- A bachelor's degree or an appropriate combination of experience, training and education.
- A degree in natural sciences or engineering – An Asset
- Foreign Credential Validation against Canadian Standards
Experience
- Relevant experience in post-secondary (university, college, polytechnic, CEGEP), public, private, or not-for-profit sectors
- Experience in the use of systems and tools for searching or managing information
- Experience conducting presentations in a professional setting
- Experience in providing advice on or interpretation of policy
- Experience in the administration or management of programs (including research programs) in post-secondary (university, college, polytechnic, CEGEP), public, private, or not-for-profit sectors – An Asset
- Experience in research– An Asset
- Experience in people management – An Asset
Knowledge
- Knowledge of NSERC policies and the programs the agency administers.
- Knowledge of the research community in Canada, including an understanding of trends in science/engineering research or postgraduate education
- Knowledge of the structure of research or scholarship funding and of the university setting in Canada
- Knowledge of the area of equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) and its various applications to, and challenges in, the Science, Technology, Engineering and Math (STEM) areas and beyond – An Asset
Competencies
- Analytical thinking and sound judgement
- Organizational skills and attention to detail
- Autonomy and initiative
- Adaptability
- Client service- and delivery-oriented
- Ability to work with others
- Effective communication
Security requirements
Security clearance: Reliability
Equity, diversity and inclusion We are committed to inclusive and barrier-free recruitment to create a workforce that reflects the Canadians we serve. We promote employment equity and encourage you to indicate if you belong to one of the designated groups when you apply.
We welcome all candidates, and encourage applications from women, Indigenous Peoples (First Nations, Métis and Inuit), veterans, persons with disabilities, Black and other racialized persons, persons of ethnic origins, diverse religions, abilities, sexual orientations, gender identities and expressions, and members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community .

The role
We are looking for a senior-career Industrial Technology Advisor (ITA) to support the NRC Industrial Research Assistance Program (NRC IRAP). The ITA would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
Regarded worldwide as one of the best programs of its kind, IRAP is Canada’s premier innovation assistance program for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
We are looking for a seasoned industry professional who is absolutely enthusiastic about helping innovative Canadian companies grow and prosper. We need people who see the potential in a business and are driven to nurture it to the next level. We are increasing our staff across the country and our clients need engaged professionals to provide innovative advisory services to help them grow. We are focused on results and we aren’t afraid of risk all in an effort to add positive impact to the Canadian economy.

ITAs are self-directed and work in teams with company leaders helping their firms grow through the commercialization of innovation. They find the work very rewarding with a wide range of benefits , professional development and learn from clients and colleagues every day in a well-balanced work-life environment.
ITAs serve as trusted advisors and mentors to these SMEs, helping them navigate technical or business hurdles, providing important linkages and identifying new opportunities and thereby playing a part in their evolution, growth and success. This is what truly sets NRC IRAP apart – it is part of what we call the ITA advantage. It’s a winning model we have been using to accelerate business growth and thereby creating wealth for Canadians.

- Flexibility: work/life balance.
- A collaborative environment: at NRC IRAP, your ideas are listened to, respected and important.
