The role
Canada is an ocean nation; bounded by three oceans and one of the largest lake and river systems in the world, and with the longest coastline of any nation. Oceans and coastlines present challenges such as security, climate change adaptation and environmental stewardship, as well as economic development opportunities related to trade and natural resource development. These systems are under increasing stress because they operate in harsh environments characterized by ice, wind, waves, and river and ocean currents. The effects of climate change are also bearing new implications on the stability and productivity of these systems. The NRC’s Ocean, Coastal and River Engineering (OCRE) research centre delivers innovative technologies and support to improve Canada’s competitiveness by reducing risks and costs of marine operations while ensuring the safe and responsible development of marine-based resources. We provide the expertise and tools to improve the performance and safety of marine operations, meet the challenges of a changing climate, and protect people, property and infrastructure from severe weather events and other environmental risks. Our suite of offerings include physical and numerical modelling, engineering analysis, technology development as well as full scale experiments and field work conducted with the support of world-class test facilities capable of reproducing a wide range of ice, wave, current and wind conditions. The Director, Research and Development manages the capability embodied in assigned research centre resources, ensuring relevance, focus and utility by working with program leaders and external stakeholders, including clients. The Director supervises Team Leaders to achieve effective execution of project management and continuous professional development of staff. We have an exciting opportunity in the Central and North Region (CNR)!
The Technical Specialist, Fire and Life Safety, develops, implements, delivers, enforces and monitors Client-Partner fire and life protection programs. The incumbent acts as a technical specialist, providing technical and administrative advice and guidance on fire and life safety, prevention, engineering, investigation, training and building emergency plans.
KEY AND PERIODIC ACTIVITIES The duties and responsibilities listed below are representative but not all-inclusive: Primary
- Lead fire prevention initiatives (e.g. issue Hot Work permits, follow up on action items in fire prevention reports, inspect venues prior to events)
- Oversee fire engineering construction and commissioning plans to ensure compliance.
- Oversee inspection, testing, monitoring and/or maintenance of fire suppression and detection systems and standpipe systems
- Maintain, design and review construction and acceptance testing reports
- Provide fire training for the Client-Partners and on-site civilians
- Develop and maintain effective relationships within DCC, and with industry, the Client-Partners and/or stakeholders
- Ensure quality standards are met, in line with corporate and Client-Partner expectations
Other
- Carry out preliminary fire investigations and contact appropriate authorities, when required
- Attend meetings as a professional member (e.g. boards of inquiry, summary investigations, official planning)
- Maintain records of fire incidents (i.e. Integrated Fire Services Management and Reporting)
- Act as the emergency coordinator, including developing an emergency plan, monitoring adherence to government building codes, and maintaining emergency training and other records
- Support and/or lead business development activities
- Manage risk
- Other duties as assigned
SKILLS General and Specific Knowledge
- Best practices, methods, trends and legislation in fire prevention and enforcement and health and safety.
- Building materials, construction and principles of combustion
- Building extinguishing and alarm systems
- Project and risk management principles.
Formal Education and/or Certification(s) and Experience
- Minimum: college diploma in fire and life safety systems or related field with four years' relevant experience, or the equivalent
- Preferred: National Fire Protection Association certification (Fire Inspector Certificate Level III and Certified Fire Plan Examiner) with a minimum of three years’ experience in a fire engineering organization, including involvement in fire inspection, fire safety plan review, engineering plan review, compliance/acceptance testing and report review for fire detection and suppression systems; membership in the National Association of Fire Investigators.
Abilities
- Use applicable computer software and operating systems
- Read and interpret construction plans and specifications related to fire
- Apply functional advice and guidance to employees and the Client-Partners
DEVELOPMENT AND LEADERSHIP
- Provide functional advice and guidance to employees and the Client-Partners
WORKING CONDITIONS
- Typical office environment with occasional trave.
Some work may be located on construction sites; incumbent may occasionally be required to wear basic safety equipment

Your package includes:
Health and Wellness
- 100% employer-paid annual sick leave, and health and dental premiums
- $400 wellness allowance to help cover expenses such as a gym membership
- $2,500 for mental health services on top of regular $2,500 paramedical coverage
- Telus Virtual Health Care and $750 Health Care Spending Account for some expenses not covered under provincial plans
Home and Family
- Life, accidental-death, and short-term disability insurance
- Enhanced inConfidence employee and family assistance program
- Maternity and parental leave top-up plan to 93% of regular gross earnings for up to 37 weeks
- Flexible workplace options, including $400 allowance every two years, to support working from home
Leave and Retirement
- Public-service pension
- Comprehensive vacation and other paid-leave plans, along with enhanced travel benefits coverage

As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. The role
Help bring research to life and drive your career forward with the National Research Council of Canada (NRC), Canada's largest research and technology organization.
We are looking for a dynamic and collaborative Director to provide leadership to the Prevention and Field Operations Directorate of the Health, Safety and Environment Branch and to the leaders within the organization. The Director would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) Branch develops and delivers initiatives for the purpose of strengthening occupational health and safety (OHS) and environmental management throughout NRC. HSE branch develops and implements policies for the purpose of protecting people and the environment from the risks associated with NRC’s operations and to accurately identify and reduce associated liability while providing NRC with OHS and environmental services that include guidance and support to our operations for the purpose of complying with applicable policies and legislative requirements.
The successful candidate provides strategic and operational leadership in the management of Occupational Safety & Health and Environmental Stewardship activities ensuring that these activities are aligned with NRC’s strategic goals and impacts. The individual oversees the delivery of high quality services through the implementation of policy instruments, and ensures that systems are in place to maintain compliance, as well as reports on these as required. In addition, they will oversee a group of PFO Managers across the Council from their homebase in Ottawa.

University degree in engineering, business, science, industrial hygiene or in a related field from a recognized university or an equivalent combination of education and recent practical experience in a similar environment may be considered.

- Experience developing and implementing policies, procedures and supporting systems for occupational health and safety as well as environmental management.
- Experience providing advice and briefings to executives, management boards and external stakeholders.

We are looking for an RPAS Pilot – Flight Operations Specialist to support advanced research and development and join the Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) and RPAS Traffic Management (RTM) team within the Centre for Drone Innovation (CDI) in Mirabel. The new CDI is part of the Aerospace Research Centre’s Drone and Flight Autonomy Lab. It will strengthen Canada’s ability to research, develop, test and validate advanced drone technologies.
The successful candidate would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect, and Creativity.
Working with a multidisciplinary team of engineers, technicians and researchers, the RPAS Pilot will support experimental aircraft integration, flight‑test campaigns and operational demonstrations. The role includes responsibility for operational planning, flight safety, regulatory compliance and coordination of flight activities supporting research and technology development.
The role will contribute to the safe and efficient operation of experimental RPAS platforms while supporting research activities in autonomy, sensor integration, communications and mission systems.

- Experience coordinating aviation operations with engineering or research teams in multidisciplinary technical environments; and
- Experience developing operational procedures, flight test plans or aviation safety documentation

- Experience supporting experimental aircraft development or technology demonstrations;

We are seeking a Director, Research and Development (R&D) –Immunology to provide scientific and strategic leadership within the Human Health Therapeutics (HHT) Research Centre. The successful candidate will be an accomplished scientific leader with a demonstrated record of advancing innovative therapeutics from discovery through pre-clinical development while building impactful collaborations with industry, academia, hospitals, government organizations, and international partners.
The Human Health Therapeutics Research Centre accelerates the discovery, development, and translation of innovative biologics and advanced therapies that improve the health and well-being of Canadians. Through collaborative research and technology development, HHT advances vaccines, antibodies, cell and gene therapies, biomanufacturing technologies, and emerging therapeutic platforms while supporting the growth and competitiveness of Canada's life sciences sector. The Director, R&D –Immunology is one of the senior scientific leaders within HHT, reporting to the Director General. The Director provides leadership for multidisciplinary research activities spanning immunology, translational sciences, pre-clinical development, advanced analytics, in vivo imaging, animal models, biologics and vaccine development, cell and gene therapies, and phage-based therapeutics. Working closely with other R&D Directors and operational leaders across HHT, the Director will shape scientific strategy, oversee complex research programs, develop partnerships, and ensure the delivery of high-impact outcomes that advance Canadian innovation and public health priorities.

Senior Specialist, Workforce Capability
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
What you will do
Help shape the workforce capabilities the Bank needs for the future. As Senior Specialist, Workforce Capability, you will lead high-impact, enterprise-wide initiatives spanning organizational development, strategic workforce planning, competency enablement and workforce transformation. Working across Human Resources and with leaders throughout the Bank, you will turn emerging priorities—including artificial intelligence (AI), work redesign and new ways of working—into practical strategies, tools and experiences that strengthen organizational effectiveness and workforce readiness.
In addition:
- Lead enterprise workforce capability initiatives supporting priorities such as AI adoption, work redesign and new ways of working.
- Advance strategic workforce planning by identifying future needs, critical capabilities, talent risks and actions.
- Provide expert organizational development advice and facilitation by diagnosing needs, designing interventions and guiding complex discussions.
- Create and improve frameworks, tools and playbooks that help leaders assess challenges and act on insights.
- Embed the Bank’s competency framework across workforce, talent, learning, leadership and employee-development practices.
- Provide senior-level thought and project leadership, aligning stakeholders, managing risks and supporting adoption.
What you need to succeed

About the role
Join the Enterprise Risk and Organizational Resiliency team in the Advisor, Initiatives position. In this role, you will lead enterprise risk oversight and stakeholder engagement by providing strategic advice to senior management on emerging risks, control effectiveness and the impact of internal and external forces on CMHC’s objectives. You will lead the development and execution of the Internal Control Framework (ICF), including governance, risk and control assessment, monitoring, reporting and continuous improvement.
This is a temporary position ending in December 2027.
What you'll do:
- Provide independent risk oversight, effective challenge and strategic advice to senior management on material risks, control effectiveness, and alignment with CMHC’s risk appetite and strategic objectives.
- Assess internal and external developments to identify emerging risks, interdependencies and potential impacts, and translate findings into clear, timely risk insights, recommendations and briefing materials for senior management, governance committees and government stakeholders.
- Lead the development, implementation and ongoing execution of the Internal Control Framework (ICF), establishing clear governance, standards, roles and accountabilities across the organization.
- Coordinate risk and control assessments, control design and documentation, testing, issue management, remediation tracking and management reporting, ensuring controls are proportionate to risk, consistently applied and operating effectively.
- Drive continuous improvement of the ICF (Internal control framework) by incorporating lessons learned, regulatory expectations, emerging risks and stakeholder feedback, while maintaining an enterprise-wide view of risks, controls and dependencies.
- Lead risk oversight for major initiatives, policies, programs and significant change by identifying, assessing, monitoring and escalating risks, control gaps, issues and interdependencies.
- Establish clear action plans, ownership and timelines for risk treatment and remediation, and monitor progress through to sustainable closure.
- Develop and manage key stakeholder relationships, leading discussions and negotiations to align priorities, clarify accountabilities, resolve roadblocks and secure commitment to material risk and control priorities.
- Facilitate cross-functional forums and governance discussions, translating complex risk information into clear decisions and actions, and establish performance indicators and feedback mechanisms to assess outcomes and effectiveness.
- Demonstrate strong human relations and leadership skills to motivate, influence and develop others, fostering collaboration and accountability while serving as a trusted advisor who advances CMHC’s risk management maturity.
What you should have:
- An undergraduate degree in business administration, public administration, finance, risk management or a related field.
- A minimum of ten years of relevant experience in enterprise risk management, risk oversight, internal controls and/or stakeholder engagement, including demonstrated experience supporting transformation or significant change initiatives. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
- An in-depth knowledge of enterprise risk management, internal control frameworks, and the financial, legislative and regulatory environments relevant to CMHC’s mandate.
- A demonstrated experience in building strategic partnerships.
- Strong oral and written communication and presentation skills; ability to persuade, influence and debate with senior level management; and tact, diplomacy and judgment.
- Strong time management skills and ability to analyze and understand large volumes of data.
It would be great if you also had:
- A professional designation or certification in risk management, internal controls, audit, finance or a related discipline.
- An experience working within a regulated financial institution, Crown corporation, government organization or similarly complex environment.

Gaps have been identified among Indigenous peoples and visible minorities for this position. We will also ensure that appropriate accommodations are made (e.g., specialized equipment, changes to physical workspace) to provide employment opportunities for all qualified candidates. In support of achieving a greater, diverse and skilled workforce, we strongly encourage those individuals who belong to one or more of the employment equity groups to self-identify when applying.
Should you require accommodation in relation to a disability, please tell us at the beginning of the selection process. This information will be kept confidential.
CSIS Offices in Canada are located on various ancestral and traditional lands. In the spirit of reconciliation, we acknowledge all Indigenous People across Canada and their connection to these lands.
The personal information provided in your application is protected under the Privacy Act and will be held in Personal Information Bank SIS/P-PU-025.

2474903.text:
About the job
CRA's National EE Staffing Strategy strives to eliminate gaps for the four EE designated groups: Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, members of visible minorities, and women. Where an EE gap exists at the time of appointment, EE may be used as an appointment criterion for permanent and temporary appointments over six months made through this process.
Employees are required to work on-site in accordance with the CRA's requirement for on-site presence. Workplace arrangements are based on the position, work location and operational requirements, and are subject to change. Specific on-site presence requirements will be shared with candidates selected for appointment. Workplace accommodations based on the duty to accommodate as well as individual exceptions may be granted depending on the circumstances and the nature of the work being performed.
Ready to grow your career? The Compliance Program Branch (CPB) is looking for people who recognize themselves in these statements to staff various AU-01 positions across the country.
We encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. The closing date and time on this notice of job opportunity may be shortened or extended.
We may give preference to the first 300 candidates who meet the staffing requirements to apply. Additional candidates may be considered as needed. If you are considered further, we will notify you in writing of the next step in this staffing process.
If you require accommodation at any time during this process, we encourage you to contact the staffing board at the bottom of the poster. Your request will be treated confidentially. When contacting the staffing board, please do not include any medical or accommodation-related information (e.g. diagnosis) or documentation.
Why work at the CRA?
The CRA is one of Canada's top employers! We excel in the areas of employee engagement and performance, training and skills development, community involvement, health and family benefits, well-being, diversity and inclusion , and much more.
In addition to exciting and meaningful job duties , we offer some of the most sought-after benefits:
- Flexible schedules to find the balance that is right for you between your work and your personal life;
- Generous vacation leave and other leave provisions (i,e. family-related, sick days, etc,).;
- A healthcare plan which covers many of life's events: medical, prescription drugs, vision care, dental care, out-of-province medical expenses and hospitalizations, etc.);
- Access to an advantageous pension plan ;
- A workplace that supports workforce diversity and the development of talents; and
- All necessary work equipment is provided by the employer.
There are also other advantages for candidates joining CPB as an auditor:
- An opportunity to work on some of the largest, most complex legal entities in the country, as well as high-complexity audit cases;
- The possibility to participate in CPA pre-approved programs;
- The annual reimbursement of professional membership dues ;
- The possibility of educational assistance helps cover the cost of eligible learning activities (e.g. tuition reimbursement); and
- Career development and growth within various programs in compliance.
For more information on salaries, please click here .
What does the job entail? We are currently seeking talented candidates to fill various AU-01 positions across Canada in several program areas. Positions that may be filled through this staffing process include:
Income Tax Auditor, Excise Tax Auditor, GST/HST Auditor, International Tax Auditor, Financial Reviewer, and Business Intelligence Quality Assurance Officer.
A few AU-01 key activities include:
- Auditing taxpayers' returns, books, records, taxpayer requests, and supporting documents to confirm and enforce compliance with the statutes administered by the CRA. Prepares working papers, letters and reports to support work completed and compiles asset information to assist in the collection of taxpayer indebtedness.
- Planning how the audit will be conducted; reviews documents and research legislation, jurisprudence, publications and policies.
- Discussing with taxpayers and/or their representatives technical and contentious issues, proposed reassessments, and recommendations regarding penalties and consideration of waiving of interest
For more information on Compliance Programs and job descriptions, please email the contact below.
What is the intent of this process?
The intent of this process is to create pools of eligible candidates at Ontario locations where positions are available, or vacancies exist. The work location for which you will be considered will be based on the address in your Candidate profile, with the aim of maximizing your opportunities to be considered in this process.
Permanent CRA employees at the AU-01 group and level: Lateral moves within the AU group will not be offered as part of this staffing process. You may create and update your profile in the CRA National Mobility Bank to facilitate lateral moves, and you are encouraged to continue to apply to other staffing processes.
Permanent CRA employees who occupy an equivalent or lower level position outside the AU group: You are encouraged to apply for this opportunity to join the audit field, however you must still meet the essential education listed in this job posting.
The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) currently has restrictions on certain hiring activities. As a result, any staffing from this process will be limited to temporary opportunities. Permanent staffing may be considered if circumstances change while this pool is still valid.
To apply
Who can apply
Any individual residing in Canada, and Canadian citizens and permanent residents residing abroad,
And eligible veterans and Canadian Armed Forces members ,
And individuals with preferred status who live or work less than 40km from the position(s) being staffed.
Preference for appointment will be given to veterans first, followed by Canadian citizens and permanent residents.
Please note that this process will be used to staff positions in Ontario only . If you are a candidate from the general public, you will have to pay for any expenses related to your participation in this staffing process.
Pools of eligible candidates may be established for various sites based on business needs. Employees appointed through this process may be required to physically report to the designated work location as stated on the letter of offer.
Minimum staffing requirement
Education:
The CRA's Minimum education standard webpage for AU .
If you have foreign education credentials, you must have your education credentials confirmed by a recognized credential assessment service and provide proof of Canadian equivalency to the staffing board. For more information, visit the Canadian Information Centre for International Credentials .
If you have a foreign accounting designation, you must have your designation confirmed by the Chartered Professional Accountants Canada (CPA) .
Any applicable fees are your responsibility.
Essential staffing requirements
Experience: Option 1:
Have recent and significant* experience with small sized** businesses, partnerships, corporations and/or trusts in provincial tax administration, public practice or industry performing one or more of the following functions:
- Conducting/managing audits;
- Tax preparation;
- Administering accounting policies;
- Providing tax advice under the Income Tax Act, Excise Tax Act and/or Provincial Tax Act(s);
- Interpretation of the statutes administered by the CRA;
OR
Option 2:
Have recent and significant* experience performing audits or audit support functions*** at the SP-05 group/level or higher within the Canada Revenue Agency.
OR
Option 3:
A combination of experience under Options 1 and 2
*Recent and significant is defined as the experience that would normally associate with the performance of these functions as part of the major job duties accomplished for a period of at least twenty four (24) cumulative months in the last three years.
** Small sized businesses, partnerships, corporations and trusts generally refer to those with gross revenues between $1 Million and $4 Million; however, each example will be assessed for its relative complexity based on the information presented on a case-by-case basis.
*** Experience performing audits, examinations, audit support or examination support functions within the Canada Revenue Agency may include, but will not be limited to, experience in the Audit, Business Intelligence & Quality Assurance (BIQA), Appeals, Criminal Investigations (formerly known as Enforcement) or SR&ED Divisions for the purposes of administering and/or enforcing the Income Tax Act or the Excise Tax Act.
The onus is on the candidate to clearly demonstrate that they meet the experience requirement. Insufficient information may result in your application not being given further consideration.
Asset staffing requirements:
- Master of Accounting
- Master of Taxation
- Chartered Professional Accountants (CPA) accreditation designation and are currently a CPA member in good standing
- Currently enrolled in the CPA accreditation program and are working towards obtaining their CPA designation, and are currently a student CPA member in good standing.
Asset staffing requirements may be used at any stage of the staffing process, including to screen applications for further consideration or to identify a candidate for a position.
You must upload your education credentials in the education section of your candidate profile and submit all required documents by the closing date and time of this poster. Failure to provide this information may result in your application being screened out without further consideration.
Assessment
Minimum staffing requirements:
- Performance validation, if required
- Language requirements : English essential, Bilingual imperative CBC/CBC
- Suitability* (if applicable)
*If you are a former CRA employee whose most recent period of CRA employment ended due to one of the following ways, a case-by-case review will be conducted to determine if the reason(s) for your end of CRA employment impacts your ability to meet the Suitability requirement for the position(s) being staffed through this staffing process:
- Rejection on probation
- Termination of employment for incompetence
- Termination of employment for misconduct
Asset staffing requirements:
- Employment Equity
- Qualifications
- Knowledge
- Specific experience
- Additional education or training
- Budgetary considerations
- Duration of appointment
- Start date
- Minimize business disruption
Conditions of employment
- Reliability and Security: (Reliability Status)
Depending on the position to be staffed, you may have to satisfy other conditions of employment, which may include (but are not limited to):
- Willingness to work overtime
- Willingness to travel
- Valid driver's license or personal mobility to a degree normally associated with the possession of a driver's license
- Willingness to work on evenings and/or on weekends
- Willingness to take and successfully complete training
- Willingness to work shifts or a flexible schedule (including weekends and statutory holidays)
- This position requires the performance of field audits and regular attendance at the assigned office. Fieldwork and office presence are mandatory components of the role in audit.
Want to know more?
The pool established from this staffing process may be used to staff similar positions.
Qualified members and former members of the Canadian Armed Forces who receive an offer of employment are not entitled to relocation costs from the CRA. They may, however, be entitled to a final relocation from the Department of National Defence.
Definitions of key terms to simplify some of the language you will find on our job posters are available at:
- Important information on staffing at the CRA
- Definitions for job seekers - Canada.ca
Contact
Name: 62635389 AU01 Staffing Board Email address: 62635389AU01VarPos-62635389AU01DivPostes@cra-arc.gc.ca Important: Although the email address includes a different requisition number, it is the correct contact address for this staffing process.

2474885.text:
About the job
CRA's National EE Staffing Strategy strives to eliminate gaps for the four EE designated groups: Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, members of visible minorities, and women. Where an EE gap exists at the time of appointment, EE may be used as an appointment criterion for permanent and temporary appointments over six months made through this process.
Employees are required to work on-site in accordance with the CRA's requirement for on-site presence. Workplace arrangements are based on the position, work location and operational requirements, and are subject to change. Specific on-site presence requirements will be shared with candidates selected for appointment. Workplace accommodations based on the duty to accommodate as well as individual exceptions may be granted depending on the circumstances and the nature of the work being performed.
MANY JOB OPPORTUNITIES REQUIRE AN ON-SITE PRESENCE 5 DAYS A WEEK OR 100% OF THE REGULAR MONTHLY WORK SCHEDULE.
- Come work for the CRA, one of the Top 100 Employers in Canada !
This staffing process is intended to staff positions at the following job levels:
SP03 (Salary Range – $59,623 to $65,813)
- Bilingual Imperative
SP04 (Salary Range – $65,389 to $73,595)
- Bilingual Imperative
What You'll Do
Be part of a team that helps Canadians access the programs and benefits they rely on. As a member of our organization, you will analyze taxpayer and benefit information, apply legislation and policies, solve complex problems, and engage with individuals and stakeholders to deliver high-quality service and informed decisions. This is an excellent opportunity to build transferable skills, gain valuable public service experience, and make a positive impact every day.
Language:
Bilingual Imperative: BBB/BBB, BBC/BBC, CBC/CBC
INTENT OF THE PROCESS
The Sudbury Tax Centre will be offering temporary appointments for a duration of up to 6 months. Shifts for these opportunities may vary between the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. in the Eastern Standard Time Zone.
As there is an immediate need to staff these positions, applications may be reviewed and processed as they are received. We encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. The closing date and time indicated on this notice of job opportunity may change.
The pool(s) established from this staffing process may be used to staff similar positions.
Assessments will be conducted in waves, and additional candidates may be assessed as staffing needs arise. Candidates who are placed in one or more pools may be considered for appointment based on current and future staffing needs. If you are selected to proceed, you will be notified in writing of the next step in the staffing process.
If you accept an offer of employment resulting from this staffing process, you may not be considered for another opportunity from the process until your appointment ends, to minimize business disruption. You will, however, remain in the pool(s) until they expire.
Types of staffing requirements
Minimum : the minimum staffing requirements indicated in this notice of job opportunity are mandatory for all positions to be staffed. The minimum staffing requirements are- education, language, performance level, security status and/or clearance and suitability.
Essential: essential staffing requirements indicated in this notice of job opportunity will be assessed and may be used to identify candidates for positions to be staffed.
Asset : asset staffing requirements indicated in this notice of job opportunity may be assessed and may be used to identify candidates for positions to be staffed. You will be notified in advance of any asset staffing requirements being assessed, at the evaluation stage, that are not listed on this notice.
To apply
Who can apply :
Persons residing within reasonable commuting distance (under 125 kilometres) of the Sudbury Tax Centre located at 1050 Notre Dame Avenue, Sudbury Ontario.
Preference for appointment will be given to veterans, Canadian citizens and permanent residents.
If you are a candidate from the general public, you will have to pay for any expenses related to your participation in this staffing process, as well as any relocation costs if you receive an offer of employment from this process.
Qualified members and former members of the Canadian Armed Forces who receive an offer of employment are not entitled to relocation costs from the CRA. They may, however, be entitled to a final relocation from the Department of National Defence.
Please note that this process will be used to staff positions at the Sudbury Tax Centre located at 1050 Notre Dame Avenue. As indicated above, many of the job opportunities will require an on-site presence 5 days a week. Further information will be provided if you are selected for the position.
As there is an immediate need to staff these positions, applications will be processed when they are received. For this reason, we encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. Note that the closing date and time on this notice of job opportunity may change.
We may give preference to the first 200 applicants who meet the staffing requirements. Candidates will be screened against the prerequisite staffing requirements on an on-going basis. If you are considered further, we will notify you in writing of the next steps in this staffing process.
Candidates may only submit one application. Subsequent applications will not be considered.
ESSENTIAL STAFFING REQUIREMENTS
EDUCATION
Minimum Education Required for SP03 Positions :
- Successful completion of two years of secondary school
Minimum Education Required for SP04 Positions:
- Successful completion of a secondary school diploma
Some SP04 positions require the following additional educational requirements:
- Successful completion of the following courses or field of studies from a recognized postsecondary institution or from a recognized professional accounting association: Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) Introductory Financial Accounting or FA1 or Introductory Accounting or Introductory Financial Accounting.
You MUST upload your education credentials and proof of your education credentials in the Education Section of your candidate profile and submit all required documents at the time you submit your application. Failure to do so may result in your application not being considered further.
Candidates are responsible to ensure that clear and legible electronic copies of their education credentials are uploaded as attachments into the education factor(s) in the education section of their candidate profile. Failure to do so by the close of this notice of job opportunity may result in your application not being given further consideration.
You must provide education documentation demonstrating that you meet the minimum education requirement for each group and level for which you are applying. You must also provide documentation confirming your highest completed level of education, as this may be used as an asset staffing requirement. If you submit a graduate or postgraduate certificate, please also provide the underlying degree or diploma completed before admission to the program, where applicable.
For more information on how to upload your education document(s) to your candidate profile, please click the following link: How to add your education to your candidate profile
If you require further assistance with uploading your education documents, please email the staffing board at ExternalRecruitmentSUDTC-RecrutementExterneCFSUD@cra-arc.gc.ca . Ensure that you quote "62653773" in the subject line of your email.
Foreign education credentials and designations:
Please note : If you have education credentials or designations completed outside of Canada, please review the following link for additional documentation requirements: Foreign education credentials and designations .
If you have foreign education credentials, you must have your education credentials confirmed by a recognized credential assessment service and provide proof of Canadian equivalency to the staffing board. For more information, visit the Canadian Information Centre for International Credentials . Any applicable fees are your responsibility.
If you have a foreign accounting designation, you must have your designation confirmed by the Chartered Professional Accountants Canada (CPA) . Any applicable fees are your responsibility.
When submitting your application, please review the Education questionnaire for further details.
Note : Your name in your candidate profile of the Integrated Staffing System (ISS) should match the name on your government issued photo ID and your education credentials. If it does not, please correct your name in your candidate profile by logging in to the Careers website or contact the staffing board with any questions/concerns. If your education credentials show a different or former name, please provide proof of legal name change. Failure to upload and/or to provide supporting document(s) will result in your application not being considered further.
EXPERIENCE
No prior experience is required for the above-noted opportunities.
Assessment
If you have a limitation that may impact your performance during an assessment, such as a test or interview, you may require an accommodation, and we encourage you to ask for it. Assessment accommodations are designed to remove the obstacles without altering the criteria being assessed so candidates with limitations can fully demonstrate their abilities. If we invite you to be assessed, we will send you more information on how to request accommodation measures throughout this staffing process. Each request will be individually reviewed. You will be asked to provide information regarding your limitations to be reviewed by a trained assessment accommodation advisor. If needed, professional documentation may be requested to determine the appropriate accommodation measures. All information will be kept confidential. For examples of assessment accommodations, please visit: Accommodation during an assessment as a candidat e .
Minimum and essential:
The minimum and essential staffing requirements indicated below will be assessed during the process and may be used to identify candidates for positions.
- Second Language Evaluation (BBB/BBB and/or BBC/BBC and/or CBC/CBC) for Bilingual Imperative positions.
- Performance Validation
- Suitability If you are a former CRA employee whose most recent period of CRA employment ended due to one of the following ways, a case-by-case review will be conducted to determine if the reason(s) for your end of CRA employment impacts your ability to meet the Suitability requirement for the position(s) being staffed through this staffing process: Rejection on probation Termination of employment for incompetence Termination of employment for misconduct
Asset staffing requirements may also be assessed during the staffing process and may be used to identify candidates for positions. Please note that the list of assets below is not exhaustive. You will be notified in advance of any asset requirements to be evaluated/used.
- Qualifications
- Specific Experience
- Additional Education/Training
- Budgetary Considerations
- Duration of Appointment
- Start Date
- Minimize Business Disruption
- Employment Equity
- Accounting Education
We may limit the number of candidates to be considered further in this staffing process by using a top-down approach to select candidates with the best results achieved on any asset assessment conducted.
You are expected to make yourself available for assessment when scheduled. Assessments will only be rescheduled for exceptional circumstances. The staffing board will make these decisions on a case-by-case basis.
Conditions of Employment:
- Reliability/Security - Reliability Status
- Candidates who have lived outside of Canada continuously for 6 months or longer in the last 5 years must provide a Certificate of Good Conduct (police clearance certificate) from the other country. Candidates are advised to request this as soon as possible. Information on how to obtain a police clearance certificate can be found on Citizenship and Immigration Canada's web site .
- Physically work from the Sudbury Tax Centre located at 1050 Notre Dame Avenue, Sudbury Ontario
- Willingness and ability to workday shift and/or evening shift (between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 11:30 p.m. in the Eastern Time Zone) or a flexible schedule (including weekends and statutory holidays)
- Willingness to be part of a flexible workload team
- Willingness to take and successfully complete training
- Willingness to work in an environment where difficult conversations with clients may occur in daily interactions.
Want to know more?
We encourage you to read Important information on staffing at the CRA to find out more about staffing processes and how to apply. CRA employees support the economic and social well-being of Canadians and build public trust. We have high expectations, and our employees are held to the standards of conduct outlined in our Code of integrity and professional conduct and Directive on conflict of interest, gifts and hospitality, and post-employment .
Information regarding the status of your application will be communicated via the candidate profile on the CRA Careers site. We strongly encourage you to verify the email address attached to your profile and to check your messages (including both your email inbox and junk mail) regularly for any updates.
Contact
Name: SP-03 to SP-04 Staffing Board
Email address: ExternalRecruitmentSUDTC-RecrutementExterneCFSUD@cra-arc.gc.ca
Ensure that you quote "62653773" in the subject line of your emails.

2474988.text:
Reference number: RF-17283
About CSE
The Communications Security Establishment (CSE) is Canada's agency responsible for foreign signals intelligence, cyber operations and cyber security. Learn more about our mission .
CSE is committed to fostering a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion. This isn't just an ideal, it's crucial to our mission. Find out about our workplace culture , including our diversity and inclusion initiatives.
Become part of our team and you'll understand why CSE is the most important organization you've never heard of (YouTube) .
Job summary
CSE is currently looking for Cyber Security Practitioners to work in a dynamic and innovative environment. As a Cyber Security Practitioner, you will use your expertise to provide cyber security advice and guidance, and design and develop secure information technology (IT) and operational technology (OT) solutions. You will also review product and solution assessments according to security risk management principles in a variety of positions relating to Cyber Security.
We are looking for people who are curious to learn new technologies, who possess great communication skills and enjoy collaborating with others to deliver exceptional services to clients. Cyber security roles also call for self-motivation and problem-solving. Being comfortable managing your own time and balancing conflicting priorities will help you thrive in our fast-paced environment.
When applying to this process, you will be asked to select which positions you would like to be considered for. Matching you to the best hiring group will be based on a combination of your interests and our organizational needs. We have a variety of positions to fill, including but not limited to:
Cyber Security Advisor
Provides advice and guidance to clients by:
- performing design reviews and participating in design workshops
- liaising between partners/clients and our internal technical staff
- representing CSE in technical partner/client discussions
- working with design, engineering, and IT/OT security teams to assess risk for IT/OT systems or cloud solutions
- creating practical and technical advice and guidance on cyber security
Information Systems Security Developer/Architect/Engineer
Develops and documents innovative secure IT security solutions such as:
- secure cellular / wireless capabilities
- wireless intrusion detection and continuous monitoring solutions
- secure cloud environments
- cross domain solutions
- cyber security research environment
Cyber Security Analyst
- Specializes in network and IT infrastructure security and understands cyberattacks, malware and behaviour of cybercriminals
- Investigates, analyzes, and helps clients respond to cyber security incidents
- Searches for threats to Canada's threat surface, including ongoing cyber activity and vulnerabilities in software, hardware, or firmware
- Produces reports relating to cyber activities for dissemination to partners/clients
Information Security Assessor
- Assesses IT systems, applications, and networks for security vulnerabilities
- Performs static and dynamic analysis of software and systems
- Uses industry tools, techniques and methodologies to detect, analyze and exploit network vulnerabilities
- Provides tailored advice and guidance to clients based on these assessments
- Conduct or assist Government Departments in conducting IT security and risk assessments on cloud service providers (CSPs)
Salary
To find out more about our salary scale, vacation allowances and benefits (health, dental & pension plans, etc.) visit the Compensation page on our website.
Area of selection
Open to Canadian citizens.
Location
The majority of our jobs are in Ottawa, Ontario. CSE has two accessible facilities . Flexible work arrangements, including telework for a portion of the work week, may be possible.
Conditions of employment
A valid Enhanced Top Secret (ETS) security clearance is a condition of employment that must be met before an offer can be made.
More information about our hiring and security processes can be found on our website.
Essential qualifications
In order to be considered, your cover letter must clearly explain how you meet the following education and experience requirements.
Education
You must have either one of the following:
- a University degree in a field related to the position, such as (but not limited to): Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology or Engineering
- a College diploma in a field related to the position (as above)
- an acceptable combination of education and experience relevant to the position
Note: The educational program must be recognized in Canada, and you must be able to provide proof of education credentials. Students graduating within the next twelve months are eligible to apply.
Experience
You must demonstrate two (2) of the three (3) following criteria:
- experience designing, creating, testing, deploying or operating information technology (IT) and/or operational technology (OT) security solutions
- experience designing, analyzing, planning, developing, implementing or operating IT and/or operational technology (OT) programs, projects or technical systems
- experience providing advice and recommendations to clients, peers or management of IT and/or operational technology (OT)
Recent graduates should note that school projects can be considered as relevant experience.
Official language requirements
English essential or bilingual imperative: language profile BBB/BBB
- English essential means that the position is unilingual English.
- Bilingual means that knowledge of both official languages (English and French) is required for the position. Imperative means that you must possess the knowledge of both official languages before a job offer can be made.
- The profile (BBB/BBB) represent the proficiency level you must demonstrate in each of the language skills (reading, writing and oral interaction) for the bilingual position. For bilingual positions, second language evaluations will be offered to successful candidates who don't have valid language test results issued by the Government of Canada.
Find out more about the language requirements of positions.
Competencies
The following technical, behavioural and leadership competencies will be assessed at a later date. You do not need to include information about them in your application.
Technical competencies
- Knowledge of Information Management (IM)/Information Technology (IT) Architecture
- Knowledge of Information Technology (IT) Security
- Knowledge of Information Technology
Functional competencies
- Analytical Thinking (only applies to UNMA-08 and UNMA-09 positions)
Behavioural competencies
- Accountability/autonomy
- Interactive communication
- Working in a team
Leadership competencies
- Change and innovation
- Collaboration
- Achieving Results (only applies to UNMA-09 position)
Assets
Assets are "nice-to-have" expertise and skills we're interested in. Your application will not be rejected if you do not meet or possess these qualifications. However, if you do have them, they may be used to identify which team you could best complement.
Asset education
- Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
- Certified Cloud Security Professional (CCSP)
Note: The educational program must be recognized in Canada and you must be able to provide proof of education credentials.
Asset experience
- Experience in network virtualization, cloud technologies and/or cryptography
- Experience in operational technology (OT) environments
- Experience in Identity and Access Management
- Experience presenting briefings to clients, peers, or management in IT
- Experience writing or working with Threat and Risk Assessments
- Experience in product testing and evaluation
- Experience in the security-related system management of either Windows or Linux server(s) or workstation (including Virtual Machines)
- Experience in the security configuration of enterprise telecommunications / unified communications platforms and/or enterprise networking (e.g., Cisco, Juniper)
- Experience with security protocols (e.g., TLS, HTTPS, IPSec, IKE), communications protocols (e.g., VoIP/SIP, REST interfaces, RCP, TCP streaming) and/or analysis tools (Wireshark, tcpdump, SIPp, etc.)
- Experience in component hardening and/or writing/editing component hardening guides
- Experience evaluating and testing IT security products against security requirements (e.g., Common Criteria, FIPS 140-2, High Assurance standards)
- Experience using vulnerability assessment software and tools (Nessus, Nexpose, nmap, Burpsuite, Qualys, OpenVAS)
- Experience with designing or implementing an Enterprise Vulnerability management program
- Experience with the security control catalogue specified by ITSG-33 or NIST 800-53
- Experience conducting cyber security functions (configuring, collecting logs, monitoring, hardening, etc.) in a public cloud
- Experience in handling cyber incidents
- Experience in scripting or automation
Asset competencies
The following asset technical, behavioural and leadership competencies may be assessed at a later date. You do not need to include information about them in your application.
Asset technical competencies
- Risk Management
Operational requirements
Overtime and standby duty may be required.
How to apply
You may submit your candidacy online by selecting "Apply" at the bottom of this page.
If you cannot apply online or have a disability preventing you from applying online, please inform us by email at careers-carrieres@cse-cst.gc.ca prior to the closing date of this hiring process.
Important information
We ask you to not discuss your application with others (including on social media) besides your partner, or close family members - who should also be reminded about the need to be discreet.
Assessments of candidates are conducted in the official language of their choice.
To address CSE's current representation gaps, priority may be given to persons who self-declare as belonging to one, or more, designated employment equity groups: women; Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, including people with a mental health condition and neurodivergent people; and persons from racial or ethnic groups.
Please note the Employment Equity Act , which is under review, uses the terminology Aboriginal peoples and visible minorities.
CSE offers an assessment process that will accommodate any reasonable measures you require to be assessed in a fair and equitable manner. Those measures are available to all candidates during our processes. Information you provide will be addressed confidentially.
The level of competence demonstrated in the various assessments will be used to determine your qualifications for the UNMA-07, UNMA-08 or UNMA-09 level.
If you do not meet all technical competencies, you could be considered for an underfill appointment. For example, if during the assessment phase of the selection process, a candidate has not demonstrated the required proficiency level for some of the technical competencies of the position but has demonstrated the potential to develop those competencies through specified training and/or development, an underfill appointment could be considered. The candidate would be appointed at one level lower than the substantive level of the position. In which case, an individual development plan will be established, depending on your qualifications and experience.
All communications with CSE relating to this process, including email messages and telephone conversations, may be used in the assessment of qualifications.

Senior Data Scientist, Economics & AI
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
What you need to know
We are seeking a Senior Data Scientist with strong economics and quantitative modelling expertise to help shape the future of economic research, policy analysis, and data-driven decision-making at the Bank of Canada. You will provide technical and methodological leadership in applying advanced analytics, machine learning (ML), artificial intelligence (AI), and quantitative methods to complex economic research and policy challenges. Your work will influence analytical practices, strengthen organizational capabilities, and support evidence-based decisions across the Bank’s policy and research functions.
Reporting to the Assistant Director, Data Science, within the Department of Data and Digital Services (DDS), you will bring together economics, data science, and emerging technologies. Partnering closely with economists, researchers, business clients, and technology teams, you will develop and apply advanced analytical solutions, AI-enabled tools, and modelling capabilities that enhance the effectiveness, accessibility, and productivity of research, policy analysis, and decision-making. This role offers a unique opportunity to influence how advanced analytics and AI are adopted across the organization, helping modernize research and analytical practices while contributing to high-impact initiatives that matter to Canadians. Through your expertise, you will contribute to building new, sustainable analytical capabilities that support the organization's long-term research, policy, and strategic objectives.
What you will do
As a Senior Data Scientist, you will lead complex analytical initiatives that advance economic research, forecasting, policy analysis, and evidence-based decision-making. Drawing on expertise in economics, data science, and emerging technologies, you will provide technical and methodological leadership while strengthening the Bank’s AI and data science capabilities.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Leading the design, development, validation, deployment, and operationalization of statistical, econometric, ML, and AI models that address complex economic, research, and policy questions.
- Building AI-enabled applications, analytical tools, reusable frameworks, and scalable data products that improve research, modelling, forecasting, and decision-making workflows.
- Partnering with economists, researchers, business stakeholders, and technology teams to identify, prioritize, and implement opportunities where data science and AI can improve analytical outcomes and operational effectiveness.
- Translating analytical findings into actionable insights and clearly communicating methodologies, assumptions, limitations, and results to technical and non-technical audiences.
- Providing technical and methodological guidance, mentoring team members, and supporting the successful delivery of complex analytical initiatives.
- Establishing and promoting best practices in reproducible research, model governance, responsible AI, model explainability, documentation, and analytical quality.
- Evaluating emerging AI, ML, and analytical methods and guiding their appropriate adoption to strengthen economic models, research methodologies, forecasting approaches, and decision-making workflows.
What you need to succeed
You are a collaborative and innovative data scientist with strong expertise in economics and quantitative modelling. You combine deep technical knowledge and sound methodological judgment with the ability to communicate complex concepts clearly, influence stakeholders, and translate economic research and policy challenges into impactful analytical solutions.
You are comfortable navigating ambiguity and working in complex environments. You continuously expand your knowledge of emerging AI and data science methods and contribute to a culture of learning, collaboration, and knowledge-sharing.
You bring:
- Demonstrated experience leading complex analytical projects and delivering impactful business, policy, or research outcomes.
- Expertise in econometrics, forecasting, statistical modelling, ML, AI, and quantitative analysis.
- Experience applying large language models (LLMs), generative AI, agentic AI systems, or other emerging AI technologies to research, analytical, or decision-support use cases.
- Proficiency with programming languages such as Python, MATLAB, or similar analytical computing tools.
- Experience working with cloud-based analytics platforms such as Azure, Databricks, or equivalent environments.
- Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
- Experience contributing to economic research, forecasting studies, policy papers, or other analytical publications that support evidence-based decision-making.
Nice-to- Have
- Experience:
- designing enterprise analytical solutions or analytical platforms.
- supporting AI adoption initiatives and organizational capability development.
- leading cross‑functional collaborations involving business partners, researchers, and technology teams.
Education and Experience
This position requires a master’s degree or higher in economics, econometrics, statistics, mathematics, data science, computer science, or a related quantitative discipline, along with a minimum of six years of experience applying advanced quantitative methods, including ML, AI, statistical modelling, and econometrics, in support of economic policy, research, forecasting, or evidence-based decision-making. An equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may also be considered.
Innovative Mindset We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. Although the position language requirement is English or French essential, we do encourage everyone to improve their second language proficiency for future career growth and to contribute towards fostering a bilingual environment.

- Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Reliability
- Relocation assistance may be provided, if required
- Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.

Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.

About the role
Join the Enterprise Data and Analytics team, in the Bilingual Senior Manager, Data and Information Governance position, and play a key role in advancing how CMHC manages data as a strategic enterprise asset.
In this role, you will lead the operationalization of enterprise data management capabilities and services across the organization, including data quality, metadata, lineage, reference and master data, data domains, observability and lifecycle controls. Through this work, you will strengthen the quality, consistency and accessibility of CMHC’s data and help ensure it is trusted, discoverable and fit for purpose, enabling reliable reporting and analytics, strong operational performance, regulatory compliance and informed decision-making.
What you’ll do:
- Lead and manage the enterprise Data Management function, including its priorities, service commitments, performance targets, resources and delivery plans.
- Operationalize and continuously improve enterprise capabilities for data quality, metadata, lineage, observability, lifecycle management, data domains, reference data and master data.
- Establish scalable standards, processes and controls to improve the consistency, accessibility, reliability and responsible management of data throughout its lifecycle.
- Oversee enterprise data quality practices, including monitoring, controls, issue management, remediation oversight and continuous improvement for critical data assets and priority domains.
- Advance metadata, business definitions, lineage and domain management to improve data discoverability, understanding, traceability and confidence in reporting and analytics.
- Lead master and reference data services to support consistent enterprise definitions, reduce fragmentation and improve integration and operational efficiency.
- Own and evolve enterprise data management tools and services, including the business ownership and adoption of platforms such as Informatica.
- Collaborate with business, IT, architecture, governance, privacy, security and risk partners; define KPIs, KRIs and service measures; and lead a high-performing team that delivers measurable enterprise value.
What you should have:
- An undergraduate degree in a relevant field such as information management, computer science, business administration, engineering, data management or analytics. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
- A minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in data management, data governance, data quality, metadata management, master/reference data management or a related discipline, including at least 5 years in a leadership role.
- Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, data modelling, data domains, master/reference data, observability and the operationalization of data management services in complex organizations.
- Experience with enterprise data management platforms and tools such as Collibra, Informatica or equivalent technologies.
- Experience working in a regulated environment with strong expectations for data controls, compliance, audit support and risk management.
- The ability to establish performance measures and use KPIs, KRIs and service metrics to guide priorities, decisions and continuous improvement.
- Strong leadership, stakeholder-management and executive-communication skills, with the ability to influence adoption across business, technology and governance communities in both official languages (French and English).
It would be great if you also had:
- A master’s degree in data management, analytics, information systems, business administration or a related discipline.
- An industry-recognized certification such as DAMA Certified Data Management Professional (CDMP), DCAM, CIPP/C or a related credential.
- Experience leading enterprise data management in financial services, a Crown corporation or another regulated, public-interest environment.
- Knowledge of mortgage loan insurance, affordable housing programs, real estate or finance.

Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
We are looking for a Supervisor, Design to support our Design and Fabrication Services Branch (DFS). The Supervisor, Design would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
Both directly and through the management of staff, the Supervisor, Design is responsible for producing, reviewing and approving designs of experimental apparatus, mechanical instrumentation and high quality, complex mechanical prototypes. The emphasis in creating designs is on meeting client requirements while efficiently utilizing available human and physical resources and methods. The position serves as the source of highest-level technical expertise within the design unit and provides input, guidance, direction and leadership to the design unit staff.
The incumbent is responsible for a range of operational management functions, as well as a full range of supervisory activities with emphasis on leadership, health and safety, performance management, promotion of innovation, and motivation of staff. He/she will provide input to the director of production for HR, finance, and operations for short and long-term planning purposes. The position works within a team environment where effective interaction with clients and DFS staff is essential. The incumbent is expected to work closely with other DFS Supervisors and Team Leaders to meet commitments.
The incumbent operates the design unit according to sound project management principles and may serve as a manager or leader of large design and fabrication project teams. The incumbent is responsible for ensuring that agreed upon project delivery commitments and technical specifications on design projects are met.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
University degree in mechanical engineering or college diploma in mechanical engineering technology (2400 hours).
Candidates with an acceptable combination of education, training and/or experience may also be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Extensive* experience and expert knowledge in the application of methodology, principles and technologies in the subject matter area, including the planning, design, fabrication, assembly, modification, Quality Management Systems, processes, machines and tools;
- Experience in coordinating activities in a facility or technical service delivery setting including scheduling of resources and of equipment operation and maintenance, training and oversight of laboratory users, and purchasing and inventory control;
- Significant** experience leading and supervising people in a production environment;
- Significant** experience in managing complex, multi-faceted, cross-functional projects and teams, and applying project management methodologies;
- Significant** experience in finance, HR, procurement and other management related principles, policies and procedures;
- Experience in client relationship management and change management;
- Ability to communicate effectively and concisely both orally and in writing with staff and clients in both official languages;
- Asset: Experience in research and development environment. (i.e. change leadership, training & development, coaching, motivation).
*Extensive is defined as 7 years or more **Significant is defined as 2 to 6 years
Condition of employment
Secret Clearance
A thorough security clearance process will be applied.
For a Secret Clearance, verification of background information over a period of 10 years is required. Individuals must have lived in Canada for a sufficient period of time to enable the security screening process.
Language requirements
Bilingual Imperative CBC/CBC
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Knowledge in the application of design methods, principles and technologies for the fabrication, modifications and repair of scientific equipment and installations or facilities, including, fabrication methods, additive manufacturing, composites, materials selection, finishing processes and assembly techniques;
- Ability in managing complex, multi-faceted, cross-functional projects and teams, and applying project management methodologies;
- Knowledge of health and safety programs such as COSH and ability to implement a hazard prevention program;
- Knowledge of NRC’s finance, procurement and other management related policies and procedures.
Behavioural competencies
- Supervisor - Client focus (Level 3)
- Supervisor - Communication (Level 3)
- Supervisor - Developing others (Level 2)
- Supervisor - Results orientation (Level 4)
- Supervisor - Self-knowing and self-development (Level 3)
- Supervisor - Teamwork (Level 4)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile: Supervisor
View all competency profiles
Compensation
From $99,281 to $117,859 per annum.
In addition, the incumbent will receive the Bilingualism Bonus of $800 per year.
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
Notes
