2475367.text:
The role
We are looking for an Airworthiness Engineer to join our Aerospace Research Centre and support aircraft modifications and research integrations across the Flight Research Laboratory (FRL) fleet, including newly introduced platforms such as the Global 6500. You would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The Flight Research Laboratory (FRL) operates a small fleet of research aircraft under experimental flight permits. These aircraft are heavily-modified in-house to meet the flight research needs of partners and clients in the Canadian aerospace sector. Ongoing airworthiness of the aircraft is ensured through an internally-driven compliance process. The incumbent will be expected to use their engineering expertise to provide advice on the safety and risks associated with the design, development, and installation of equipment and any accompanying aircraft modifications required for flight research projects. They will serve as an in-house resource during project development to identify and communicate airworthiness issues to other support personnel, and ensure that proposed aircraft installations meet NRC/FRL and Transport Canada airworthiness requirements.
The incumbent will be expected to interact with a multi-disciplinary team of researchers, test pilots, engineers, designers, fabrication and aircraft maintenance personnel.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
- Bachelor's degree in aeronautical or mechanical engineering; and
- Successful completion of the Transport Canada Aircraft Certification Specialty Course, or equivalent.
A Master’s degree in a related field would be considered an asset.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Minimum of 15 years of aircraft modification-related engineering experience supporting major modification design for experimental installations, special-mission, or research-integration programs;
- Experience providing technical advice and recommendations to management and/or clients on engineering-related issues;
- Significant experience in the certification of aeronautical products or modifications to aeronautical products in accordance with the Canadian Aviation Regulations, or another regulatory system; and
- Experience managing complex technical projects involving multi-disciplinary teams in a matrix environment.
Assets :
- Experience identifying and advising on airworthiness or certification challenges for new or non-standard technologies;
- Experience working with transport category (FAR 25/CAR 525) aircraft;
- Qualifications equivalent to a Transport Canada Design Approval Representative.
Condition of employment
- Secret clearance
A thorough security clearance process will be applied.
For a Secret Clearance, verification of background information over a period of 10 years is required. Individuals must have lived in Canada for a sufficient period of time to enable the security screening process.
- Must be able to obtain and maintain a Restricted Area Identity Card (RAIC) from the Ottawa Airport Pass Control Office;
- Working conditions: This position requires work to be performed on and around aircraft, and candidates must be physically able to perform the duties of this position. These duties include: working from elevated platforms, lifting moderate weights, and wearing personal protective equipment such as a respirator and safety goggles. The candidate is expected to work with chemicals and materials commonly found in the aircraft industry;
- Eligibility for membership as a Professional Engineer in Ontario (PEO);
- Ability to fly as a member of FRL aircraft crew; and
- Domestic and international travel will be required, with the possibility of extended stays.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Knowledge in one or more of aerospace structures/stress/loads, powerplant & emissions, hydro-mechanical systems, occupant safety & environmental systems, and/or aircraft integration & safety assessment;
- Extensive knowledge of the Canadian Aviation regulatory system, including Canadian Aviation Regulations (CARs) and design standards (AWM); familiarity with airworthiness approaches for flight-test and experimental aircraft configurations;
- Demonstrated ability to lead and coordinate multi-disciplinary teams through all phases of aircraft modification or integration projects; and
- Knowledge of project management concepts and principles.
Behavioural competencies
- Technology extension - Results orientation (Level 3)
- Technology extension - Conceptual and analytical ability (Level 3)
- Technology extension - Teamwork (Level 3)
- Technology extension - Client focus (Level 2)
- Technology extension - Communication (Level 3)
- Research - Continuous professional learning (Level 2)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profiles: Research ; Technology Extension
View all competency profiles
Compensation
The intent of this hiring action is to staff this position at the RCO-3/RCO-4 level, which is a mid-career level position with a salary range of $119,688 to $168,192 .
NOTE: Please note that the full RO/RCO salary scale has five levels. Salary determination will be based on a review of the candidate’s expertise, outcomes and impacts of their previous work experience relative to the requirements of the level. As such, the initial salary could be within another level of the RO/RCO salary scale (i.e. above or below the intended level for this position).
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.

Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. Reference number: RF-17248
About CSE
The Communications Security Establishment (CSE) is Canada’s agency responsible for foreign signals intelligence, cyber operations and cyber security. Learn more about our mission .
CSE is committed to fostering a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion. This isn’t just an ideal, it’s crucial to our mission. Find out about our workplace culture , including our diversity and inclusion initiatives.
Become part of our team and you’ll understand why CSE is the most important organization you’ve never heard of .
Job summary
The Tutte Institute for Mathematics and Computing (TIMC) is a government research institute housed within CSE. TIMC ’s mission is to conduct strategic research that has an impact on the most important scientific challenges faced by the Canadian security and intelligence community and its international partners. TIMC delivers on this mission through a research program in foundational mathematics and computer science, with concentrations in cryptology and machine learning research.
TIMC is seeking highly qualified researchers to contribute to the Mathematical Foundations of Cryptography research area
Strategic Researchers at TIMC work on a variety of complex challenges and they draw on a variety of tools including deep mathematical theory and cutting-edge computational resources. Success in this role requires adaptability, creativity, and a passion for advancing knowledge.
Key Responsibilities:
- Conduct high-quality research toward TIMC research focus topics.
- Identify research problems and projects in alignment with CSE’s research strategy.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues at TIMC, across CSE, and with external partners.
- Disseminate research results through technical reports, presentations, peer-reviewed publications, and software contributions.
- Maintain situational awareness in research developments and provide advice and guidance to clients and decision-makers.
Salary
To find out more about our salary scale, vacation allowances and benefits (health, dental and pension plans, etc.), visit the Compensation page on our website.
Area of selection
Open to Canadian citizens.
Location
The majority of our jobs are in Ottawa, Ontario. CSE has two accessible facilities . Flexible work arrangements, including telework for a portion of the work week, may be possible.
Conditions of employment
A valid Enhanced Top Secret (ETS) security clearance is a condition of employment that must be met before an offer can be made.
More information about our hiring process and security page can be found on our website.
Essential qualifications
In order to be considered, your cover letter must clearly explain how you meet the following education and experience requirements.
Education
You must have either one of the following:
- A MSc in mathematics, statistics, computer science or a related field, with at least eight (8) years of post-MSc research experience.
- A PhD in mathematics, statistics, computer science or a relevant field, with at least three (3) years of post-PhD research experience.
Note: The educational program must be recognized in Canada, and you must be able to provide proof of education credentials.
Experience
- Conducting original research with tangible impact in cryptography, quantum information theory, combinatorics, algebra, number theory or a relevant scientific field demonstrated by sustained contributions of publication, presentation and/or code-release. Examples include papers in peer-reviewed journals and proceedings, presentations at top conferences, and widely recognized contributions to software projects.
- Designing, developing, implementing, and/or evaluating novel cryptanalytic methods, computational algorithms, or practical cryptologic applications.
- Leading research teams and/or supervising junior researchers, post-docs or graduate students.
- Establishing and executing research programs, demonstrated, for example, by successful grant applications, contributing to strategic planning, and achieving key project milestones.
Official language requirements
Various language profiles, including English Essential and Bilingual Imperative (CBC/CBC)
- English essential means that the position is unilingual English.
- Bilingual means that knowledge of both official languages (English and French) is required for the position.
- CBC/CBC represent the proficiency level you must demonstrate in each of the language skills (reading, writing and oral interaction) for the bilingual position. For bilingual positions, second language evaluations will be offered to candidates who don’t have valid language test results issued by the Government of Canada.
Find out more about the language requirements of positions.
Competencies
The following technical, behavioural and leadership competencies will be assessed at a later date. You do not need to include information about them in your application.
Technical competencies
- Knowledge and Application of a Field of Mathematics, Computer Science, Physics or Engineering
- Cryptography and Cryptanalysis
- Application Development
- Problem Formulation and Response
Behavioural competencies
- Accountability/Autonomy
- Interactive Communication
- Working in a Team
Leadership competencies
- Achieving Results
- Change and Innovation
- Collaboration
Assets
Assets are “nice-to-have” expertise and skills we’re interested in.
Please demonstrate on your application if you meet or possess the asset experience listed below.
Asset competenciesh3>
The following asset technical, behavioural and leadership competencies will be assessed at a later date. You do not need to include information about them in your application.
Asset technical competencies
Machine Learning
Operational requirements
Overtime and standby duty may be required.
How to apply
You may submit your candidacy online by selecting “Apply” at the bottom of this page.
Note: Be prepared to provide two (2) letters of reference regarding your research experience upon request.
If you cannot apply online or have a disability preventing you from applying online, please inform us by email at careers-carrieres@cse-cst.gc.ca Important information
We ask you to not discuss your application with others (including on social media) besides your partner, or close family members - who should also be reminded about the need to be discreet.
Assessments of candidates are conducted in the official language of their choice.
We are committed to a diverse and representative workforce and an open and inclusive work environment; as such we encourage candidates to self-declare as members of the following designated employment equity groups : women; Indigenous peoples, including First Nations who are status, or registered and non-status, or non-registered, Inuit and Métis; persons with disabilities, including people with a mental health condition and neurodivergent people; and persons from racial or ethnic groups.
Please note the Employment Equity Act , which is under review, uses the terminology Aboriginal peoples and visible minorities.
CSE offers an assessment process that will accommodate any reasonable measures you require to be assessed in a fair and equitable manner. Those measures are available to all candidates during our processes. Information you provide will be addressed confidentially.
The level of competence demonstrated in the various assessments will be used to determine your qualifications for the UNMA 09, UNMA 10 or UNMA 11 level.
All communications with CSE relating to this process, including email messages and telephone conversations, may be used in the assessment of qualifications.
The intent of this process is to fill vacant positions at CSE. The process may also be used to establish a pool of qualified candidates which could be used to staff similar or identical positions with various tenures.
Due to the nature of CSE’s mandate certain roles may expose employees to content that is difficult to process. Mental health is a priority at CSE and if any personnel feel they require assistance to preserve their mental wellbeing, they have access to services, tools and other resources to help them in both their personal and professional lives.
Please note that in an effort to maintain balance between employee development and business needs, candidates who are hired at CSE must remain in their substantive position for a minimum of twelve (12) months subject to operational requirements.
We thank you for your interest in CSE. However, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

Job Summary
The Canadian Security Intelligence Service (CSIS) is looking for dedicated individuals to fill the position of Communications Analyst in its various regional offices across Canada. Candidates must possess a high level of initiative, motivation and discretion.
This position will be of interest to individuals who are able to translate from one or more foreign languages identified below into French or English and who are able to work effectively as part of a team. As a Communications Analyst, you will read or listen to foreign language material, determine its relevance and importance as well as produce translations and draft reports based on the intelligence value in the material, to generate leads for investigations.
Under the direction of a Team Leader, you will be responsible for assessing, identifying oral and written communications, collaborate with counterparts and stakeholders, and provide advice to management. This requires the ability to conduct extensive research and analysis on various subjects (social, economic, geopolitical and ethno-cultural), and be able to draw on your understanding of the culture concerned. - Russian
- Punjabi
- Urdu
- Hindi
- Spanish

Undergraduate degree and two (2) years of experience*

2475515.text:
The Royal Canadian Mint (the Mint) is hiring a Senior Manager, Privacy and Access to Information who can thrive in a dynamic and inclusive environment.
Reporting to the Senior Director, Regulatory and Corporate Affairs, the Senior Manager, Privacy and Access to Information is responsible for ensuring the Mint’s management of the Privacy, Access to Information, CASL and Parliamentary questions programs include key program design and statutory and regulatory as applicable. The Senior Manager will lead and assign work under this portfolio to the ATIP team.
Your Responsibilities:
- Promote and support the mandate of the ATIP office and the Mint’s Privacy Program which includes protecting the Mint’s directors, officers and employees from the serious adverse consequences of non-compliance with privacy legislation (including regulatory sanction and damage to reputation), CASL and Access to Information legislation.
- Responsible for the day-to-day management of access to information, CASL, Parliamentary Questions and privacy-related programs throughout the Mint to foster a culture of privacy by leading and supporting the integration of privacy considerations in organizational activities and decisions, developing of tools and resources, and delivering employee training awareness/building awareness.
- Develop the Mint’s privacy policy governance framework to support the Mint’s mission and to ensure that corporate privacy policies and practices align with legislative requirements and best practices.
- Manage two ATIP team members to ensure the accuracy and timeliness of Access and Privacy Act access responses and maintenance of accurate records and compliance with all reporting requirements under the applicable legislation.
- Provide technical and professional advisory and compliance services on all aspects of privacy and privacy-related queries for the organization, including Privacy Impact Assessments, procurement processes, and the oversight of consultants as needed.
- Develop annual work plans to prioritize and implement privacy deliverables aligned with internal stakeholders’ and organizational programs and/or initiatives.
- Act as the privacy representative on senior committees as required to promote best practices and excellent customer service on privacy-related matters including on the AI Council
- Responsible for liaison with external stakeholders, the Treasury Board Secretariat and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner, including for the resolution of complaints.
- Manage the ATIP Office’s responsibilities and actions for the privacy incident/breach response process (investigation, assessment, reporting, mitigation/prevention oversight, etc.)
- Support the ATIP Office’s operational work as required by providing high-level expertise on ATIP request files.
This position offers a hybrid work arrangement, requiring on-site presence at our Ottawa location three to five days per week, depending on meeting requirements and other activities.
This selection process may also qualify you for other positions with similar requirements and qualifications.
Qualifications:
Languages Requirements:
Proficiency in both official languages (English & French) is required at the time of hire. The linguistic profile for this position is:
- Reading Comprehension : C Advanced
- Written Expression : B Intermediate
- Oral Proficiency : C Advanced
If no qualified candidate fully meets the linguistic profile of the position, other bilingual profiles may be considered, in accordance with the Mint’s Staffing Policy.
Education & Designation:
- University Degree in related field
- Professional privacy certification (CIPP/C) or commensurate designation.
Experience:
- Minimum of 10 years of related business experience
- Minimum of 7 years of progressive management experience.
Additional Qualifications:
- Advanced knowledge of Canadian and international privacy legislation, familiarity with the Access to Information Act, and excellent knowledge of TBS policies, directives and privacy best practices as they apply to Crown corporations.
- Ability to interpret laws, regulations and legal advice.
- Able to solicit and keep the goodwill and cooperation of a wide range of individuals, including operational staff and senior management, while providing advice, guidance and strategic influencing on complex privacy compliance issues.
- Proficient at written and verbal communications, in particular, the development of succinct and useful reporting on compliance issues for a senior management audience.
- Sound judgment and a strong practical approach to considering courses of action.
- The flexibility to balance multiple accountabilities with competing priorities; and
- The ability to work independently and to meet tight deadlines, and to quickly adapt to unforeseen circumstances, changes in priorities and initiatives.
Why the Mint?
At the Mint, you will collaborate with a diverse group of people and be a part of an iconic Canadian organization. Your safety and wellbeing are our top priority. We offer outstanding pay and total rewards for you and your family and you will be supported to continuously learn throughout your career.
The Mint is committed to building an inclusive workforce that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We value diversity and aim to provide an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment, selection and onboarding process to ensure that each candidate is treated respectfully.
If you need accommodation at any point in the application or interview process, please let us know. We are committed to being an inclusive employer. For a confidential inquiry, simply email us directly at ee@mint.ca to make arrangements.
What to Expect
In order to be considered for an interview, please clearly demonstrate on your application how you meet the education and experience qualifications. The additional qualifications may be assessed through interviews, exams, reference checks, etc. If successful, you will be required to complete a background check facilitated by the Mint in order to obtain a security clearance.
Ready to mint your career?
Please forward your resume to careers@mint.ca by October 22, 2026. We look forward to receiving your application!

2475516.text:
The Royal Canadian Mint (the Mint) is hiring an experienced Legal Counsel with 8-10 years experience who can thrive in a dynamic and inclusive environment.
Reporting to the Director & Senior Legal Counsel, Legal Services, the Legal Counsel is responsible for providing legal advisory services across the Mint’s commercial and operational activities, with a particular focus on regulatory compliance, anti-money laundering and anti-terrorist financing (AML/ATF), privacy and corporate/commercial matters. The role also includes contract drafting and negotiation, procurement and other matters supporting the Mint’s operations.
This is a broad in-house role offering the opportunity to work on sophisticated commercial transactions and evolving regulatory issues within a unique Canadian organization.
Your Responsibilities:
- Provide practical legal advice across corporate/commercial, procurement, employment, intellectual property, privacy, AML/ATF and regulatory compliance matters.
- Draft, review and negotiate contracts, agreements, procurement documents, policies and other legal instruments.
- Identify legal risks, advise on compliance obligations and recommend practical mitigation strategies.
- Support internal stakeholders through timely, business-oriented legal advice and file management.
- Monitor legal and regulatory developments and support updates to policies, templates and practices.
- Collaborate with business units and external counsel to support organizational objectives while managing legal risk.
This position offers a hybrid work arrangement, requiring on-site presence at our Ottawa location three to five days per week, depending on meeting requirements and other activities.
Qualifications:
Languages Requirements:
Proficiency in both official languages (English and French) is required at the time of hire. The linguistic profile for this position is:
- Reading Comprehension : C Advanced
- Written Expression : B Intermediate
- Oral Proficiency : C Advanced
If no qualified candidate fully meets the required levels, other candidate language profiles may be considered in accordance with the Mint’s Staffing Policy.
Education & Designation:
- University degree in law from a recognized university in Canada.
- Member in good standing of the Bar of one of the provinces or territories of Canada.
Experience:
- A minimum of 8–10 years of experience in the practice of law, with demonstrated expertise in regulatory compliance and/or corporate/commercial law, and meaningful experience in one or more of the following areas: AML/ATF, privacy, contract drafting and negotiation, procurement or other regulated business activities.
Additional Qualifications:
- Strong knowledge of corporate/commercial law, contract law, regulatory compliance, and the legal principles applicable to the Mint’s business and operational activities, with experience in public procurement law and related trade agreements considered an asset.
- Demonstrated ability to draft, review, negotiate and advise on contracts, agreements, procurement documents, policies, legal opinions, briefing notes and other legal instruments.
- Working knowledge of labour and employment, intellectual property, privacy, AML/ATF, legislative, policy and other legal advisory matters relevant to Legal Services.
- Strong analytical, research, problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to identify legal issues, assess risks and provide practical, business-oriented advice and mitigation strategies.
- Ability to synthesize legal, policy, business and operational information and provide clear oral and written advice that balances legal requirements, client objectives, organizational interests and risk management considerations.
- Ability to manage client relationships, competing priorities and workload to ensure timely, effective and high-quality delivery of legal services
- Ability to collaborate with, guide and coordinate the work of less experienced counsel, Legal Researcher & Technician, articling students and legal support staff, as required.
- Experience advising a Crown corporation, government entity or regulated organization is considered an asset.
Salary Range: Salaries are based on qualifications and experience and typically range from $112,800 to $155,000.
Performance Incentive: Employees in this role may be eligible for an individual performance bonus of up to 10% with an additional corporate bonus based on their annual base salary .
Why the Mint?
At the Mint, you will collaborate with a diverse group of people and be a part of an iconic Canadian organization. Your safety and wellbeing are our top priority. We offer outstanding pay and total rewards for you and your family and you will be supported to continuously learn throughout your career.
The Mint is committed to building an inclusive workforce that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We value diversity and aim to provide an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment, selection and onboarding process to ensure that each candidate is treated respectfully.
If you need accommodation at any point in the application or interview process, please let us know. For a confidential inquiry, simply email us directly at ee@mint.ca to make arrangements.
What to Expect
In order to be considered for an interview, please clearly demonstrate on your application how you meet the education and experience qualifications. The additional qualifications may be assessed through interviews, exams, reference checks, etc. If successful, you will be required to complete a background check facilitated by the Mint in order to obtain a security clearance.
Ready to mint your career?
Please forward your resume to careers@mint.ca by November 8, 2026. We look forward to receiving your application!

2475666.text: Build Projects That Matter. Support construction excellence and Strengthen Canada. Are you a construction professional who thrives in dynamic project environments and enjoys working closely with contractors, consultants, and clients to bring projects to life? Do you excel at solving challenges, building strong relationships, and ensuring projects are delivered safely, efficiently, and to the highest standards? If so, we'd love to hear from you. As a Coordinator, Construction Services, you'll play a key role in administering construction contracts and supporting the successful delivery of infrastructure projects that directly support the Canadian Armed Forces. You'll be the connection between contractors, consultants, Client-Partners, and project teams, helping to manage risks, resolve issues, and keep projects moving forward from start to finish. By becoming a team member of a trusted partner of the Government of Canada and the Canadian construction industry since 1951, you will have the opportunity to deliver infrastructure and environmental solutions to support Canada’s troops and the defence of the Country. DCC is proud to be the first federal, and only government organization recognized as a Gold Seal Employer under the Canadian Construction Association’s Construction Management Certification Program and proof of our commitment to excellence and professional development. What You'll Do Oversee Construction Contracts You'll administer construction, professional service, and service contracts throughout project delivery, ensuring compliance with contract requirements, quality standards, and project objectives. From project startup to closeout, you'll help drive successful project outcomes. Be the Trusted Point of Contact Client-Partners, contractors, and consultants will rely on you for guidance and solutions. You'll review progress claims, coordinate contract changes, address project risks, and help resolve day-to-day contract and construction issues. Coordinate People & Keep Work Moving You'll work closely with site teams, contractors, consultants, and stakeholders to ensure activities remain aligned, communication flows effectively, and projects stay on track. When challenges arise, you'll collaborate with the right people to find practical solutions. Champion Quality, Safety & Compliance You'll help ensure work meets contractual, quality, health and safety, environmental, and industrial security requirements. Through regular site engagement and contract oversight, you'll contribute to safe and successful construction delivery. Additional Responsibilities • Manage contract financials and change orders. • Coordinate consultant reviews and third-party testing activities. • Maintain project records, reports, and site documentation. • Support business development initiatives and stakeholder engagement. • Perform other duties as required. Working Environment • Primarily construction site-based, with regular interaction with contractors and project stakeholders. • Some work takes place in a typical office environment with occasional travel. • Personal protective equipment (PPE) is required when working on active construction sites. What You’ll Bring Education & Experience Minimum Requirements • College diploma in Engineering, Applied Science, Construction Management, or a related field • Four (4) years of related construction or contract administration experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience Asset Qualifications • Certification in a related field (such as Certified Engineering Technologist) Knowledge & Skills • Construction methods, materials, and industry best practices • Contract, project, and risk management principles • Health and safety legislation and requirements • Ability to interpret drawings, plans, specifications, and contract documents • Strong communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills • Proficiency with common software applications and project documentation tools What You’ll Get We don’t just offer a job — we offer one of the best overall benefits packages in the market, valued at 25–30% of your salary, plus long-term career growth. Health & Wellness • 100% employer-paid health, dental, and sick leave • $400 annual wellness allowance • $2,500 for mental health services + $2,500 paramedical • Virtual healthcare and a $750 Health Spending Account Home & Family • Life, accident, and short-term disability insurance • Enhanced Employee & Family Assistance Program • Maternity & parental leave top-up (93% for up to 37 weeks) • Flexible work options + $400 home office allowance every 2 years Time & Future • Public service pension plan • Generous vacation and leave packages along with deluxe travel benefit plans About Wainwright Just two hours east of Edmonton, Wainwright offers both urban amenities and the family-oriented country lifestyle of the beautiful Battle River Valley. Known as the “Buffalo Capital of Canada,” it is a strong vibrant community of over 6,700 people, 500 of whom are at Camp Wainwright. Rich with health, educational, and recreational facilities, Wainwright offers a well-rounded quality of life, as well as a full slate of social and cultural facilities and events. You will find yourself enjoying the state-of-the-art Peace Memorial Multiplex, with its twin hockey rinks, a walking track and climbing wall, as well as the Communiplex, which has a pool, weight training facilities, dance studio, and much more. Wainwright also maintains outdoor soccer fields, baseball diamonds, tennis courts, a quality 18-hole golf course, and an extensive network of walking trails. Plus, Wainwright is also about 10-20 minutes from the Arm Lake, Clear Lake, and the Riverdale Park, where residents can camp, ride horses, canoe and kayak, fish, and sail. Ready to make an impact? Apply now and help deliver a variety of infrastructure projects that support Canada’s Defence and Security.

2475678.text:
Join Defence Construction Canada (DCC) in Greenwood, NS, and play a vital role in supporting Canada’s National Defence! As a Federal Crown corporation with over 70 years of contribution to national defence, DCC is renowned for its innovative and cost-effective solutions in contracting, construction management, and infrastructure services.
What you bring
You are a good fit if you have experience with:
- Managing and administering construction and professional service contracts
- Coordinating day‑to‑day contract issues and supporting schedule control
- Liaising with Client‑Partners on contract changes, risks and quality expectations
- Monitoring site activities and ensuring compliance with health, safety and environmental requirements
- Applying project, contract and risk management principles in a construction setting
The Coordinator, Construction Services, manages and administers medium-complexity construction, professional services and service contracts during construction to ensure compliance with contract requirements. The incumbent engages in daily discussions and negotiations with contractors, consultants and the Client-Partners about quality of work, interpretation of contract documents, scope changes, progress claim reviews and other issues. The incumbent addresses contract management risks within delegated authority, complies with service line requirements, and integrates activities with site teams and other service lines.
KEY AND PERIODIC ACTIVITIES The duties and responsibilities listed below are representative but not all-inclusive: Primary
- Manage and administer contracts to ensure compliance with contractual requirements and quality specifications
- Coordinate and solve day-to-day contractual problems
- Monitor and control schedules
- Liaise with Client-Partner representatives (e.g. on contract-related problems and risks, negotiate and issue change orders)
- Maintain site activity records (e.g. photos, activity reports)
- Liaise with other service lines and site teams, as required
- Develop and maintain effective relationships within DCC, and with industry, the Client Partners and/or stakeholders
- Ensure quality standards are met, in line with corporate and Client-Partner expectations
- Manage contract risks
Other
- Manage contract financials
- Coordinate consultant construction review and third-party testing
- Ensure health and safety, industrial security and environmental compliance
- Support and/or lead business development activities
- Other duties as assigned
SKILLS General and Specific Knowledge
- Best practices, methods, trends and legislation in construction
- Construction, products and materials
- Project, contract and risk management principles
- Health and safety management
Formal Education and/or Certification(s) and Experience
- Minimum: college diploma in engineering, applied science or related field with four years’ relevant experience, or the equivalent
- Preferred: certification in applicable field (e.g. Certified Engineering Technologist)
Abilities
- Use applicable computer software and operating systems
- Interpret drawings and specifications
- Apply project, contract and risk management techniques to construction and consultant contracts
DEVELOPMENT AND LEADERSHIP
- Provide functional advice and guidance to employees and to Client-Partners
WORKING CONDITIONS
- Typical construction site environment; incumbent is required to wear basic safety equipment
- Some work may be in a typical office environment with occasional travel
Check out your benefits Working with us offers excellent opportunities for growth and advancement—and entitles you to one of the job market’s best benefits packages valued at between 25 and 30% of your salary.
Your package includes:
Health and Wellness
- 100% employer-paid annual sick leave, and health and dental premiums
- $400 wellness allowance to help cover expenses such as a gym membership
- $2,500 for mental health services on top of regular $2,500 paramedical coverage
- Telus Virtual Health Care and $750 Health Care Spending Account for some expenses not covered under provincial plans
Home and Family
- Life, accidental-death, and short-term disability insurance
- Enhanced inConfidence employee and family assistance program
- Maternity and parental leave top-up plan to 93% of regular gross earnings for up to 37 weeks
- Flexible workplace options, including $400 allowance every two years, to support working from home
Leave and Retirement
- Public-service pension
- Comprehensive vacation and other paid-leave plans, along with enhanced travel benefits coverage
You have not already discovered the beauty of the Annapolis Valley? Here are some reasons to consider relocation to Greenwood and the Surrounding Annapolis Valley…
Located in the heart of Nova Scotia’s Annapolis Valley is 14 Wing Greenwood, the largest air force base on the east coast of Canada. The Wing’s Aurora crews conduct sovereignty and surveillance missions over the Atlantic Ocean routinely, while Search and Rescue (SAR) capabilities are standing by year-round. The valley region includes Canada’s earliest historic sites and delivers a unique rural lifestyle just minutes from the Bay of Fundy, scenic rivers, lakes, and the Atlantic coastline. The climate and terrain offer year-round outdoor activities including camping, kayaking, hiking, mountain biking, and skiing. Sheltered by the North and South Mountains, the Annapolis Valley is known for rich agriculture and boasts a vibrant farm to table food movement, outstanding dining, festivals, numerous vineyards, and micro-breweries. Greenwood is within driving distance to nine (9) Universities and Community Colleges including Acadia University, one of Canada’s top 5 undergraduate schools.
This position may also offer a competitive relocation package for candidates moving across the province or the country.

2475746.text:
We have an exciting opportunity in the National Service Region (NSR)!
Reporting to the Team Leader, Business Intelligence, the Business Intelligence Analyst provides intelligence services to both internal clients, as well as to the Client-Partners and external stakeholders. Among other duties, the incumbent identifies business requirements, develops analytical processes using various data sources, interprets data analysis and validates data, recommends and communicates analysis, and produces visual tools such as dashboards and reports. The incumbent also ensures these deliverables provide key information as part of visual and evidenced-based analysis to help DCC and the Department of National Defence (DND) identify data to support key decisions, measure key performance metrics and manage portfolio requirements. - Identify client business intelligence requirements, interpret, and establish viable data modelling to complete analytical and visualization tools (e.g. dashboards, reports)
- Coordinate applicable data to provide analysis and visual tools using various automated data sources and technologies
- Interpret output of completed analysis and ensure accuracy of data
- Validate data with various stakeholders, including DCC, DND and industry
- Provide advice and recommendations to key senior-level Client-Partners
- Develop and maintain effective relationships within DCC, and with industry, the Client-Partners and/or stakeholders
- Ensure quality standards are met, in line with corporate expectations
- Manage risk

- Best practices, methods, trends and legislation in real property and construction
- Database design, statistics and data sciences
- Best practices, methods, trends and legislation in business intelligence
Formal Education and/or Certification(s) and Experience Minimum: university degree in engineering, data sciences, computer science, business, mathematics, economics, statistics, management, accounting or related field with six to eight years’ relevant experience, or the equivalent Abilities
- Use computer programs to perform advanced tasks
- Use applicable computer software and operating systems
DEVELOPMENT AND LEADERSHIP Provide occasional functional advice and/or guidance to other employees, and to ClientPartners and stakeholders WORKING CONDITIONS Typical office environment with occasional travel Some work may be located on construction sites; incumbent may occasionally be required to wear basic safety equipment
Check out your benefits Working with us offers excellent opportunities for growth and advancement—and entitles you to one of the job market’s best benefits packages valued at between 25 and 30% of your salary.
Your package includes:

- 100% employer-paid annual sick leave, and health and dental premiums
- $400 wellness allowance to help cover expenses such as a gym membership
- $2,500 for mental health services on top of regular $2,500 paramedical coverage

Home and Family
- Life, accidental-death, and short-term disability insurance
- Enhanced inConfidence employee and family assistance program
- Maternity and parental leave top-up plan to 93% of regular gross earnings for up to 37 weeks
- Flexible workplace options, including $400 allowance every two years, to support working from home
Leave and Retirement
- Public-service pension
- Comprehensive vacation and other paid-leave plans, along with enhanced travel benefits coverage

2475581.text:
Company Description
The House of Commons Administration delivers outstanding services to Members of Parliament and their employees in support of parliamentary democracy. Our success is made possible by our talented and dedicated workforce. We leverage diversity in all its forms and recognize that everyone has valuable contributions to make and the potential for individual growth. If you dream of joining an organization that is small enough for you to be noticed, but big enough to provide you with a meaningful career, then we want to hear from you!
Job Description
The House of Commons’ Parliamentary Precinct Operations is currently looking to staff the Kitchen Helper position.
Food services provide various hospitality services to Parliamentarians and their employees, House Administration employees and visitors to the Hill. These services are offered by the Parliamentary Dining Room and cafeterias located in different buildings on the Hill.
Food services also provide a full catering service for a variety of functions ranging from a simple coffee service to the complexities of a banquet. We also offer Gourmet at home meals along with various gourmet market items including canapes preserves, pastries, wine and ready set bake meals.
The Kitchen Helper is responsible for working in the Food Production Facility and assisting in all food production, assembling meals, packaging and distribution for an assigned station.
The role requires that the incumbent work weekends and evenings, and at times extended hours and in multiple locations.
The purpose of this posting is to staff the position of Kitchen Helper on a seasonal/on-call/determinate basis (temporary). Hourly Rate $20.85 to $26.39
**For seasonal/on-call basis, the hours of work can vary between 15 to 35 hours. The needs are determined according to the parliamentary sessions. Work periods are from mid-September to mid-December, late January to late June. Operational requirements are interrupted during the summer months and between parliamentary sessions.
Top Reasons to Join the Food Services Team
Our dynamic and people-driven team works to deliver exceptional and quality service. In this role, you will be working in a diverse, inclusive and collaborative environment without compromising your work/life balance. You will have the unique opportunity to work in the high-quality food service spaces of our Parliamentary Precinct kitchens and the Food Production Facility. We also value and encourage training and development opportunities to develop your skills and talents.
Qualifications
Education :
- High school diploma OR an acceptable combination of education, training and relevant experience;
- Food handler’s certification.
Experience :
- Relevant experience in cafeteria and/or deli/sandwich counter in a high-volume food preparation environment;
- Experience in the preparation and plating of meals and packaging of foods;
- Experience in the application of methods, procedures and techniques to ensure food safety.
Additional Information
We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace by providing a barrier-free recruitment and selection process. If you have an accommodation request, require material in an accessible format, or need additional support with the application process, please contact Recruitment and Selection Services at HOCCareers-CarrieresCDC@parl.gc.ca .
Each bilingual position is assigned a linguistic profile that identifies the level of second language proficiency for reading comprehension, written expression and oral interaction required. The profile for this position is English or French essential. Consideration may be given to candidates with other linguistic profiles.
Priority may be given to applicants who apply early.
Qualified candidates may be considered for future vacancies for this role or for other similar and/or related roles on an indeterminate and/or fixed term basis.
Learn more about us! Visit Ourcommons.ca .
To learn about our hiring process, visit Eligibility and Selection .

2475631.text:
About the role
Join the Chief Risk Officer’s team in the Senior Specialist, Compliance and Quality Assurance position. In this role, you will provide strategic insight and independent challenge on operational risks. You will work closely with first-line teams to enhance risk practices, improve control effectiveness, strengthen risk data, analytics and reporting, and support proactive, data-driven management of operational risk.
What you’ll do:
- Provide expertise and execution in developing, implementing and continuously improving operational risk management, internal control, quality assurance and compliance frameworks and practices.
- Provide strategic advice on risk governance, risk appetite, operational direction and governance documentation, leveraging relevant industry frameworks, standards and leading practices.
- Lead objective setting, risk assessments, monitoring, testing, evaluation and reporting of key risks, controls, processes and policy/program requirements, ensuring rigor and consistency.
- Identify existing and emerging risks, control issues and improvement opportunities; recommend and monitor timely remediation actions and escalate significant concerns to senior management.
- Establish and maintain performance measures and risk indicators, analyze operational risk data to identify trends and emerging issues, and improve the quality, completeness and consistency of information used for risk monitoring and decision-making.
- Design, build and continuously improve Power BI dashboards, data models and reporting solutions that bring together information from multiple sources and translate operational risk data into clear, accessible and actionable management insights, while reducing manual reporting.
- Build strong relationships across business lines, risk teams and oversight/monitoring functions within the three lines of defence, partnering with stakeholders to understand evolving risk, data and reporting needs, and applying effective change management to build trust and engagement.
- Use strong communication, presentation and influencing skills to communicate complex results, influence decisions, lead effective committees and working groups, document and follow actions through to closure, and promote strong risk awareness and an effective risk culture.
What you should have:
- An undergraduate degree in a related field such as business administration, commerce, finance, data/analytics, or a related discipline.
- A minimum of 7 years of demonstrated experience in audit, quality assurance, compliance, risk management and/or internal control, including experience using data and analytics to support oversight, reporting or decision-making.
- Knowledge of financial and/or nonfinancial risk management policy development and oversight, including the use of risk data, metrics and indicators to monitor risk.
- A demonstrated experience designing and developing dashboards and reporting solutions, including working with data from multiple sources and translating complex data into clear management insights.
- Strong communication, presentation and influencing skills (written and verbal), including the ability to speak and write clearly and succinctly in a variety of settings and styles.
- Demonstrated negotiation, influencing and relationship-building skills.
- A sound judgment, analytical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess data quality, identify trends and patterns, and manage multiple priorities under time constraints.
It would be great if you also had:
- A professional designation in a related field including a CPA, CISA, CIA, CRM, or CRMP.
- Bilingualism (French and English).
- A certifications in Operational Risk Management, Business Continuity Management, Data Governance and/or related disciplines.

2475615.text:
About the role
Join the CRO’s Financial Risk Oversight team, in the Senior Specialist, Strategic and Reputational Risk (Financial Risk Oversight – Credit Risk) position. In this role, you will play an important role in providing risk oversight and supporting the effective management of financial risks across CMHC. Working within the Financial Risk Oversight team, you will monitor, assess, and report on enterprise-wide financial risks across areas such as Counterparty and Institutional Credit, Housing Programs and Mortgage Loan Insurance, Market Risk, Capital Investments, Liquidity, and Securitization, helping ensure alignment with CMHC’s strategic objectives.
What you'll do:
- Conduct independent oversight to ensure CMHC’s financial risk management and risk control activities are robust and effective.
- Conduct independent analysis of financial strength, credit worthiness, operational capability of program participants, vendors and other counterparties.
- Serve as a subject matter expert to identify, assess, measure, monitor and report on key financial risks to the Corporation including counterparty strength against internal risk appetite, eligibility criteria and program requirements.
- Employ a combination of quantitative and qualitative assessment techniques such as financial statement analysis; internal data analysis; use of tools, models and analytics; risk policy compliance; risk appetite development or monitoring; and build and maintain forward-looking capabilities.
- Collaborate with internal stakeholders and provide support and guidance on risk management frameworks and policies to ensure effective management of risks and controls.
- Influence strategic direction, policy setting and business decisions using tools, models, and analytics to measure financial risk exposure and build and maintain forward looking capabilities analytics and risk assessment results.
- Remain current regarding regulatory guidance and industry-leading practices related to business and financial risk management and the housing market industry.
- Influence strategic direction, policy setting and business decisions by identifying emerging issues and trends related to financial and credit risks and developing innovative solutions to complex problems.
What you should have:
- A postgraduate degree in a relevant discipline such as finance, accounting or business management.
- A minimum of five (5) years of experience in credit risk and financial risk oversight experience or related relevant experience.
- A demonstrated knowledge and expertise in utilizing risk management practices and in analyzing financial statements.
- A demonstrated expertise in some of the following areas: counterparty credit, institutional credit, rating methodologies, investments, capital markets, understanding of financial instruments, etc.
- Superior communication and presentation skills with demonstrated expertise in articulating complex concepts to various levels of stakeholders.
- A demonstrated ability to conduct analysis to support problem-solving and decision-making.
It would be great if you also had:
- A professional designation, certification and/or specific training in risk management or financial analysis (e.g., Chartered Financial Analyst, Professional/Certified Risk Manager, Financial Risk Management, Chartered Professional Accountant).
- An experience developing and maintaining stochastic projections and forward-looking capabilities to quantify risk and provide data-driven insights.
- An experience in data analytics and/or risk reporting leveraging programming capabilities like Python or R.
- Bilingualism in both official languages (English & French) would be an asset.

Company Description
The House of Commons Administration delivers outstanding services to Members of Parliament and their employees in support of parliamentary democracy. Our success is made possible by our talented and dedicated workforce. We leverage diversity in all its forms and recognize that everyone has valuable contributions to make and the potential for individual growth. If you dream of joining an organization that is small enough for you to be noticed, but big enough to provide you with a meaningful career, then we want to hear from you!
Job Description
The House of Commons’ Parliamentary Precinct Operations (PPO) is currently looking to create a pool of candidates for anticipatory staffing of the Cook and Pastry Cook positions.
Food services provide various hospitality services to Parliamentarians and their employees, House Administration employees and visitors to the Hill. These services are offered by the Parliamentary Dining Room and cafeterias located in different buildings on the Hill.
As a Cook or Pastry Cook, you will play an important role in delivering high-quality food services within the Food Production Facility and parliamentary finishing kitchens/food outlets. You will work as part of a professional culinary team to assist in the preparation of food for the main dining room, catering services for special events such as banquets, Cabinet meetings, MP receptions, Senators' and Speakers' events; and cafeterias. Both the Cook and Pastry Cook are expected to maintain high standards of food quality, presentation, sanitation, and food safety.
The Cook’s focus will be on general food preparation and cooking across a variety of culinary operations. The Pastry Cook brings specialized expertise in pastry and baking, preparing desserts and baked goods and contributing recommendations related to recipe development, baking techniques, ingredients, and product presentation.
These roles require the incumbents to work weekends and evenings, and at times extended hours and in multiple locations.
The purpose of this posting is to staff the positions on a seasonal/on-call/determinate basis (temporary). Hourly Rate ranges from $27.88 to $35.27.
**For seasonal/on-call basis, the hours of work can vary from 15 to 35 hours per week. The needs are determined according to the parliamentary sessions. Work periods are from mid-September to mid-December, and from late January to late June. Operational requirements are interrupted during the summer months and between parliamentary sessions.
Top Reasons to Join the Food Services Team:
Our dynamic and people-driven team works to deliver attractive and balanced menus. By joining our team, you will be able to participate in the creation of delicious dishes without compromising your work/life balance and working in a diverse, inclusive and collaborative environment. You will have the unique opportunity to work in the high quality food service spaces of our Parliamentary Precinct kitchens and the Food Production Facility.
Qualifications
COOK
Education :
- Official training, apprenticeship or completed culinary program OR an acceptable combination of education, training and relevant experience;
- Food handler’s certification.
Experiences :
- Minimum of three (3) years of pertinent experience in high-end and large volume food production;
- Minimum of two (2) years of experience in food preparation, modern cooking methods and presentation.
PASTRY COOK
Education:
- Official training and certification as a Pastry Cook and/or Baker, or an equivalent combination of related education, training, and work experience.
Experiences :
- Minimum of three (3) years of relevant experience in high-end and high-volume food production;
- Minimum of two (2) years of experience in food preparation, modern cooking methods, and food presentation;
- Experience preparing, producing, and presenting a wide variety of pastries and baked goods.
Asset :
- Qualifications (Red Seal or TQ5) is regarded as an asset.

It offers unmatched exposure to complex and significant legal issues, direct mentorship from Canada’s most respected jurists and the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to the development of Canadian jurisprudence. If you strive for excellence, enjoy intellectually rigorous work and are motivated to have real impact at a pivotal stage of your legal career, this role may be the perfect fit.
Intent of the process
The intent of this selection process is to hire up to 27 law clerks to support the Court’s 9 judges.
Who can apply
Persons residing in Canada, and Canadian citizens and Permanent residents abroad.
Preference will be given to veterans first, followed by Canadian citizens and permanent residents.
Learn more about preference to veterans .
General information
- Work location : In-person presence at the Supreme Court of Canada, 344 Wellington Street, Ottawa, Ontario
- Group and level : Law Clerk LP-00
- Salary : $85,440 annually; a relocation lump sum may be provided
- Duration : 1 year term appointment beginning mid August 2028
Essential qualifications
Education
- A Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) , Juris Doctor (J.D.) , Licence in Law (LL.L.) or any combination thereof from a recognized Canadian university, or an equivalent degree. Note 1 : Your degree must be completed before the start of the clerkship, though it does not need to be completed at the time you apply. Note 2 : Not all law societies recognize law clerk experience toward articling requirements. You are responsible for verifying eligibility with the appropriate law society. Accordingly, law clerks must be able to devote their full time and attention to their duties and may not take time off during the term to attend bar admission courses or examinations.
- For legal degrees obtained outside Canada , applicants must consult Foreign Credential Validation against Canadian Standards and provide proof that their foreign credentials are comparable to Canadian Standards at the time of submitting their application.
Experience
- Experience in researching and analyzing Canadian legal matters
Competencies
- Ability to communicate effectively in writing
- Ability to work collaboratively and maintain effective working relationships
- Ability to work effectively under pressure
Asset qualifications
- Membership in a bar
- Academic excellence at law school
- Receipt of academic honours or distinctions in law studies, such as placement on the Dean’s List, graduation with honours or an award recognizing academic achievement
- Law-related graduate studies
- Prior clerkship experience
- Publications
- Experience in one or more of the following fields of law: Criminal Law Administrative Law Aboriginal Law Constitutional Law Private Law Quebec Civil Law
Language requirements
- English essential
- French essential
- Bilingual imperative - BBB/BBB
Conditions of employment
- Secret security clearance
Operational requirements
- Willingness and ability to work extended hours, including outside core hours and overtime on short notice.
Equity, diversity and inclusion – Self-declaration
The Public Service of Canada is committed to building a skilled and diverse workforce reflective of the Canadians we serve. The Court encourages applicants to self-declare if they belong to any of the designated groups under the Employment Equity Act, S.C. 1995, c. 44 . Applicants may do so in the Application Form.
Equity, diversity and inclusion – Our commitment
The Court is committed to having inclusive, barrier-free selection processes and work environments. If you are contacted about a job opportunity or interview, you should advise the Court in a timely manner of any accommodation measures you require in order to participate fairly and equitably. Please send all accommodation requests to the Law Clerk Program by email: lcp-paj@scc-csc .ca. Information received about accommodation measures will be treated confidentially.
How to apply
Applications for the 2028-2029 Law Clerk Program must be submitted online and received no later than January 7, 2027, at 11:59 pm (Pacific Time) . Your application will be considered complete only once all required materials have been received by the Court.
- 2028‐2029 Law Clerk Program Application
- 2028-2029 Law Clerk Program Reference
Required application materials
- Completed PDF Application Form You must download, save and open the Application Form using a PDF reader. Court communications will be conducted by email and telephone. In your Application Form, you must provide a daytime telephone number where you can be reached or where a message can be left.
- Cover letter Your cover letter must: Be addressed to the Honourable Justices. Explain why you would be an excellent candidate for a law clerk position at the Court by providing, among other things, specific examples that demonstrate: Your experience researching and analyzing Canadian legal issues; and How you meet the competencies stated above. In your Application Form, identify any experience or activities you expect to undertake between the date of your application and the start of a potential clerkship with the Court. If you submit your cover letter in both official languages, you must include both versions in a single document.
- Curriculum vitae If you submit your curriculum vitae in both official languages, you must include both versions in a single document.
- Official law school transcript Official transcripts must be sent directly by the university: By email : lcp-paj@scc-csc.ca By mail : Law Clerk Program Supreme Court of Canada 344 Wellington Street Ottawa, ON K1A 0J1 Note : Secure digital transcripts issued directly by Electronic Transcript Services (secure online platforms that enable law schools to issue official academic documents) are accepted and should be submitted by email to lcp-paj@scc-csc.ca .
- Writing samples You must submit 2 writing samples. Requirements: Each sample must be between 5 and 10 pages in length. Your samples must be relevant to the work of the Court. Your samples must be written solely by you. All pages must be numbered and include your name. New this year , you must provide a summary of a maximum of 80 words for each writing sample in the Application Form, in the same language as the sample. If you are proficient in both official languages, you must submit separate English and French writing samples. Factums prepared for court proceedings or moot court competitions will not be accepted.
- Letters of reference You must provide 4 letters of reference. Requirements: Your letters of reference may be submitted with the application or sent directly by your referees through the 2028-2029 Law Clerk Program Reference online form. One of your 4 letters may be from the Dean of the faculty where you obtained your law degree. A Dean’s letter is optional. Collectively, your letters must provide specific examples demonstrating how you meet the competencies stated above. Your referees should address the competencies they have directly observed in your work, studies or activities. Your letters of reference must be addressed to the Honourable Justices and signed by your referees. Wherever possible, your letters of reference should be printed on official institutional letterhead.
Naming convention
New this year , to ensure the proper processing of applications, all submitted documents, including the completed Application Form, cover letter, curriculum vitae, transcripts, writing samples and letters of reference, must follow the naming convention set out in the table below. Adhering to this convention helps prevent technical issues and allows our systems to accurately identify, sort and process your application materials throughout the selection process.
Requirements:
- Start each file name with the document number (01, 02, 03, etc.) specified in the naming convention below.
- Follow the number with your LAST NAME in uppercase letters, then your first name.
- Do not use commas in file names.
- Use the exact document title provided in the naming convention. If you wish to add details to better identify a document, place the additional information in parentheses at the end of the file name.
- Use only the short hyphen (-) to separate elements of the file name, rather than the longer dash (–) that may be automatically inserted by AI tools or certain software programs.
- When requesting letters of reference, provide your referees with the required document title and ask them to use it when naming their file.
Documents Naming convention For example, if Alex Smith applies, the documents are named as follows:
Application Form 01 LASTNAME FirstName - Application Form 01 SMITH Alex - Application Form
Cover letter 02 LASTNAME FirstName - Cover Letter 02 SMITH Alex - Cover Letter
Curriculum vitae 03 LASTNAME FirstName - CV 03 SMITH Alex - CV
Signed letters of reference 04 LASTNAME FirstName - Reference - Referee’s last name 04 SMITH Alex - Reference – Johnston (Judge)
Copies of transcripts 05 LASTNAME FirstName - Transcript 2 – non official; Transcript 3; etc., if there is more than one transcript. Do not use Transcript 1, as it is reserved for the official law school transcript. Transcript 2 is used for the non-official law school transcripts. 05 SMITH Alex - Transcript 2 – non official (Ottawa University) 05 SMITH Alex - Transcript 3 (Toronto University) 05 SMITH Alex - Transcript 4 (Calgary University)
Writing samples 06 LASTNAME FirstName - Writing Sample 1 06 LASTNAME FirstName - Writing Sample 2 06 SMITH Alex - Writing Sample 1 (Powers of administrative tribunals) 06 SMITH Alex - Writing Sample 2 (1459 QCC)
You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete and that all materials, including the 4 letters of reference, have been received by January 7, 2027 . Incomplete applications will not be considered.
We thank all applicants for their interest in the Program. Only applicants selected for an interview will be contacted. Interviews will be conducted by the judges of the Court via MS Teams during the week of February 22, 2027 , and all hiring will be finalized by March 12, 2027 .
FAQ and contact information
For more information about the Law Clerk Program and the clerkship application process, please consult the Frequently asked questions .
For any other questions, contact the Law Clerk Program: lcp-paj@scc-csc.ca .

Company Description
The Library of Parliament is a non-partisan organization that provides a unique and stimulating work environment. We are led by our guiding principles of agility, collaboration, excellence, impartiality, and inclusion. For more information about the Library and what we offer, visit Employment opportunities at the Library of Parliament .
Job Description
The Information Management Technician is responsible for managing the technical configuration of the Information Management Modules within the Electronic Document and Records Management System (EDRMS) which manage the information resources lifecycle; provides significant technical support to clients (i.e., Library staff and managers from all service areas) related to the management of electronic information resources; develops and delivers technical training sessions to clients and recommends technical solutions.
The incumbent performs the following duties:
- Participates in the development and use of institutional repositories, particularly EDRMS by managing the Records Management module within the Electronic Document and Records Management System (EDRMS) and developing business processes to facilitate the capture, control, maintenance, and disposition of information resources and IM metadata.
- Provides significant technical support to clients (i.e., Library staff and managers from all service areas) related to the management of electronic information resources.

- Experience participating in projects or collaborating with stakeholders regarding the management of electronic documents and records

- Knowledge of legislation, policies, guidelines, and standards relevant to information management
- Knowledge of principles, techniques and experience with complex systems used for the management of electronic Information Resources (such as an EDRMS) is required to support and participate in the implementation and effective use of information management tools, processes and practices within the system

- Adaptability
- Client Focus
- Embracing Diversity
- Exemplifying Integrity
- Information and Knowledge Resource Management
- Quality Focus
- Attention to Detail
- Initiative
- Teamwork
- Planning and Organizing
Asset Criteria :
- Experience implementing digital multimedia asset management systems and workflows

- A successful pre-employment security screening.
- A second-language evaluation (Bilingual staffing – Imperative): CBC/CBC.
Second language self-assessment test:
To help you decide if you should apply to a bilingual position, an optional self-assessment of your written expression and reading comprehension in your second official language is available for you to take before completing your application.
Try out the self-assessment tests for written expression and reading comprehension. For more information on language requirements, see the language requirements for candidates . https://www.canada.ca/en/public-service-commission/jobs/services/gc-jobs/language-requirements-candidates.html

Please include a cover letter with your application describing how you meet the education and experience requirements of the position. Applications without a cover letter may not be considered . The Library of Parliament welcomes all candidates to apply and encourages applications from Indigenous persons, racialized persons, 2SLGBTQIA+ persons and persons with disabilities for this position.

Satisfactory references and proof of education are essential conditions of appointment.
Travel and relocation expenses are the responsibility of the candidates.
Visit About the Library of Parliament of Canada to learn more about us!
To learn more about our staffing process, consult our FAQs.

The program
The NRC’s Postdoctoral Fellowship program offers PDFs access to unique world-class facilities and the opportunity to work alongside multi-disciplinary teams of expert researchers and technicians on projects of critical importance to Canada. PDFs will carry out research on innovative research projects, with opportunities for career development (publications and/or industry interaction).
PDFs will be offered appointments to the staff of the National Research Council on a term basis and will be offered salaries and benefits currently available to Research Officers. Salaries commensurate with experience are taxable and subject to other deductions. As a guide, the current annual PhD recruiting rate is $83,985. In addition PDFs will be allocated a travel fund to support their work.
Project title
Next-Generation Battery Management System for Electrified Transportation and Energy Storage
The role
Battery systems are central to electrified transportation, including electric vehicles, trains, and aircraft. Every battery pack requires a battery management system (BMS), an electronic controller that monitors, protects, and optimizes battery operation. Current BMS technology has critical gaps: existing platforms are closed and restrict research use; temperature sensing is sparse, forcing engineers to rely on unreliable simulation models; and the standard cell-balancing method wastes energy as heat.
This project will develop a next-generation, NRC-built BMS platform integrating three novel capabilities: a flexible, cloud-connected architecture for research use; fiber Bragg grating (FBG) optical sensors embedded in battery packs, providing hundreds of real-time temperature sensing points to support thermal management and fast charging; and an active cell-balancing prototype that redistributes energy between cells rather than dissipating it. The project will produce peer-reviewed publications and patent opportunities, and directly supports Canada's net-zero transportation goals.
As the postdoctoral fellow, you will be the primary researcher on this project, taking each of its three components from early-stage work to working hardware. In your first year, you will be a part of the development of the NRC BMS platform, expanding its hardware and software capability. Across both years, you will build on a completed proof of concept to embed FBG sensor arrays into battery modules and connect them to the platform for real-time thermal mapping. In your second year, you will develop a physical active cell-balancing prototype and benchmark it against conventional passive balancing.
You will work with a high degree of autonomy, supported by a project lead and other team members. You will have hands-on access to NRC’s state-of-the-art battery testing facility and will collaborate with researchers across NRC, including the Aerospace and Construction research centres, as well as external partners. In this role, you will build expertise in embedded sensing, power electronics, and software development, and you will be encouraged to publish in peer-reviewed journals, present at conferences, and pursue patents arising from the work.
Education
PhD in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or in a field related to the position.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Experience conducting research in a field related to energy storage, power electronics, or embedded systems.
- Experience using programming and data analysis software such as Python, MATLAB, or C/C++.
The following experience criteria would be considered assets:
- Experience designing, building, or testing electronic hardware or battery systems in a laboratory setting.
- Experience working with battery management systems and related functions such as state estimation, cell balancing, or thermal management.
- Experience developing circuit design, simulation, or printed circuit board (PCB).
- Experience developing embedded firmware for microcontrollers.
- Experience using cloud connectivity, IoT systems, and connected devices.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Condition of employment
Reliability Status
For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
Who is eligible?
- Fellowships will be for two years contingent on satisfactory progress achieved during the first year.
- Candidates should have obtained a PhD (or equivalent) within the past three years (PhD received on or after July 1, 2024*) or expect to complete their PhD within 6 months of appointment.
- Fellows will work in a lab under the direct supervision of an NRC researcher.

Project title
Learning Driver Attention Strategies in Adverse Weather Using Graph-Based Inverse Reinforcement Learning.
The role
The successful candidate will develop a graph-based inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) framework for analyzing and forecasting eye-gaze scanpaths of human drivers of motor vehicles. Our objective is to infer the underlying reward structures that govern gaze behavior and thereby reveal how attention strategies adapt to changing environmental conditions. By applying spectral graph analysis , we aim to derive quantifiable and interpretable metrics that capture shifts in gaze patterns across different weather scenarios. To the best of our knowledge, this will be the first in-depth study of driver eye-gaze behavior under adverse weather, representing a novel contribution to the field.
