Project title
Immune Monitoring Using a Centrifugal Microfluidic System: Strategies Towards Workflow Implementation and Automation for Remote Precision Diagnostics
The role
Are you looking for a unique opportunity where you can grow your career while having a tangible impact for Canada, Canadians and far beyond our borders? Do you want an environment that will encourage growth and development? Do you want to be part of the development of new and innovative applied research? This PDF project positions Canada at the intersection of two national priorities: space exploration and equitable healthcare access.
The long-term vision of this research is to establish autonomous immune monitoring technologies for space exploration and remote healthcare applications. As a critical step toward this vision, the primary objective of this two-year PDF project is to develop and experimentally validate a laboratory prototype of an autonomous centrifugal microfluidic immune monitoring platform.
The project focuses on prototype development, subsystem integration, and analytical performance evaluation. The aim is to develop a novel, platform-based approach for assessing changes in immune function through semi-quantitative analysis of cytokines released following ex vivo stimulation of whole blood. Unlike conventional immune monitoring workflows that rely on manual sample preparation, centralized laboratory infrastructure, and delayed post-mission analysis, the proposed system integrates immune stimulation, sample processing, and multiplex cytokine detection within a single autonomous microfluidic cartridge. While scientifically demanding, this approach offers the potential to redefine point-of-need immune monitoring, including for long-duration spaceflight, by enabling near real-time analysis and reducing sample-to-result turnaround from several days to a few hours, thereby supporting more timely clinical decision-making and enabling the rapid implementation of countermeasures.
The outcome is an immune monitoring capability with direct translation to astronaut health, Indigenous and Northern community healthcare, critical care, and pandemic preparedness. The project is embedded in a larger collaboration effort involving LMU Hospital (Munich, Germany) with support from both the Canadian and European Space Agency.
Integrated into the MD–Precision Diagnostics Team at NRC Boucherville, where you can leverage established expertise, infrastructure, and ongoing research activities, you will lead the experimental design, optimization, integration, and validation of the incubation cartridge and multiplex immunoassay, including data analysis, interpretation, manuscript preparation, and dissemination of results.
The role (continue)
Opportunities to pursue independent research aligned with the project objectives will be encouraged. The project will provide comprehensive interdisciplinary training in :
- microfluidic system design,
- centrifugal automation,
- immunology,
- multiplex immunoassay development,
- analytical validation,
- prototype integration,
- project management,
- scientific communication, and
- translational medical device development.
Through full participation in all stages of the project, you will gain experience spanning the complete technology development pipeline, from prototype design and fabrication to experimental validation, performance benchmarking, and knowledge dissemination.
Your training will be supported through multidisciplinary mentorship within the NRC and collaboration with the Laboratory of Translational Research – Stress & Immunity at LMU Hospital (Munich, Germany), providing additional expertise in translational immunology and opportunities for international collaboration and professional networking.
Conference participation and publication of at least two peer-reviewed manuscripts will further support your professional development as a highly qualified researcher in translational diagnostic technologies.
About Medical Devices
The Medical Devices (MD) Research center has the mandate to support economic development through innovation in health care, including innovative diagnostic tests and instruments. The research center's primary sector of activity is the medical devices and diagnostic industry with impact on all aspect of life sciences in innovative analytics and biomarker detection (medical diagnostics, point-of-care devices, process analytics, biodefence, cell & gene therapy, etc.).
We support the Canadian ecosystem in the development, translation and implementation of medical device innovations.

A PhD in Biomedical engineering, Immunology, Microbiology, Biotechnology, Microfluidics, Material science, Experimental medicine, Analytical chemistry or related discipline is required.

- Hands-on experience with immunological, cell-based, and/or biochemical assays, including the detection and quantification of cytokines, proteins, or other immune biomarkers;

Project title
Uncertainty Quantification and Calibration for Large Language Models
The role
Are you looking for an opportunity to conduct cutting-edge research with real-life impacts? Do you want to grow in a team environment that provides guidance and autonomy? Do you want ownership over outcomes allowing you to present your work at competitive international venues? Look no further we have a rewarding opportunity for you!
Current human-AI interaction is plagued by over-reliance on AI predictions, an inability to distinguish AI-generated content, and the risks of AI-generated falsehoods and deceptions. Quantifying the uncertainty in AI generations is a pathway to mitigating all of these risks.
Traditionally in AI research, a well-designed certainty measure assigns a probability of correctness to each generated output. Combining AI outputs with these interpretable confidence scores is immensely valuable for informed human-AI interaction. In the new era of generative large language models (LLMs), uncertainty quantification becomes less well-defined due to the open-ended nature of LLM outputs (i.e., it is necessary to simultaneously estimate the uncertainty in what is being said, and how it is being said, while dealing with an infinite output space). However, LLMs are now the backbone of most human-facing AI systems. How to meaningfully capture these uncertainties to provide useful context on LLM generations is an active research question.
Separately, recent work suggests that LLMs represent human-interpretable concepts (e.g., emotions, truthfulness, harmfulness, etc.) at intermediate points in their computation. This opens up a new opportunity to inspect uncertainty in the LLMs’ encoding of these concepts, which would enable new insights and intervention mechanisms. To date, we are not aware of any work that applies certainty calibration methods to intermediate model representations.
This project develops methods for uncertainty quantification that can be applied to both output generations, and intermediate features. Foundational work on this subject is both technically challenging and highly applicable to a wide range of open problems. The anticipated research outcomes are appropriate for publication in top-tier international venues for Computational Linguistics and Machine Learning research, such as ACL* conferences, ICLR, or ICML.
The Research Problem
Large language models produce text by iteratively generating a probability distribution over possible next-word choices, then sampling from that distribution. The problem of uncertainty quantification aims to consolidate that probability distribution into a few meaningful and interpretable certainty metrics. Certainty metrics can answer questions about reproducibility (i.e., if asked the same thing again, how likely is the LLM to respond in the same way?), or embedded knowledge (i.e., if asked a factual query, how certain is the LLM about its prediction?). Such measures can help contextualize LLM outputs for users or developers, and are a critical ingredient for trustworthy AI systems.
The proposed research agenda develops new methods for uncertainty quantification that can apply to features, determines whether such signals can be used to improve uncertainty metrics for text generation, and enables a host of impactful research applications:
- Hallucination detection
- Deception detection
- Synthetic content detection
- Mitigation of safety failure modes
- Improved evaluation
- Trustworthy decision support systems
In the long-term, the new knowledge that is created can support Canada’s commitment to safe and responsible use of generative AI, support strategic defence applications, and open new research opportunities.
In addition to the proposed research program, you will benefit from proximity to related work that is ongoing in the team. We currently work on distinct, but related, work in LLM interpretability and evaluation. There is potential for you to contribute to those works as well, if desired. We have ongoing collaborations with Mila (one of Canada’s leading AI research institutes) and Cohere (Canada’s largest LLM provider), which creates good networking or collaboration opportunities. It is expected that you will work autonomously, with guidance from the project lead, such that you have ownership over the outcomes, obtain first-author publications, and present the work at these competitive international venues.

The role
The NRC is currently working on syngas fermentation for ethanol production, to serve as a replacement for fossil fuels, thus strengthening low-carbon fuel value chains in Canada.
The objective of this project is to develop synthetic microbial consortia with complementary metabolic functions and capable of converting syngas into ethanol with higher efficiency and stability than conventional monoculture systems. The research will comprise three research components:
- Isolate and adapt microbial strains capable of thriving in syngas environments using enrichment and adaptive laboratory evolution;
- Design synthetic microbial consortia composed of microorganisms with complementary metabolic functions;
- Evaluate the performance of these consortia in laboratory-scale bioreactors.
The outcomes of this work will advance the emerging field of microbial community engineering and support the development of scalable technologies for sustainable fuel production and carbon circularity.
Within a multidisciplinary team, the successful candidate will lead the design, construction, and experimental evaluation of synthetic microbial consortia.

Project title
Engineered Recycled Glass as a Supplementary Cementitious Material for Low Carbon, High Performance Concrete ─ Stabilizing the Supply Chain in Canada
The role
Concrete, the most widely used construction material worldwide, is essential for resilient infrastructure but also generates significant greenhouse gas emissions due to cement production. A key strategy for reducing these emissions is lowering the clinker content of cement through supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs). However, the traditional SCM supply chain is shrinking as coal power generation is phased out and steel production technologies evolve, creating an emerging materials challenge for low‑carbon concrete in Canada. This project will address the challenge by investigating ground recycled glass (GRG) as a scalable, sustainable alternative SCM supporting both decarbonization and circular economy objectives.
The PDF will play a central role in designing and executing the experimental research program. Responsibilities will include investigating hydration kinetics and pozzolanic reactivity in cementitious systems incorporating GRG, evaluating the fresh and hardened performance of concrete mixtures, and conducting life cycle and techno-economic assessments.

- Significant experience in cementitious materials research, including cement chemistry, hydration mechanisms, supplementary cementitious materials, concrete performance evaluation, and/or low-carbon concrete technologies.
- Experience in the full spectrum of research activities, including identifying research needs, developing research proposals, planning and managing projects, conducting laboratory investigations, analyzing and interpreting data, and disseminating results through technical reports, presentations, and peer-reviewed publications.
- Experience in the design, execution, and interpretation of laboratory experiments related to cementitious materials and concrete, including analytical characterization techniques, performance testing, durability assessment, and modelling approaches.
- Experience in evaluating concrete durability and long-term performance, including investigation of deterioration mechanisms, service-life assessment methodologies, and performance-based testing approaches.

Description du poste
Relevant de l’avocate générale du Comité mixte permanent d’examen de la réglementation, l’analyste (conseiller/conseillère juridique) est responsable de fournir des conseils juridiques au Comité mixte sur les lacunes juridiques et procédurales relevées dans les instruments statutaires émanant du pouvoir exécutif.
La personne titulaire du poste assume les tâches suivantes :
- Comparaître devant le Comité mixte afin de fournir des conseils sur des questions juridiques nouvelles et complexes en droit réglementaire et de répondre aux questions des membres.
- Rédiger des avis juridiques pour le client et appliquer les principes juridiques régissant l’exercice des pouvoirs législatifs délégués, l’interprétation des lois et le droit administratif.
- Rédiger des lettres aux ministères et organismes gouvernementaux sur une question juridique ou sa résolution pour le client.
Qualifications
Éducation :
- un baccalauréat en droit (LL.B.) / Juris Doctor (J.D.) obtenu d'une université reconnue, combiné à une adhésion en règle à un barreau provincial ou territorial.
Expérience :
- expérience récente dans la rédaction d’avis juridiques complexes dans l'un des domaines juridiques de la sphère fédérale;
- expérience récente dans la conduite de recherches et d’analyses juridiques en droit réglementaire, interprétation des lois, droit administratif, droit constitutionnel et droit parlementaire.
- récente fait référence à l’expérience acquise au cours des cinq (5) dernières années.
Connaissances :
- connaissance du rôle et du mandat du Comité mixte permanent d’examen de la réglementation;
- connaissance du processus réglementaire fédéral;
- connaissance du droit administratif et des principes juridiques régissant l’exercice des pouvoirs législatifs délégués;
- connaissance des méthodes, techniques et pratiques juridiques, telles que l’interprétation des lois et la recherche juridique (électronique et manuelle).

- Faculté d’adaptation
- Orientation client
- Modèle d’intégrité
- Souci du détail
- Recherche
- Travail d’équipe
- Réflexion analytique
- Communication

- expérience dans la formulation de conseils et d’avis juridiques et leur présentation adaptée à divers publics;
- expérience de la prestation de services juridiques dans la fonction publique, en cabinet privé ou en milieu parlementaire.

Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
We are looking for Technical Officers to support the Canadian Photonics Fabrication Centre (CPFC) within NRC’s Emerging Technology and Photonics Research Centre portfolio. The Technical Officer is someone who shares the NRC core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect, and Creativity.
The position will focus on providing process support for semiconductor prototype development and pre-commercial production in a class 100 – 1000 clean room facility environment.
The successful candidates will be involved in hands-on wafer fabrication activities while maintaining high standards of quality to support client demands. These candidates would be members of a team of technical specialists responsible for the performance of a wide range of semiconductor wafer fabrication processes. Processes relevant to this position include, but are not limited to; electron-beam (e-beam) lithography, plasma dry-etch, chemical wet- etch, and metrology processing on indium phosphide (InP) substrates for relevant client projects, but other processing may be assigned as required by supervisors. All processing must be accomplished in accordance with instructions contained in the manufacturing execution system (MES) and the schedule set by the operations and planning teams.
The Government of Canada has decided to undertake a spin-off of the NRC's Canadian Photonics Fabrication Centre (CPFC) into a commercial entity with firmly Canadian foundations and with Canadian industrial development at its core.
For more information, visit Canadian Photonics Fabrication Centre .
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Post-secondary education in Electronic Engineering Technology, or Scientific discipline related to the position or an appropriate combination of education and work experience.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency

The role
We are looking for a Vehicle Power and Energy Systems Engineer to support the Automotive and Surface Transportation (AST) Research Centre. The successful candidate would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity. NRC Automotive and Surface Transportation (AST) Research Centre has the mandate to advance product and process technologies for producing more efficient, safe, affordable and environmentally responsible ground vehicles, and to deliver engineering solutions to complex technology challenges facing today’s surface transportation industries including automotive, heavy and specialized vehicles, and rail. The engineer will contribute to the development, integration, testing, validation, and demonstration of advanced vehicle systems for automotive, commercial vehicle, rail, and other ground transportation applications. The primary responsibility of the candidate is to support the goals of NRC and the Research Centre in providing Canadians access to research, scientific knowledge, and technologies for innovation in ground transportation. The candidate will work in a multidisciplinary team environment with researchers and technical experts in unique research facilities and in the field. The candidate will be responsible for developing, conducting, coordinating, and reporting on research and engineering projects related to vehicle systems architecture, power and energy systems integration, energy management, and the validation of advanced transportation technologies. Duties and responsibilities will include:
- Author, review, and critique research plans, detailed work plans, technical reports, and technical papers
- Lead and support research projects involving vehicle systems integration, energy management, controls, and advanced transportation technologies.
- Develop and evaluate vehicle architectures and integrated systems involving propulsion, energy storage, thermal management, power distribution, and control systems.
- Apply systems engineering principles including requirements development, interface management, system integration, verification, and validation activities.
- Conduct vehicle-level performance assessments and optimization analyses to improve efficiency, safety, reliability, and operational effectiveness.
- Assist in the development of research proposals including collaboration with industry partners, scope definition, research planning, and funding estimates.
- Interpret and analyze experimental, simulation, and operational data and develop robust conclusions and recommendations.
- Conduct literature reviews and technology assessments related to advanced vehicle systems, energy management strategies, and emerging transportation technologies.
- Present research findings in technical forums including conferences, seminars, standards committees, and working groups.
- Support technology transfer and engagement with industrial, academic, and government stakeholders.

- Experience designing, implementing, testing, and validating vehicle power management, control, or energy systems, including the analysis of vehicle-level performance and system optimization.

About CSE
The Communications Security Establishment (CSE) is Canada’s agency responsible for foreign signals intelligence, cyber operations and cyber security. Learn more about our mission , and what it means to work in a security and intelligence field .

Job summary
In this role you will perform psychological assessments on potential candidates and current employees. You will be responsible to administer and interpret standardized psychological tests and conduct psychological interviews. Your assessment reports will offer advice and recommendations about the suitability and organizational complementarity of candidates, or about the psychological readiness of employees for a mission.
Salary
To find out more about our salary scale, vacation allowances and benefits (health, dental and pension plans, etc.) visit the Compensation page on our website.

Open to Canadian citizens.
Location
Ottawa, Ontario. CSE has two accessible facilities . Flexible work arrangements, including telework for a portion of the work week, may be possible.

More information about our hiring and security processes can be found on our website.
Essential qualifications
In order to be considered, your cover letter must clearly explain how you meet the following education and experience requirements.
Education
- Hold a master's or doctoral degree in psychology from a recognized university with a specialization in clinical or forensic psychology, and
- Be an active member of the College of Psychologists of Ontario, the Order of Psychologists of Quebec or in your province of residence and be authorized to practice independently, as a psychologist, in the field of forensic or clinical psychology.
Note: The educational program must be recognized in Canada, and you must be able to provide proof of education credentials.
Experience
- Conducting psychological assessments with adults, including experience in assessing personality, emotional and behavioral functioning and psychopathology.
- Administering and interpreting standardized psychological assessment instruments (ie. MMPI-2; MMPI-3 MMPI-RF, PAI, NEO-PI)
- Writing psychological reports and communicating psychological assessment results in a clear, concise and professional manner.
Official language requirements
Bilingual imperative: CCC/CCC
- Bilingual means that knowledge of both official languages (English and French) is required for the position. Imperative means that you must possess the knowledge of both official languages before a job offer can be made.
- The profile (CCC/CCC) represent the proficiency level you must demonstrate in each of the language skills (reading, writing and oral interaction) for the bilingual position. For bilingual positions, second language evaluations will be offered to candidates who don’t have valid language test results issued by the Government of Canada.
Find out more about the language requirements of positions.

The following technical, behavioural and leadership competencies will be assessed at a later date. You do not need to include information about them in your application.
Technical competencies
- Knowledge of Clinical Psychology (Psychopathology, Mental Health Issues and Treatment)
- Knowledge of Methods Related to Individual Psychological Assessment of Adults
- Consultation Services, Communication and Education on Psychological Indicators and Behavioural (which may pose a Risk for the Organization)

- Cognitive Thinking Skills
- Interactive Communication
- Working in a Team
Leadership competencies
- Achieving Results
- Collaboration
- Integrity, Respect and Awareness
Assets
Assets are “nice-to-have” expertise and skills we’re interested in.

Asset experience
- Completing psychological assessments that are relevant to personnel selection in a high security environment.
How to apply
You may submit your candidacy online by selecting “Apply” at the top or bottom of this page.
If you cannot apply online or have a disability preventing you from applying online, please inform us by email at careers-carrieres@cse-cst.gc.ca prior to the closing date of this hiring process.
Important information
We ask you to not discuss your application with others (including on social media) besides your partner, or close family members - who should also be reminded about the need to be discreet.
Assessments of candidates are conducted in the official language of their choice.
To address CSE’s current representation gaps, priority may be given to persons who self-declare as belonging to one, or more, designated employment equity groups: women; Indigenous peoples, including First Nations who are status, or registered and non-status, or non-registered, Inuit and Métis; persons with disabilities, including people with a mental health condition and neurodivergent people; and persons from racial or ethnic groups.
Please note the Employment Equity Act , which is under review, uses the terminology Aboriginal peoples and visible minorities.
CSE offers an assessment process that will accommodate any reasonable measures you require to be assessed in a fair and equitable manner. Those measures are available to all candidates during our processes. Information you provide will be addressed confidentially.
All communications with CSE relating to this process, including email messages and telephone conversations, may be used in the assessment of qualifications.
The intent of this process is to fill vacant positions at CSE. The process may also be used to establish a pool of qualified candidates which could be used to staff similar or identical positions with various tenures.

The role
We are looking for a Software Developer and Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) Specialist to join our Aerospace Research Centre at the Flight Research Laboratory’s (FRL) Flight Recorder Playback Center (FRPC). You would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The FRPC provides flight data recorder (FDR) data recovery and analysis services to the Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF). These services include data and audio recovery and analysis from aircraft accidents and incidents as well as the annual evaluation of flight data recorder systems and cockpit voice recorders (CVR) installed in aircraft across multiple fleets, using a variety of recording systems from different manufacturers.
As a Software Developer and CVR Specialist, you will develop and maintain software tools at NRC and those provided by FDR manufacturers to play back, process and analyze flight data downloaded from FDRs. You will manage the facility’s internal computer network and coordinate with the corporate IT team from NRC as needed. You will also become NRC’s subject-matter expert for CVR systems, including conducting annual CVR audio evaluations for RCAF aircraft.
FDR and CVR data downloads could arrive daily. You will manage the associated workflow and prepare analysis reports within established timeframes.
Your work will involve:
- Developing, maintaining and enhancing FRPC software tools and databases using Qt, C++, Python, Microsoft Access and VBA;
- Maintaining FRPC procedures, equipment documentation, specialized external software and internal IT systems—including legacy and current Windows environments, basic network administration, and data backup and recovery;
- Conducting annual CVR audio evaluations for RCAF aircraft;
- Supporting CVR requirements development and assessment for new RCAF aircraft acquisitions;
- Supporting flight-recorder recovery activities, including crash-damaged recoveries, and collaborating with the FRPC Facility Manager and NRC IT team; and
- Participating in a rotating on-call schedule with other engineers, including occasional work outside regular business hours.
The ideal candidate will be an organized and adaptable problem solver with strong software-development, computer networking, data-analysis and technical-reporting skills. The candidate will be comfortable working with legacy and modern computer systems, specialized flight-recorder software, and audio hardware systems and analysis procedures. The ideal candidate will be an innovative problem solver who enjoys working hands-on with facilities as well as network and computer systems while collaborating with scientists, engineers, and clients to advance flight safety and Canada’s aerospace research capabilities.

- Basic experience configuring, maintaining and troubleshooting computer systems, operating systems, specialized technical equipment, data storage and backup/recovery systems;

Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
Help bring research to life and drive your career forward with the National Research Council of Canada (NRC), Canada's largest research and technology organization.
Are you passionate about helping Canadian innovators access global resources, tools and collaborators? Do you have a solid track record of making things happen on the international stage? Are you a polished negotiator and communicator adept at implementing strategies?
If so, help the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) maximize the impact of its international relations. We are looking for a vibrant and driven Director for our International Relations Office. The successful candidate will be someone who shares our core values of impact, accountability, leadership, integrity and collaboration and who thrives in a fast-paced high-pressure environment.
Working closely with your Director General, Director colleagues and with senior managers and executives across the organization, you will use your own STI network, understanding and relationships to design and execute international advice, briefings, strategies and agreements that are important to NRC and to Canada. As a natural leader, you will energize and build a strong team to serve the corporation and you will negotiate with diverse groups within NRC and around the globe to bring ideas and strategies to life. Senior Security Analyst
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
In addition to the position being staffed, this competition may be used to fill similar opportunities (Regular or Term) that become available at the same job grade. If you’re interested in this type of role, we encourage you to apply.
What you will do Reporting to the Senior Manager, Security Threat Monitoring, Screening and Access Programs, you will be the Bank's senior technical specialist for complex personnel security assessments and risk analysis. You will handle highly sensitive information with discretion and sound judgment, following privacy, confidentiality, information-handling and need-to-know requirements.
You will assess high-risk screening cases, including adverse information, unresolved security concerns, Resolution of Doubt, Reviews for Cause and enhanced screening.
You will provide expert advice to support personnel security decisions, working alongside Screening Analysts and the Screening Manager. You will also support Threat Monitoring and incident response when demand increases.
Specifically, you will:
Lead Complex Personnel Security Assessments
- Assess complex, escalated personnel security cases involving adverse information, elevated risks or unresolved concerns.
- Gather, verify and analyze information from authorized internal and external sources to identify concerns, credibility issues, vulnerabilities and mitigating factors.
- Evaluate risks based on duties, access and organizational exposure, and provide evidence-based recommendations to management.
Conduct Security Interviews
- Plan and conduct fair, objective security screening and Resolution of Doubt interviews tailored to identified risks.
- Verify information, assess the credibility and consistency of responses, and document findings for assessments and recommendations.
Support Resolution of Doubt
- Analyze criminal, financial, association, credibility and behavioural concerns to support Resolution of Doubt.
- Develop assessment and interview plans, and coordinate information gathering with internal and external partners.
- Ensure assessments follow applicable policies, standards, procedural fairness and personnel security principles.
Conduct Advanced Open-Source Intelligence Research and Analysis
- Conduct advanced open-source intelligence (OSINT) research to verify information and identify personnel security concerns and emerging risks.
- Evaluate source credibility, reliability and limitations, and document research methods, findings and conclusions.
- Provide OSINT expertise for personnel security, threat assessments and complex work across teams.
Prepare Findings, Assessments and Recommendations
- Prepare clear, accurate and defensible assessment reports, case summaries and briefings that meet applicable policies and standards.
- Present balanced, evidence-based recommendations to decision-makers on risks, mitigation measures, conditions, monitoring and organizational impacts.
Provide Technical Leadership
- Advise analysts and management as the technical expert on complex personnel security assessments, interviewing and risk analysis.
- Review complex, sensitive or precedent-setting files, identify quality gaps and improve standards, procedures and tools.
- Mentor and coach Screening Analysts to strengthen analytical, interviewing and risk assessment skills.
Support Threat Monitoring and Incident Response
- Support Threat Monitoring during heightened threats, major events, incidents, employee safety concerns or increased demand.
- Use OSINT and internal and external information to assess emerging threats, actors and behaviours affecting the Bank, its employees, operations, assets and reputation.
- Prepare threat assessments, intelligence reports and briefings, and provide rapid analysis, escalation and decision support during incidents and crises.
- Stay current on evolving threats and tactics, and improve monitoring, analytical methods and intelligence sharing.
What You Need to Succeed
You are an experienced security professional with expertise in personnel security screening, assessing adverse information, risk analysis and security interviews.
You use sound judgment to balance security risks, organizational needs, privacy, procedural fairness and risk-management principles when making recommendations.
You demonstrate:
- Advanced knowledge of personnel security screening processes, standards, and practices.
- Advanced knowledge of personnel security risk assessment methodologies.
- Experience supporting Resolution of Doubt activities, enhanced screening reviews, and Reviews for Cause processes.
- Experience conducting security screening interviews and fact-finding interviews.
- Strong analytical and critical-thinking abilities.
- Advanced OSINT research and analytical capabilities.
- Experience preparing assessment reports, security assessments, risk assessments, briefing notes, and recommendations for management.
- Strong written communication, briefing, and presentation skills.
- Exceptional judgment, discretion and attention to detail, with a demonstrated ability to protect highly sensitive personal and security information and share it only on an authorized need-to-know basis.
- Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
- Ability to mentor and provide technical guidance to others.
- Ability to influence decisions through expertise, rigorous analysis and professional credibility, without formal authority.
Nice-to-Have
- Experience conducting complex personnel security assessments.
- Experience supporting Reviews for Cause and other personnel security review processes.
- Experience conducting OSINT activities related to personnel security or threat assessment matters.
- Knowledge of Government of Canada security screening standards and best practices.
- Experience working with law enforcement, intelligence, regulatory, or security partners.
- Experience developing assessment methodologies, procedures, or analytical frameworks.
Education and Experience This position requires a bachelor's degree in Criminology, Security Studies, Intelligence Studies, Psychology, Sociology, Law, Public Administration, Political Science, International Relations, Business Administration or a related discipline and a minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in personnel security screening or assessments, security risk assessment, intelligence analysis, threat assessment, law enforcement, regulatory investigations or related security functions. An equivalent combination of education and experience may also be considered.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional). If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.
What you need to know
- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Top Secret Relocation assistance may be provided, if required Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.
Hybrid Work Model
The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.
What you can expect from us This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit A great deal to consider .
- Salaries are based on qualifications and experience and typically range from $111,051 to $130,649 (job grade 17) The Bank offers an incentive for successfully meeting expectations at 7 to 10% of your base salary. The Bank offers additional performance pay (5%) for those who exceed expectations. Exceptional performers who far exceed expectations may be eligible for higher performance pay. Flexible and comprehensive benefits so you can choose the level of health and dental coverage that meets your needs Extra vacation days (up to five each year) that you can purchase to add to your vacation entitlement Option to join the indexed, defined-benefit pension plan after 24 consecutive months of service
We wish to thank all applicants for their interest and effort in applying for this position. Only candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

The Role
We are looking for a senior-career Industrial Technology Advisor (ITA) to support the NRC Industrial Research Assistance Program (NRC IRAP). The ITA would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
Regarded worldwide as one of the best programs of its kind, IRAP is Canada’s premier innovation assistance program for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
We are looking for a seasoned industry professional who is absolutely enthusiastic about helping innovative Canadian companies grow and prosper. We need people who see the potential in a business and are driven to nurture it to the next level. We are increasing our staff across the country and our clients need engaged professionals to provide innovative advisory services to help them grow. We are focused on results and we aren’t afraid of risk all in an effort to add positive impact to the Canadian economy.
Why Work With Us?
ITAs are self-directed and work in teams with company leaders helping their firms grow through the commercialization of innovation. They find the work very rewarding with a wide range of benefits , professional development and learn from clients and colleagues every day in a well-balanced work-life environment.
ITAs serve as trusted advisors and mentors to these SMEs, helping them navigate technical or business hurdles, providing important linkages and identifying new opportunities and thereby playing a part in their evolution, growth and success. This is what truly sets NRC IRAP apart – it is part of what we call the ITA advantage. It’s a winning model we have been using to accelerate business growth and thereby creating wealth for Canadians.
In addition, we offer:
- Flexibility: work/life balance.
- A collaborative environment: at NRC IRAP, your ideas are listened to, respected and important.
- A rewarding career: we offer the opportunity to provide value to Canadian companies and have a positive impact on the Canadian economy at large.
https://nrc.canada.ca/en/support-technology-innovation/make-your-mark-become-industrial-technology-advisor
Screening Criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Post-secondary degree in Science or Engineering in a discipline related to the position from a recognized university.
A combination of a post-secondary degree in another field with significant work experience relevant to the position will be considered.
Preference may be given to candidates with a complementary degree or diploma in business, management, administration, finance or marketing.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience

The role
The Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre (HAA) is seeking an Optical Engineer to lead the conception, development and delivery of advanced optical instrumentation and systems for current and future astronomical observatories. The successful candidate will be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect, and Creativity and will work closely with astronomers, engineers, and technical specialists. The role involves translating scientific and technical requirements into practical engineering solutions, developing optical designs and performance analyses such as tolerancing, stray-light, image quality, throughput, and alignment planning. You will make significant contributions to the design, integration, testing, and verification of complex UV/VIS/NIR optical systems, analyze test results, and recommend design improvements or corrective actions as required. Working within multidisciplinary teams, the Optical Engineer will collaborate closely with mechanical, electrical, software, systems, scientific, and technical specialists to develop instrument concepts, perform technical trade studies, and guide engineering decisions throughout the instrument lifecycle. Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
- leading or contributing to strategic research and development activities;
- investigating and evaluating emerging optical technologies;
- preparing technical documentation such as optical specifications, interface control documents, test and verification plans, alignment procedures, technical reports, and design review materials;
- supporting procurement activities, vendor interactions, component evaluation, and acceptance testing.
The position offers the opportunity to contribute to facility-class astronomical instrumentation, space-based observatories and strategic research and development initiatives, participate in national and international collaborations, and provide technical guidance and knowledge transfer to colleagues, students, and junior staff where appropriate. We welcome applications from candidates at different career stages who can demonstrate strong technical foundations, a commitment to learning, and the potential to contribute to the development of advanced scientific instrumentation.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Graduation with a Masters or PhD from a recognized post-secondary institution in Optical Engineering, Physics, Engineering Physics, Electrical Engineering, or another field relevant to the position. Graduation with a Masters or PhD from a recognized post-secondary institution in Engineering combined with relevant work experience in astronomy or other sectors such as aerospace, space systems, defense, remote sensing, biomedical imaging, photonics, or other precision optical industries may also be considered. As part of their application package, applicants are required to provide the following:
- Cover Letter
- Resume
- 2-page Executive Summary: The summary must describe a relevant project, completed from design to delivery, and include key information such as project overview, optical design, modelled performance, tolerance summary, delivered performance, and lessons learned. Applicants should clearly identify their own role and contributions, and focus on the most important technical aspects of the project, including driving requirements, design choices, performance metrics, and verification strategies. Confidential or proprietary details may be anonymized.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Extensive* experience in optical engineering, including most of the following areas: optical lens design, modelling, performance analysis, tolerancing, procurement, testing, alignment, integration, verification/validation, and optical metrology.
- Significant** experience leading or making substantial technical contributions to at least one optical engineering project through the full lifecycle, including requirements definition, design, integration, testing, verification, and final delivery or acceptance.
* Extensive: Typically 8–10+ years of deep technical experience. ** Significant: Typically 4–5+ years of progressive technical experience.
The following will be considered as assets:
- Experience developing, integrating, or supporting complex, facility-class scientific instruments, observatory-class astronomical instrumentation, mission-class spaceflight payloads, or large-scale remote sensing systems in a multidisciplinary environment.
- Experience designing or building spectrographs, spectrometers, or other dispersive optical instruments. (IFU/IFS, MOS, echelle, slit or slitless)
- Experience designing, specifying, procuring, testing, and aligning custom optics such as dispersive elements, aspherics and free-forms.
- Experience with one or more of the following specialized technologies: Adaptive optics, fiber-fed instruments, detector systems, calibration systems, cryogenic optical systems, precision opto-mechanical systems, photonics.
- Experience applying systems engineering practices to complex scientific or engineering projects, including development of performance budgets (wavefront error, throughput, image/pupil quality) requirements management, interface control, verification and validation, risk management, or technical reviews.
- Experience providing technical leadership, including conceptualizing new instruments, leading technical work packages, coordinating multidisciplinary teams, mentoring technical personnel, or influencing technical decisions.

English

Technical competencies
- Optical Design Knowledge: Depth and breadth of knowledge in optical engineering theory, design, modelling, and analysis. This may include optical system and lens design; optical modelling and optimization; tolerancing; wavefront, diffraction, image quality, polarization, fibre, or stray-light analysis; optical performance budgeting; radiometric or throughput modelling; coating design; detector performance modelling; and thermal and flexural analyses.
- Instrument Development, Integration and Delivery: Ability to contribute to the integration, testing, verification, and delivery of optical systems or scientific instrumentation. This may include optical alignment and integration; the use of optical metrology, alignment, and diagnostic equipment; development of alignment and test procedures; procurement of custom optical components and assemblies; performance characterization and testing; assembly, integration, and test (AIT) planning and execution; troubleshooting and root-cause analysis; acceptance testing; and interpretation of engineering drawings and optical specifications.
- Technical Problem Solving and Innovation: Ability to identify, analyze, and resolve complex technical challenges.
- Software, Modelling, and Analytical Tools: Knowledge of optical design, modelling, simulation, or data-analysis tools to support engineering decisions. (e.g., Zemax, Code V, FRED, MATLAB, Python, or equivalent tools).
- Technical Communication and Collaboration: Ability to communicate technical information and work effectively in multidisciplinary teams. This may include experience preparing and presenting technical documentation such as design reports, specifications, procurement documents and drawings, test plans and procedures, verification and validation reports, engineering analyses, design review materials, or technical recommendations.

About the Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre
We are Canada's gateway to the stars. At the Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre (HAA), we maintain and operate Canada's largest and most powerful observatories and represent the country in some of the world's leading astronomy initiatives. We are astronomy and astrophysics experts, conducting cutting-edge research, operating Canada's national observatories, providing extensive data management and analysis tools through our Canadian Astronomy Data Centre, supporting activities at international observatories and developing advanced astronomical instruments with industrial partners. More…
About DAO
HAA has a rare combination of staff involved in astronomy research, instrumentation design and development, engineering, data science and observatory support. Our facilities are located on two sites: Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory (DRAO) in Penticton, BC, Canada, and the Dominion Astrophysical Observatory (DAO) in Victoria, BC, Canada. HAA is a leading developer of instrumentation for Canada’s current and future ground- and space-based telescopes at radio through ultraviolet wavelengths, including major facilities such as the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), the Canada France Hawaii Telescope (CFHT), the International Gemini Observatory, and Canada’s flagship space telescope: Cosmological Advanced Survey Telescope for Optical and UV Research (CASTOR). Current and future ground- and space-based facilities from the UV to radio are represented in our instrumentation development, which includes radio astronomical instrumentation (receivers, correlators, antennas, etc) and UV/visible/near-IR instrumentation (spectrographs, imagers, adaptive optics, precision mechanics, photonics, detectors, etc). Our instrument development activities also include the development of pathfinder instruments and on-sky demonstrators. HAA is eager to diversify the fields of research represented at our Research Centre. The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) is an independent agency of the Government of Canada, dedicated to fostering public trust and confidence in Canada's financial system by rigorously regulating and supervising over 400 federally regulated financial institutions (FRFIs) and 1200 federally regulated pension plans (FRPPs). OSFI has offices located in 4 major cities across Canada: Ottawa, Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver. Safeguarding Canada’s Financial Future: Through diligent regulation and supervision of FRFIs and FRPPs, we ensure that these entities operate soundly and securely. Our proactive approach to risk management and early intervention safeguards the interests of depositors, policyholders, pension plan members, and beneficiaries. We remain committed to fostering public confidence and supporting the competitive and resilient nature of Canada's financial landscape. Our Mandate: Our mandate is to ensure the stability and integrity of Canada's financial system. We achieve this by: Maintaining Financial Soundness: Ensuring that FRFIs and FRPPs remain in sound financial condition. Safeguarding Against Threats: Ensuring that FRFIs protect themselves against threats to their integrity and security, including foreign interference. Proactive Intervention: Acting swiftly when issues arise, requiring FRFIs and FRPPs to implement necessary corrective measures without delay. Risk Management: Continuously monitoring and evaluating risks, promoting sound risk management practices among FRFIs and FRPPs. Our Approach: In fulfilling our mandate, we adopt a balanced approach: For FRFIs: We protect the rights and interests of depositors, policyholders, and financial institution creditors. At the same time, we recognize the need for FRFIs to compete effectively and take reasonable risks. For FRPPs: We safeguard the rights and interests of pension plan members, former members, and entitled beneficiaries. Join Us: Be part of a system that ensures financial stability and security for all Canadians. Learn more about our work and how you can contribute to a stronger Canadian financial future. OSFI has offices located in 4 major cities across Canada: Ottawa, Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver. Safeguarding Canada’s Financial Future: Through diligent regulation and supervision of FRFIs and FRPPs, we ensure that these entities operate soundly and securely. Our proactive approach to risk management and early intervention safeguards the interests of depositors, policyholders, pension plan members, and beneficiaries. We remain committed to fostering public confidence and supporting the competitive and resilient nature of Canada's financial landscape. Our Mandate: Our mandate is to ensure the stability and integrity of Canada's financial system. We achieve this by: Maintaining Financial Soundness: Ensuring that FRFIs and FRPPs remain in sound financial condition. Safeguarding Against Threats: Ensuring that FRFIs protect themselves against threats to their integrity and security, including foreign interference. Proactive Intervention: Acting swiftly when issues arise, requiring FRFIs and FRPPs to implement necessary corrective measures without delay. Risk Management: Continuously monitoring and evaluating risks, promoting sound risk management practices among FRFIs and FRPPs. Our Approach: In fulfilling our mandate, we adopt a balanced approach: For FRFIs: We protect the rights and interests of depositors, policyholders, and financial institution creditors. At the same time, we recognize the need for FRFIs to compete effectively and take reasonable risks. For FRPPs: We safeguard the rights and interests of pension plan members, former members, and entitled beneficiaries. Join Us: Be part of a system that ensures financial stability and security for all Canadians. Learn more about our work and how you can contribute to a stronger Canadian financial future. Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!6
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
We are looking for a Facility Leader to support the NRC’s Clean Energy Innovation Research Centre in Ottawa. The Facility Leader would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The successful candidate will work closely with researchers, facility operations staff, contractors, and vendors to maintain and advance the performance of NRC’s state-of-the-art research infrastructure.
The position plays a key role in ensuring that facilities are operated safely, efficiently and in alignment with project requirements, quality standards, budgets and client expectations.
If you’re a technically skilled, safety-minded professional, we’d like to hear from you.
The key responsibilities of the Facility Leader are the following:
- Manages assigned facilities, laboratories and physical resources to maximize utilization, safety, cost efficiency and reliability.
- Prepares annual budget requirements for facility operations and maintenance, managing assigned budgets, and supporting facility rate reviews and cost recovery.
- Oversees maintenance, calibration, troubleshooting, repair and installation of complex equipment, tools and instrumentation.
- Provides functional supervision and guidance to facility coordinators, including workload planning, scheduling, coaching and follow-up.
- Manages, oversees, or supports capital equipment acquisition and installation projects.
- Develops, reviews, or validates technical instructions, protocols, standard operating procedures and laboratory set-ups.
- Designs, plans, conducts and analyzes complex tests and experiments.
- Interacts with clients, project managers, researchers, engineers, vendors and internal service groups to coordinate work and resolve issues.
- Supports project planning, delivery, quality assurance, lessons learned and continuous improvement.
- Develops tools and procedures in support of implementing NRC’s safety-related programs, such as the hazard prevention program (HPP).
- Oversees or leads the implementation of specific health and safety programs.
- Promotes and adheres to NRC’s established health, safety, and environmental standards
- Participates in hazard identification, risk assessment, and mitigation planning.
- Provides appropriate on-the-job instruction and orientation to staff on HSE programs and procedures.
- Reports safety and environmental concerns and proposes improvements to enhance workplace safety and compliance.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Post-secondary education in a technical, engineering or scientific discipline related to the position from a recognized university.
A combination of a post-secondary degree in another field with significant work experience relevant to the position will be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Significant experience in managing activities in a research institute or industrial research facility or laboratory including scheduling of resources, equipment calibration, operation and maintenance, training and oversight of laboratory users, and purchasing and inventory control, preferably in a chemistry or materials processing related setting.
- Experience in setting up, maintaining, and optimizing research laboratories or facilities.
- Significant and recent experience in implementing environmental, health and safety programs in a laboratory environment.
- Experience working in multi-disciplinary teams and functional supervision of technical staff.
- Experience working with internal and external clients, vendors, suppliers, researchers, engineers, project managers and health and safety representatives.
- Experience coordinating small projects or capital projects, including planning, resourcing, risk management and delivery.
- Experience designing and implementing processes and procedures in a research facility environment including those related to health and safety.
- Experience providing advice and support to management related to facility investments and health and safety.
"Significant" refers to 2 to 6 years of experience and "recent" refers to experience obtained within the last 3 years.
Condition of employment
Reliability Status
For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
Language requirements
Bilingual Imperative CBC/CBC
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Knowledge of facility, laboratory or technical service operations, including equipment scheduling, maintenance, calibration, procurement and inventory management.
- Knowledge of research facility practices, quality assurance, standard operating procedures and good laboratory practices.
- Knowledge of occupational health and safety regulations, procedures and practices required to maintain a safe work environment.
- Ability to troubleshoot complex facility, laboratory and equipment issues and determine practical solutions.
- Ability to prepare technical reports, protocols, and standard operating procedures.
- Ability to use general office software and specialized domain-specific software.
- Ability to interpret technical drawings, instructions, specifications, manuals and scientific or technical literature.
- Ability to set priorities, manage time and adjust resources to meet changing operational and project demands.
- Knowledge of finance and procurement principles, policies and procedures would be considered an asset .
Behavioural competencies
- Technology extension - Communication (Level 3)
- Technology extension - Teamwork (Level 3)
- Technology extension - Conceptual and analytical ability (Level 3)
- Management services - Initiative (Level 3)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile(s): Management Services ; Technology Extension ;
View all competency profiles
Compensation
From $99,281 to $117,859 per annum.
In addition, the incumbent will receive the Bilingualism Bonus of $800 per year.
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
Notes
- In 2026, the NRC was chosen as one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, a National Capital Region Top Employer and Forbes Canada’s Best Employer.
- Relocation assistance will be determined in accordance with the NRC's directives.
- Must be able to travel locally, nationally and/or internationally.
- A valid driver's license and access to the use of a vehicle are required.
- A pre-qualified list may be established for similar positions for a one-year period.
- Preference will be given to Canadian Citizens and Permanent Residents of Canada. Please include citizenship information in your application.
- The incumbent must adhere to safe workplace practices at all times.
- We thank all those who apply, however only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

The position is classified as a RÉ-06 ($94,550 to $127,698 per annum – under review). JOB OVERVIEW As a Senior Architect, Design and Land use, you will assist in the implementation of the federal approvals process and other statutory requirements under the National Capital Act. You will provide architectural and urban design expertise and advice, including the evaluation of projects, conducting site inventories and research, and preparing urban design analysis and presentation material for the Division.
ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS: EDUCATION A degree from a recognized post-secondary institution in Architecture or an equivalent qualification recognized by the Canadian Architectural Certification Board for degrees obtained outside Canada.
ACCREDITATION Member of the Ontario Association of Architects or l’Ordre des Architectes du Québec or eligibility for membership.
EXPERIENCE Five (5) to eight (8) years of experience in each of the following criteria: • Managing complex real property projects from the planning through to the delivery phase in an environment characterized by competing demands: • Including the design and construction of new buildings, heritage building rehabilitation, utilities, civil engineering infrastructure, site and land development plans, security systems, structural components and interior fit-ups. • Leading multi-disciplinary complex real property project teams. • Providing strategic advice and briefings to clients, stakeholders and senior management related to complex real property projects.
KNOWLEDGE • Of Architecture and Urban Design. • Of building construction methods and sequence. • Of legislation, theories, and principles relevant to the planning and development of complex real property projects.
ABILITIES • To analyze and assess architectural and urban design proposals, plans and submissions throughout all phases of design development. • To work effectively in a professionally diverse high-efficiency environment, addressing politically sensitive issues with diplomacy and insight. • To respond to multiple, often conflicting demands, and to analyze and resolve complex and evolving issues, while making full use of limited resources.
COMPETENCIES • Demonstrating integrity and respect – Civility and well-being. • Thinking things through – Innovating through analysis and ideas. • Working effectively with others – Relationships and trust building. • Showing initiative and being action-oriented – Getting things done. ASSETS • Knowledge of the Federal Approvals framework: National Capital Act, Impact Assessment Act, Standards and Guidelines for the Conservation of Historic Places in Canada, Parks Canada & Canadian Heritage regulations and processes, Applicable Treasury Board Policies, Municipal regulations, Provincial regulations, National Building Code, LEED/ Green Globes, or similar certification processes. • Knowledge of procurement processes and contracts for architectural, engineering and construction related services. • Experience in Heritage Rehabilitation projects involving buildings from the 1800s and early 1900s, as well as a wide range of disciplines and historic construction methods in northern latitudes.
CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT • Possess or eligible to obtain Secret security clearance. • Linguistic profile: Bilingual BBB. • Position is in the National Capital Region. The person selected for this position must reside within a commutable distance from the workplace at 12 York Street, Ottawa, Ontario. • The National Capital Commission offers a hybrid and flexible work environment.
