About the Position Reporting to the Deputy Managing Director (DMD), Corporate Services (CS), the Departmental Business Coordinator plays a key role in supporting the Managing Director (MD), the DMD, and the department’s broader coordination and participation preparedness for the Executive Leadership Team (ELT). The position combines executive support with departmental coordination and business operations support, ensuring that day-to-day operations, governance logistics, and administrative processes enable CS leaders and the department to operate efficiently and effectively.
Working closely with the MD, DMD, Organizational Effectiveness Lead, and extended management team, the Departmental Business Coordinator plays a pivotal role in maintaining effective operational coordination, governance deliverables, communications, and management routines across CS.
The position also supports the MD in fulfilling the Bank’s Chief Security Officer (CSO) accountabilities, including coordination of the Bank’s participation in domestic and international security networks and the associated briefings, correspondence, agreements, commitments, and follow-up. The role requires exceptional organizational skills, sound judgement, attention to detail, and a service-oriented approach to support CS’s strategic execution and operational needs.
What You Will Do
Executive and Governance Coordination
- Manage the MD and DMD’s calendar and executive commitments, and coordinate priorities, schedules, and materials to support the readiness of both the MD and DMD for internal and external engagements.
- Coordinate, track, and ensure the completeness and timeliness of briefing materials, presentations, correspondence, and governance deliverables for Executive Council, ELT, Board, and committee meetings, in alignment with departmental priorities and content direction.
- Liaise with Executive and Legal Services (ELS), internal partners, external stakeholders, and CS business lines to ensure timely and accurate submission of materials and effective follow-up on executive and governance requirements.
- Anticipate the operational and logistical needs of the MD and DMD offices, manage incoming requests, coordinate inputs, and identify matters requiring leadership attention or escalation.
Departmental Operations and Logistics
- Oversee and continuously improve administrative and departmental coordination processes, ensuring CS support activities operate efficiently and effectively.
- Collaborate with business support resources across CS to ensure consistency, quality, and smooth operations across the department’s leadership offices.
- Collaborate with the Organizational Effectiveness Lead and other partners to manage logistics and materials for key departmental and ELT-related meetings and events, including scheduling, documentation, decisions, and follow-up.
- Lead or participate in departmental initiatives related to process optimization, document and records management, and administrative innovation, including the adoption of new tools and practices.
- Maintain and manage CS departmental SharePoint access permissions and filing systems, ensuring access, information handling, and records management comply with Bank standards, confidentiality requirements, and departmental needs.
- Support onboarding, offboarding, and other departmental HR and operational processes, identifying opportunities for improvement and escalating issues to management as required.
- Maintain tracking systems for governance deliverables, leadership decisions, commitments, and action items, ensuring visibility, accountability, follow-up, and timely completion in alignment with departmental priorities.
Collaboration, Communication, and Engagement
- Serve as a liaison between CS and other departments to clarify requirements, coordinate inputs, align deliverables, and support adherence to Bank governance and process standards.
- Foster strong relationships within CS, across the Bank, and with external security partners to support efficient collaboration, timely responses, and effective information flow.
- Support CS work environment, engagement, and departmental communication initiatives, including employee recognition, wellness, town halls, and social events.
- Manage travel arrangements and prepare expense claims for the MD and DMD in compliance with Bank policies.
What You Need to Succeed
- Demonstrated ability to manage complex workflows, competing priorities, and tight deadlines while maintaining attention to detail and quality.
- Strong analytical, planning, and problem-solving skills — able to synthesize information, identify key issues, and recommend effective solutions.
- Excellent relationship management and communication skills, with a proven ability to collaborate effectively across multiple teams and all levels of the organization.
- High degree of initiative, professionalism, and discretion, especially when handling sensitive or confidential information.
- Strong organizational and anticipatory skills, able to think several steps ahead and proactively address operational needs.
- Positive, “can-do” attitude with the confidence and flexibility to take ownership, adapt to change, and thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
- Demonstrates maturity, tact, and composure under pressure, and represents the offices of the MD and DMD with professionalism and credibility.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams), SharePoint, and Artificial Intelligence tools.
- Continuous improvement mindset, eager to learn, enhance existing processes, and contribute to a culture of excellence and collaboration.
Nice-to-have
- Experience supporting senior executives, such as a Managing Director, Chief Security Officer, or other senior executive equivalent, in a complex, fast-paced environment.
- Experience in corporate services, security, corporate governance, government, or another complex operational organization.
- Experience leading or supporting process improvement and administrative innovation initiatives.
Your Education and Experience This position requires a post-secondary diploma or degree in Business Administration, Communications, or a related field, and a minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience providing executive or departmental coordination support. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Innovative Mindset We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement T he Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional). If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.
What you need to know
- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents
- Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Reliability
- Relocation assistance may be provided, if required
- Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.
Hybrid Work Model The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.
What you can expect from us This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit A great deal to consider .
- Salaries are based on qualifications and experience and typically range from $74,981 to $88,213 (job grade 14)
- The Bank offers an incentive for successfully meeting expectations at 5 to 7% of your base salary. The Bank offers additional performance pay (3%) for those who exceed expectations. Exceptional performers who far exceed expectations may be eligible for higher performance pay.
- Flexible and comprehensive benefits so you can choose the level of health, dental disability and life and/or accident insurance coverage that meets your needs

- Indexed, defined-benefit pension

About the role
This role sits at the intersection of new mandate delivery and financial management modernization. Your work will help ensure that new supervision mandates are financially sound, transparent, and sustainable, while also contributing to the modernization of Financial Services processes, insights, and advisory models.
Reporting to the Assistant Director, Financial Management – Supervisory Mandate, within the Strategic & Financial Advice (SFA) business line of Financial Services (FIN), the Senior Financial Management Specialist plays a critical role in supporting the implementation and ongoing delivery of the Bank’s new mandates, including Retail Payment Supervision, Stablecoin, and Consumer‑driven banking.
The role combines advanced financial analysis, costing, and governance expertise with mandate implementation and operational enablement responsibilities. The successful candidate will lead the development and execution of costing and cost-recovery approaches, oversee the integrity of financial and supervisory data supporting fee and assessment methodologies, and contribute to the modernization and streamlining of SFA processes, practices, and financial management frameworks.
Specifically, you will:
- Lead Financial Planning & Performance: Drive annual and multi-year financial planning, forecasting, and performance management for new mandates, and projects to support departmental and corporate priorities.
- Develop and maintain costing models: Support the implementation and ongoing operation of cost‑recovery processes, including fee and assessment methodologies aligned with legislation, policy, and audit requirements.
- Deliver Strategic Analysis & Oversight: Provide forward-looking financial and operational analyses, oversee business cases and funding proposals, and ensure alignment with governance frameworks and value-for-money objectives.
- Enable the effective delivery of priorities: Supporting business owners through stakeholder engagement, research, process reviews, reporting improvements, financial enhancements, and governance and policy updates to advance the finance modernization agenda.
- Champion Modernization & Best Practices: Promote innovation with discipline, strengthening financial stewardship and compliance through digital finance, analytics, and AI, translating external trends into actionable recommendations, improving the timeliness and usefulness of financial information.
What you need to succeed
- Strategic Financial Expertise: Extensive experience in financial management, costing, budgeting, and performance analysis, with the ability to provide strategic insights and support executive decision-making.
- Costing & Funding Frameworks: Proven experience leading or advising on the design and implementation of cost-recovery frameworks, ideally within regulatory, supervisory, or public-sector environments
- Financial Governance & Controls: Strong knowledge of accounting standards, financial controls, governance, and compliance requirements.
- Analytical Excellence & Adaptability: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, interpret complex data, and adapt to emerging finance technologies, including automation and AI-enabled tools.
- Executive Communication & Collaboration: Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively across senior leadership, teams, and disciplines.

2481097.text:
Data Scientist, Economics & AI
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
What you need to know
We are seeking a Data Scientist with expertise in economics, quantitative modelling, and emerging AI technologies to support economic research, policy analysis, and data-driven decision-making at the Bank of Canada. You will apply data science, machine learning (ML), artificial intelligence (AI), and quantitative methods to challenging economic and research problems, helping economists and researchers make effective use of modern analytical techniques and technologies.
Reporting to the Assistant Director, Data Science, within the Department of Data and Digital Services (DDS), you will work at the intersection of economics, data science, and emerging technologies. Working closely with economists, researchers, business clients, and technology teams, you will develop analytical solutions, AI-enabled tools, and quantitative models that improve research, forecasting, policy analysis, and decision-making.
This role offers an opportunity to apply modern data science and AI approaches to meaningful economic and policy problems while contributing to the development of reusable analytical capabilities. You will work on high-impact initiatives, experiment with emerging methods and technologies, and help modernize analytical and research workflows across the organization.
What you will do
As a Data Scientist, you will contribute to analytical initiatives that support economic research, forecasting, policy analysis, and evidence-based decision-making. Drawing on your knowledge of economics, quantitative methods, and data science, you will work across the analytical lifecycle to develop practical, high-quality solutions.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Designing, developing, testing, and implementing statistical, econometric, ML, and AI models to address economic, research, and policy questions.
- Developing AI-enabled applications, analytical tools, reusable components, and data products that improve research, modelling, forecasting, and analytical workflows.
- Applying LLMs, generative AI, and emerging AI approaches to practical research and analytical use cases, including prototyping, experimentation, evaluation, and implementation.
- Working with structured and unstructured data, including preparing, transforming, validating, exploring, and analyzing datasets for modelling and research.
- Collaborating with economists, researchers, business stakeholders, and technology teams to understand analytical needs and translate them into effective data science solutions.
- Communicating analytical findings, methodologies, assumptions, limitations, and results clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Applying sound practices for reproducible research, model validation, responsible AI, explainability, documentation, and analytical quality.
- Exploring and evaluating emerging AI, ML, and analytical techniques and applying them where they can improve economic analysis, research methods, forecasting, or productivity.
What you need to succeed
You are a collaborative and curious data scientist who enjoys using quantitative methods and technology to solve challenging analytical problems. You combine strong technical skills with an understanding of economic and research contexts and can translate analytical questions into practical solutions.
You are comfortable working independently on complex assignments while collaborating closely with economists, researchers, data scientists, and technology specialists. You are an analytical problem solver and continuous learner who can adapt methods and tools as technologies and research needs evolve.
You bring:
- Hands-on experience designing and delivering econometric and economic models using statistical, ML, and AI techniques to support economic research, policy analysis, forecasting, and other quantitative applications.
- Strong knowledge of quantitative methods, with experience in areas such as econometrics, forecasting, statistical modelling, machine learning, or AI.
- Experience applying large language models (LLMs), generative AI, or other emerging AI technologies to analytical, research, or decision-support use cases.
- Proficiency with programming languages or analytical computing environments such as Python, MATLAB, R, or similar tools.
- Experience working with modern analytics platforms such as Azure, Databricks, or equivalent environments.
- Experience working across the data science lifecycle, including data preparation, exploration, modelling, evaluation, and implementation.
- Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to explain analytical approaches and results to technical and non-technical audiences.
Nice-to-Have
Experience in one or more of the following areas:
- Economic research, forecasting, policy analysis, or quantitative economic modelling.
- Time-series analysis, econometric estimation, or simulation methods.
- Building AI-enabled analytical applications or research tools.
- Working with economists, researchers, business partners, and technology teams in multidisciplinary environments.
Education and Experience
This position requires a master’s degree or higher in economics, econometrics, statistics, mathematics, data science, computer science, or a related quantitative discipline, along with a minimum of four years of relevant experience applying quantitative methods, including statistical modelling, econometrics, ML, AI, or related analytical techniques, in support of economic research, policy analysis, forecasting, or evidence-based decision-making. An equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may also be considered.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. Although the position language requirement is English or French essential, we do encourage everyone to improve their second language proficiency for future career growth and to contribute towards fostering a bilingual environment.

Who we are

Visit our career page at NSERC to learn more about why you should join our agency.

We are seeking a Program Technical Support Officer to support the implementation and advancement of program delivery tools and workflows and prepare for transition towards a new modern, user‑centric Grants Management Solution leveraging Microsoft Power Platform, Dynamics 365, Dataverse, and Azure services.
As a Program Technical Support Officer , your responsibilities will include:

2481242.text:
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2025 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
Are you passionate about safe and responsible AI? Do you want to be part of a pioneering team shaping how AI systems are evaluated, measured, and deployed safely? Do you want your work to have a real impact for Canada and Canadians? If so, we want to meet you! We are seeking a mid‑career RCO‑04 to establish and lead the NRC’s AI Safety Lab, a new capability funded by the Canadian AI Safety Institute (CAISI) and dedicated to evaluating the safety of advanced AI systems. You will be part of a pioneering team conducting rigorous AI safety evaluations and translating technical results into actionable tools, guidance, and recommendations for AI practitioners and policymakers across government and beyond.
Under the guidance of the Principal Advisor for AI Safety, and as part of the Chief Digital Research Officer’s team, you will play a central role in building and operating a scalable AI safety evaluation infrastructure. In collaboration with leading experts from our Digital Technologies Research Centre, you will design, execute, and monitor advanced evaluations at scale on frontier AI models, and contribute to cutting‑edge AI safety research carried out by the NRC in collaboration with CAISI partners nationally and internationally.
Key Responsibilities include:
- Establish and manage a multidisciplinary team of AI safety specialists forming the lab.
- Build and leverage state-of-the-art model evaluation infrastructure and frameworks.
- Work with AI safety researchers from the NRC and CAISI partners in designing, running and documenting AI safety evaluations.
- Establish and steward standardized, reproducible safety evaluation protocols.
- Develop and curate new AI safety benchmarks.
- Translate technical findings into practical solutions and advice, such as new tools for evaluators/developers, or recommendations to policy makers.
The ideal candidate would have:
- A track record of building and managing AI teams.
- Hands-on experience evaluating frontier AI models using safety evaluation frameworks (e.g., Inspect, Moonshot).
- A strong background in compute cluster operations and scalable ML infrastructure.
- Experience designing reproducible evaluation protocols and benchmarks.
- Experience translating research into practical tools, guidance, or policy recommendations.
- The ability to collaborate across research, government, and international partners.
- Strong analytical judgment and initiative.
- Clear communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Master’s degree from a recognized university in Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science or Engineering, or closely related to the position.
Equivalency
In lieu of a master degree, a combination of a Bachelor’s degree with at least 2 years of directly relevant professional experience in applied AI or AI evaluation may be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
You must meet the essential experience criteria and at least two of the Specialised Experience to move forward in this process.
Essential Experience
- Recent* experience leading or managing technical teams in an AI/ML, data analytics, or digital technologies environment.
- Recent* experience evaluating, benchmarking, or red-teaming AI models (open-source or closed-source) or AI systems.
- Experience in managing AI/ML or data analytics projects for government or industry clients.
- Experience developing Python-based tooling and automation for ML/AI workflows.
- Experience in documenting experimental AI results through technical reports, internal documentation, or scientific publications.
*Recent is defined as within the last 3 years.
Specialised Experience
- Experience with red-teaming workflows, adversarial testing, or stress-testing of AI systems (including agentic systems).
- Experience with compute clusters and job orchestration (e.g., SLURM).
- Experience with ML experiment tracking tools (e.g., MLflow, Weights & Biases).
- Experience developing or curating AI benchmark datasets and associated documentation (e.g., through HuggingFace).
- Experience translating AI research into practical tools, guidance, or policy recommendations.
- Experience conducting AI projects with researchers or through international collaboration.
Condition of employment
Secret clearance
A thorough security clearance process will be applied.
For a Secret Clearance, verification of background information over a period of 10 years is required. Individuals must have lived in Canada for a sufficient period of time to enable the security screening process.
Language requirements
Bilingual Imperative CBC/CBC
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Ability to lead the development of reproducible evaluation protocols and benchmarks for frontier AI models and systems.
- Ability to communicate complex technical findings clearly to researchers, government stakeholders, and policy audiences.
- Knowledge of AI safety concepts, risk taxonomies, or governance frameworks (e.g., TBS guidelines, NIST AI Risk Management Framework) and their connection to technical evaluation.
- Ability to design and oversee scalable AI evaluation infrastructure across on-premises and cloud environments.
- Knowledge of AI safety evaluation frameworks (e.g., Inspect AI, Moonshot) and their application to frontier model assessment.
- Ability to make sound technical decisions when configuring evaluations across different model types, balancing compute budgets, reproducibility, and result validity.
- Ability to manage and prioritize competing technical workstreams across a multidisciplinary team.
- Knowledge of agentic AI architectures and how design choices such as tool access, memory, and planning affect safety-relevant behaviours.
- Ability to design experiment tracking and data management workflows that support reproducibility across multiple researchers and evaluation campaigns.
Behavioural competencies
- Research - Communication (Level 3)
- Research - Results orientation (Level 3)
- Supervisor - Client focus (Level 2)
- Supervisor - Teamwork (Level 3)
- Supervisor - Organizational/environmental awareness (Level 2)
- Management services - Conceptual and analytical ability (Level 3)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile(s): Management Services ; Research ; Supervisor
View all competency profiles
Compensation
This position is classified as a Research Council Officer (RCO), a group that is unique to the NRC. The intent of this hiring action is to staff this position at the RCO-3 to RCO-4 level, which is a mid-career level position with a salary range of $119,688 to $168,192 .
NOTE: Please note that the full RO/RCO salary scale has five levels. Salary determination will be based on a review of the candidate’s expertise, outcomes and impacts of their previous work experience relative to the requirements of the level. As such, the initial salary could be within another level of the RO/RCO salary scale (i.e. above or below the intended level for this position).
In addition, the incumbent will receive the Bilingualism Bonus of $800 per year.
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
​
Notes
- Relocation assistance will be determined in accordance with the NRC's directives.
- ​A pre-qualified list may be established for similar positions for a one year period.
- Preference will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents of Canada. Please include citizenship information in your application.
- The incumbent must adhere to safe workplace practices at all times.
- We thank all those who apply, however only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

The House of Commons Administration delivers outstanding services to Members of Parliament and their employees in support of parliamentary democracy. Our success is made possible by our talented and dedicated workforce. We value diversity in all its forms and recognize that everyone has valuable contributions to make and the potential for individual growth. If you dream of joining an organization that is small enough for you to be noticed, but big enough to provide you with a meaningful career, then we want to hear from you!
Job Description
The House of Commons’ Parliamentary Precinct Operations is currently looking to staff the Refinisher (Furniture) position.
This position requires on-site presence five (5) days per week.
The Refinisher Apprentice is responsible for assisting in the refinishing and restoration of furniture and other pieces in the House of Commons, and learning the various specialized techniques, materials and tools used in the delivery of services to clients of the Parliamentary Precinct.
The Apprentice role is a professional development position designed to support progression toward full qualification as a Refinisher. Through a structured apprenticeship training program, employees gradually acquire the skills, knowledge, and experience required to achieve full qualification of the trade. Subject to operational requirements, an opportunity to be appointed to a Refinisher position may be offered upon successful completion of the training program and demonstration of the required qualifications.

You'll be part of a collaborative, supportive team where creativity and camaraderie are celebrated. This role goes beyond traditional refurbishment - it's an opportunity to work on historically significant elements. In our family-like atmosphere, you'll have the opportunity to fully express your creativity while mastering a specialized trade, making each project a blend of innovation and tradition. Employment at Parliament not only opens doors to professional growth and skill enhancement, it also fosters a deep sense of pride and accomplishment as a valued member of our workforce.

Lock/Bridge Operator I (GL-MOC-05)
Lock/Bridge Operator I (GL-MOC-05) Parks Canada careers: where passion meets purpose . You might be wondering why you would come to work for the Parks Canada Agency? To join a team of passionate people who care about the protection and presentation of Canada’s outstanding natural and cultural resources through a system of national parks, national marine conservation areas and national historic sites in all regions of Canada. Parks Canada is a federal government agency responsible for the protection and presentation of Canada’s outstanding natural and cultural resources through a system of national parks, national marine conservation areas and national historic sites in all regions of Canada. The Quebec Waterways unit manages five historic canals stretching from Montreal to the St. Lawrence, Richelieu and Outaouais rivers. These canals are situated in three important tourism regions in the province and also have numerous collaborations with important stakeholders and partners. • Carillon Canal National Historic Site • Chambly Canal National Historic Site • Lachine Canal National Historic Site • Saint-Ours Canal National Historic Site • Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue Canal National Historic Site ⏰ Closing date: November 30, 2026 - 11:59 p.m., Eastern Time We encourage you to submit your application promptly, as applications may be reviewed on an ongoing basis. Who is eligible: Persons residing within 75 km of Carillon Canal (Quebec), Chambly Canal (Quebec), Lachine Canal (Quebec), Saint-Ours Canal (Quebec) or Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue Canal (Quebec). Duties Do you like manual work, being outside and seeing concretely the fruit of your efforts? This position is for you! The work of a lock and bridge attendant requires rigor, resourcefulness, and good physical fitness. You will be responsible for operating locks and/or bridges*, maintaining grounds, structures and equipment, and providing courteous service to users in accordance with Parks Canada standards. The position is physically demanding and mainly works outside (more than 10 hours a day, exposure to sun, rain and bad weather). You will walk long distances on various terrains, use stairs or ladders and could lift loads up to 20 kg. Your main tasks: Paint, clean, weed, mow, empty bins and maintain sanitary facilities. Remove debris from the water, clean bird droppings and keep the area safe and clean. Answer visitors' questions and ensure compliance with regulations. Use various tools and equipment (lawnmower, pressure washer, drill, boat, golf cart, etc.). Perform certain administrative tasks using computer tools. *The locks of the Canal-de-Chambly have mechanisms that are operated manually. Join us and contribute concretely to the functioning of Quebec’s waterways, while working in a unique natural environment! Intent of the process The purpose of this process is to potentially fill twelve (12) term, full-time and/or part-time positions for the period from May to October 2027. Successful candidates may be offered an annual contract renewal. 📍Workplace: Carillon Canal (Quebec), Chambly Canal (Quebec), Lachine Canal (Quebec), Saint-Ours Canal (Quebec) or Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue Canal (Quebec). This process can also be used to create a list of qualified candidates for similar positions with different job statuses, security levels and language profiles in the same location or elsewhere across the country. 💼 Positions to fill: 12 💰 H ourly range: $ 28.61 to $31.11 ( salary under review ). 🎓 E ducation : Secondary diploma or acceptable combination of education, training and experience relevant to the position. Degree equivalency 💬 Language requirements : French essential or Bilingual Imperative (--B/--B). ✨Experiences: Experience providing customer service. Experience in general maintenance of buildings, grounds, or equipment*. Experience using work-related computer software (e.g.: Microsoft Excel, Power Point, Word, Outlook, etc.). * Experience in the general maintenance of buildings, grounds, or equipment includes, but is not limited to, performing tasks such as: carrying out minor repair and maintenance work; performing cleaning and maintenance of indoor and outdoor areas; maintaining grounds and landscaped areas; operating a variety of tools, equipment (e.g., lawn mowers, string trimmers) and light machinery; performing painting work; and ensuring the cleanliness, safety, and overall good condition of facilities and equipment. 🛠️Asset Experiences: Experience working on a canal. Experience in the field of fluvial navigation. ⚙️Abilities: Ability to communicate orally. 🤝 Personal sutabilities: Demonstrates integrity and respect. Demonstrates thinking things through. Works efficiently with others. Shows initiative and being action oriented. 📝Conditions of employment: Obtain and maintain the reliability check rating. Hold and maintain a valid Class 5 driver’s licence recognized by the applicable province or territory. Obtain a Pleasure Craft Operator Card within one month of hire, at the expense of the employee. The Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) is Canada’s largest funder of science and engineering. The Deputy Director is providing the focal point for the Division’s corporate secretariat operations, governance and compliance activities; ensuring delivery of corporate operations, legislative and policy compliance of the organization; developing and maintaining frameworks related to governance, Access to Information and Privacy (ATIP), funding eligibility and terms & conditions; coordinating special projects and studies and consulting widely with internal and external stakeholders to inform decision-making. The role
NRC Construction is implementing the “Platform to Decarbonize the Construction Sector at Scale” (NRC Platform) to accelerate and scale up new technologies to help transition the Canadian construction sector towards decarbonization and contribute to the emerging low-carbon economy. It will also establish new codes, standards, specifications, and guidelines to position the sector to achieve its 2050 greenhouse gas (GHG) carbon reduction targets. These investments will help spur the growth of Canada’s clean technology sector and help achieve Canada’s international commitments to reduce GHG emissions.
Federal Budget 2022 proposed that the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) receive $183.2 million over seven years (2022-29) to transition the Canadian construction sector towards decarbonization and enhanced productivity. The funding will support the implementation of a NRC Platform consisting of three integrated and synergistic Programs to advance the transformation of Canada’s construction sector and contribute to the emerging low-carbon economy.
The Digitalization and Productivity Challenge Program (approximately $70M over seven years) will drive transformation to digitalized and automated construction and accelerate the adoption of novel off-site construction methodologies. The program will support lower construction time and cost, while improving sector innovation potential, productivity and the pace at which low-carbon solutions can be deployed in new and retrofit construction projects.
The program will be specifically designed to harness and focus Canada’s research and innovation capacity in industry, academia and research-based OGDs to fill key knowledge gaps (e.g. guidelines, standard methods of data exchange, standards development, integration of off-site manufacturing design and practices for deconstruction, productivity quantification, among others) to realize the potential benefits of off-site construction and automation. It will seek to implement processes to optimize the designs and compliance of buildings and infrastructure, leverage benefits of advanced manufacturing processes including modular off-site construction (MOC), and advance development of low-carbon retrofit solutions that lever performance-based design.
The role (continued)
Research and development motivated by this program will provide the technical solutions needed for early adopters in the private sector to uniformly implement integrated digital construction practices throughout the asset lifecycle and across the sector. Demonstration projects with early adopters will showcase the value of digitalized construction solutions, which will help increase sector productivity, reduce time and cost, when coupled with a shift from prescriptive to performance-based solutions.
The primary responsibility of the RO is to support the goals of NRC’s Platform to Decarbonize the Construction Sector at Scale, and other Programs served by the Intelligent Building Operations unit. These goals require research of international calibre and the development and application of advanced technologies to support the needs of our numerous industry partners. The RO works in a team environment with researchers and technical experts in world-class facilities. Activities also include the development of proposals for new research initiatives, effective project management, support to the enhancement of facilities, and communication of research plans and results to stakeholders.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
A PhD in Construction Management or Industrial Engineering with an emphasis on Construction Value Chain.
A PhD in a related field, combined with significant experience in measuring and analyzing construction productivity/efficiency or related research may also be considered.
Education related to construction supply chain valuation, life cycle environmental and/or cost assessment maybe considered an asset.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Experience in conducting research on construction productivity and/or conducting comparative studies on productivity/performance data to enhance construction productivity (time, cost, environmental impacts) through applications such as MOC, IPD, BIM or other construction practices. Experience related to comparative analysis of MOC vs conventional construction may be considered an asset.
- Experience in construction supply chain logistics/network optimization, including areas such as transportation systems, operations research, or stochastic optimization.
- Experience in research proposal development, working with diverse stakeholders and multi-disciplinary teams, project execution, documentation, and reporting.
Experience in construction (on-site and/or off-site) automation (e.g. automated data acquisition, automated collision avoidance, automated manufacturing technologies and processes may be considered an asset.
Experience in business development, marketing activities, and/or the development of partnerships and collaborations may be considered an asset.
Condition of employment
Reliability Status
For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Ability to apply knowledge to research and technology development projects. Knowledge in leading/participating in research project planning, work scheduling, costing, proposal development, and engaging with stakeholders.
- Advanced knowledge in construction performance measurement frameworks and metrics focusing on productivity improvement and/or carbon reduction.
- Advanced knowledge of productivity enhancements and/or emissions reductions through non-conventional construction practices such as leveraging MOC, IPD, Digital Tools/Solutions, AI.
- Knowledge of comparison research for construction performance and productivity of:
- different construction practices, technologies, processes, and/or materials; and/or planned vs actual outputs.
Knowledge in benchmarking construction performance and productivity may be considered an asset.
Knowledge in multiple MOC practices (e.g. volumetric modular, open/closed panels, mass timber, precast) may be considered an asset.
Behavioural competencies
- Research - Creative thinking (Level 2)
- Research - Communication (Level 2)
- Research - Partnering (Level 2)
- Research - Teamwork (Level 2)
- Research - Results orientation (Level 2)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile(s): Research ;
View all competency profiles
Compensation
The intent of this hiring action is to staff this position at the RO-2-4 level, which is a mid-career level position with a salary range of $83,985 to $168,192 .
NOTE: Please note that the full RO/RCO salary scale has five levels. Salary determination will be based on a review of the candidate’s expertise, outcomes and impacts of their previous work experience relative to the requirements of the level. As such, the initial salary could be within another level of the RO/RCO salary scale (i.e. above or below the intended level for this position).
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.

The role
We are looking for an experienced and dynamic Director, Co-Innovation Programs for the Industrial Research Assistance Program. The Director would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
Working with clients and partners, the National Research Council Canada provides strategic research, innovation support, scientific and technical services to develop and deploy solutions to meet Canada’s current and future industrial and societal needs.
The NRC Industrial Research Assistance Program (NRC IRAP) is a critical component of the NRC with a clear mandate to support SMEs’ growth through innovation. The NRC IRAP has professional field staff that work with clients and give strategic advice to assist the firms with their overall development. The NRC IRAP also can provide financial support to these SMEs’ innovation projects.
As Director, Co-Innovation working closely with your Director General, other Director(s) Co-Innovation and with senior managers and executives across the organization, you will use your own STI network domestically and internationally, understanding and relationships to design and execute strategies and agreements that are important to NRC and to Canada. As a natural leader, you will energize and build a strong team to serve the corporation and you will negotiate with diverse groups within NRC and around the globe to bring ideas and strategies to life. Committed to excellence, you will use your initiative to make recommendations for continuous improvement project management practices and tools.

Reference number: RF-17607
About CSE
The Communications Security Establishment (CSE) is Canada’s agency responsible for foreign signals intelligence, cyber operations and cyber security. Learn more about our mission , and what it means to work in a security and intelligence field .
CSE is committed to fostering a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion. This isn’t just an ideal, it’s crucial to our mission. Find out about our workplace culture , including our diversity and inclusion initiatives.
Become part of our team and you’ll understand why CSE is the most important organization you’ve never heard of (YouTube) .
Job summary
Join the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security , a part of CSE, and contribute to projects that help strengthen Canada's cyber security posture and support the safety and security of Canadians.
You will work as part of a collaborative development team responsible for the administration, development, and enhancement of a Microsoft (MS) Dynamics 365 and Dataverse platform. As a MS Dynamics 365 developer you will design and implement innovative solutions, develop integrations with enterprise systems, automate business processes, and help deliver reliable services that support the mission of the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.
Whether you are an entry-level, intermediate, or experienced developer, you will have the opportunity to work on meaningful projects, expand your technical expertise, and contribute to a culture of continuous learning, innovation, and knowledge-sharing.
Key duties
- Development duties: develop Microsoft (MS) Dynamics 365 and solution maintenance and configuration develop and maintain custom plugins and automations for Microsoft Dynamics 365 develop integrations and custom components for Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Dataverse, including data lake synchronization jobs, AI-enabled Model Context Protocol servers and tools and API integrations develop data migration tools for migrating customer data into MS Dynamics 365 build MS Dynamics 365 dashboards, workflows and reports perform code reviews and ensure adherence to development standards
- Requirements gathering and user support duties: participate in requirements gathering create and maintain documentation on procedures and governance provide support to users for data entry and distribution lists administrate MS Dynamics 365, including creation of user accounts and maintenance provide or participate in demos or user training
Salary
To find out more about our salary scale, vacation allowances and benefits (health, dental and pension plans, etc.) visit the Compensation page on our website.
Area of selection
Open to Canadian citizens.
Location
The majority of our jobs are in Ottawa, Ontario. CSE has two accessible facilities . Flexible work arrangements, including telework for a portion of the work week, may be possible.
Conditions of employment
A valid Enhanced Top Secret ( ETS ) security clearance is a condition of employment that must be met before an offer can be made.
More information about our hiring and security processes can be found on our website.
Essential qualifications
In order to be considered, your cover letter must clearly explain how you meet the following education and experience requirements.
Education
You must have either one of the following:
- a professional certification, college diploma or university degree in a field related to the position, such as (but not limited to) Software Engineering Technician, Computer System Technology, Computer Science, Engineering (e.g. Computer, Software, Electrical), Mathematics; or
- a secondary school diploma and relevant experience in a field related to the position (as above).
Note: The educational program must be recognized in Canada, and you must be able to provide proof of education credentials. Students graduating within the next twelve months are eligible to apply.
Experience
- Front-end web development experience using HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
- Experience developing and customizing enterprise applications such as Microsoft Dynamics 365, Microsoft Power Platform, Dataverse, Salesforce, or similar platforms.
- Experience developing software solutions using programming languages such as C#, HTML, Python, CSS, and JavaScript.
- Experience providing technical support, troubleshooting, or advice on enterprise systems.
Official language requirements
English essential
- English essential means that the position requires the knowledge of English only.
Find out more about the language requirements of positions.
Competencies
The following core, technical and functional competencies will be assessed at a later date. You do not need to include information about them in your application.
Core Competencies (For all levels)
- Accountability and Professional Excellence
- Critical Thinking and Judgement
- Initiative
- Teamwork and Collaboration
Technical Competencies (For all levels)
- Application Development
- Knowledge of IT
- Web Design and Development
- Knowledge of the Software Development Process (for UNMA-08 and UNMA-09 only)
Functional Competencies (for UNMA-09)
- Project Management
Assets
Assets are “nice-to-have” expertise and skills we’re interested in. Your application will not be rejected if you do not meet or possess these qualifications. However, if you do have them, they may be used to identify which team you could best complement.
Please demonstrate on your application if you meet or possess the asset experience listed below.
Asset experience
- For the UNMA-07 or UNMA-08 (entry and intermediate levels) asset experience include: Microsoft (MS) Dynamics 365 or on-prem administration or development experience experience with RESTful service development experience in Power Platform, Canvas App building, Power Automate, Azure web apps, Functions, or containerized applications experience utilizing Cloud technology experience developing cloud-based solutions using Microsoft Azure or similar cloud technologies experience using and maintaining releases and deployments with Azure DevOps experience using source control like Git experience with user experience (UX) principles, usability, accessibility, and interface design best practices experience developing custom plug-ins, workflows, or extensions for MS Dynamics 365/Dataverse
- For the UNMA-09 (experienced level) assets also include: experience designing and developing integrations between enterprise applications using APIs and web services experience with AI-enabled solutions or Model Context Protocol (MCP) services experience developing data integration, synchronization, or migration solutions between enterprise systems
Operational requirements
Overtime and standby duty may be required.
How to apply
You may submit your candidacy online by selecting “Apply” at the top or bottom of this page.
If you cannot apply online or have a disability preventing you from applying online, please inform us by email at careers-carrieres@cse-cst.gc.ca prior to the closing date of this hiring process.
Important information
We ask you to not discuss your application with others (including on social media) besides your partner, or close family members - who should also be reminded about the need to be discreet.
Assessments of candidates are conducted in the official language of their choice.
To address CSE’s current representation gaps, priority may be given to persons who self-declare as belonging to one, or more, designated employment equity groups: women; Indigenous peoples, including First Nations who are status, or registered and non-status, or non-registered, Inuit and Métis; persons with disabilities, including people with a mental health condition and neurodivergent people; and persons from racial or ethnic groups.
Please note the Employment Equity Act , which is under review, uses the terminology Aboriginal peoples and visible minorities.
CSE offers an assessment process that will accommodate any reasonable measures you require to be assessed in a fair and equitable manner. Those measures are available to all candidates during our processes. Information you provide will be addressed confidentially.
The level of competence demonstrated in the various assessments will be used to determine your qualifications for the UNMA-07, UNMA-08 or UNMA-09 level.
All communications with CSE relating to this process, including email messages and telephone conversations, may be used in the assessment of qualifications.
The intent of this process is to fill vacant positions at CSE. The process may also be used to establish a pool of qualified candidates which could be used to staff similar or identical positions with various tenures.
Due to the nature of CSE’s mandate certain roles may expose employees to content that is difficult to process. Mental health is a priority at CSE and if any personnel feel they require assistance to preserve their mental wellbeing, they have access to services, tools and other resources to help them in both their personal and professional lives.
Please note that in an effort to maintain balance between employee development and business needs, candidates who are hired at CSE must remain in their substantive position for a minimum of twelve (12) months subject to operational requirements.
We thank you for your interest in CSE. However, only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

2481950.text:
About the role
Join the Insurance Business Development team, in the Senior Specialist, Client Relations position. In this role, you will draw on your extensive knowledge of homeowner mortgage loan insurance (HO MLI) policy and lender operations to provide strategic thought leadership, advice and enablement to the National Key Account Manager and regional teams. You will support the development, communication and cascade of lender strategic plans into coordinated regional activities, serving as a key liaison with internal partners to align priorities, resolve operational issues and strengthen the client experience.
This is a temporary position with a duration of 18 months.
What you'll do:
- Support the National Key Account Manager in developing and monitoring lender strategic plans aligned with corporate priorities, client needs and market intelligence, and coordinate their cascade into regional engagement plans, activities and key performance indicators.
- Provide strategic thought leadership by synthesizing lender insights, business performance, client feedback and competitive trends into actionable recommendations that inform account priorities, business development opportunities and the client experience.
- Provide guidance on HO MLI policies, products and operational requirements, working with internal subject-matter experts to support consistent interpretation, address complex inquiries and identify process or program improvements.
- Liaise with lender head office and operational contacts to understand mortgage origination and insurance workflows, identify recurring needs and coordinate solutions that support consistent national practices and effective service delivery.
- Coordinate planning, business reviews and follow-up with the National Key Account Manager and regional teams, clarifying actions, responsibilities and timelines, monitoring progress and escalating risks or barriers to implementation.
- Serve as a liaison with internal policy, underwriting, operations and other business partners to align lender initiatives, resolve complex or sensitive issues and communicate client needs and emerging risks.
- Develop coordinated communications, briefing materials, tools and training that equip the National Key Account Manager and regional teams to communicate lender priorities, implement initiatives and share knowledge consistently.
- Provide coaching and advisory support to national and regional teams, sharing HO MLI expertise and best practices and bringing regional feedback into national planning to strengthen execution and continuous improvement.
What you should have:
- An undergraduate degree in a field relevant to real estate (e.g., business administration, finance, economics, or commerce), or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
- A minimum of seven (7) years of relevant experience in client relationships and operations.
- Comprehensive knowledge of HO MLI policies, products and operational requirements, and strong understanding of lender mortgage origination, underwriting and insurance processes.
- Strong strategic thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to synthesize client insights, market intelligence, and performance data into practical advice and recommendations.
- Superior written and verbal communication skills in both official languages (English and French), including the ability to influence and negotiate; able to deliver clear, persuasive presentations and gain acceptance of proposals or plans.
- The ability to build effective relationships with lender contacts and internal partners, facilitate cross-functional collaboration, and provide coaching and advisory support to national and regional teams.
- Superior problem-solving skills and sound judgment in resolving complex policy and operational issues and identifying risks requiring escalation.
- Strong planning and coordination skills, with the ability to translate strategic priorities into actionable plans and manage concurrent initiatives in ambiguous, fast-paced environments.
It would be great if you also had:
- An MBA, PMP, Lean Six Sigma designation, or experience in residential mortgage lending, national account planning or operational improvement initiatives.
- Extensive working knowledge and experience with CRM and Dynamics 365.

Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
We are looking for a Manager of Workplace Programs to support our Human Resources Branch. The Manager of Workplace Programs would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity. You will lead a work unit responsible for leading NRC programs and initiatives in the areas of Harassment and Violence Prevention and Resolution (HVPR), Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI), wellness, and Official Languages (OL).
In this role, you will oversee the HVPR intake, case management and resolution processes and provide leadership for program and process improvements that strengthen prevention, resolution and support mechanisms. You will also lead and oversee the advancement of the NRC’s EDI strategy and programs and policies that foster a respectful, inclusive, healthy and bilingual workplace.
This role will appeal to a leader committed to an inclusive, barrier-free, respectful and safe work environment where people are enabled to reach their full potential.

Degree from a recognized university in a field relevant to the work to be performed.

- Significant experience in the field of human resources management in a government context.
- Demonstrated experience managing or advancing workplace harassment and violence prevention and resolution programs and/or initiatives under Part II of the Canada Labour Code, as amended by Bill C-65, alongside the Work Place Harassment and Violence Prevention Regulations.
- Recent experience leading or overseeing the development, implementation and continuous improvement of HR programs and/or initiatives, including related policies and/or procedures.
- Experience leading the development and execution of strategies and/or actions plans that advance organizational priorities, including the monitoring of progress and the reporting of results.

- Experience leading and managing people and teams.

Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Strong knowledge of HR management principles, practices and frameworks, and relevant government policies, legislation and central agency requirements.
- Extensive knowledge of Government of Canada harassment and violence prevention and resolution legislation, regulations, frameworks and best practices.
- Knowledge of barriers faced by equity deserving groups and progressive strategies, practices and approaches to advance EDI, official languages and workplace wellness.
- Demonstrated ability to identify and implement process improvements that enable organizational and program effectiveness including technology-enabled solutions.
- Ability to effectively plan, manage and deliver results including directing resources and overseeing projects from conception to execution.
- Ability to develop high-quality written products and presentations, and to present information confidently and persuasively to diverse audiences including senior leaders.

About CMHC
The work you do and the work we do together matters. We come to work every day with a common purpose: to contribute to a well-functioning housing system.
At CMHC, we hold ourselves accountable for our results and support our colleagues in their achievements. We thrive on collaboration, connecting across CMHC and involving the right people to get our work done. Our leadership style is guided by trust , where our leaders favour an adaptive approach based on the needs of their teams.
Join us and be part of a team that's committed to making a real difference and be part of something meaningful.
Our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion
We're committed to advancing employment equity and fostering an inclusive workplace. To reflect the diversity of Canada’s population, we encourage applications from women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQI+ individuals, veterans, and racialized peoples. We also welcome applications from all individuals eligible to work in Canada.
We are also committed to advancing reconciliation with Indigenous Peoples and supporting the meaningful inclusion of First Nations, Inuit, and Métis voices and priorities. While this position is hybrid requiring some in-office presence, a work from home arrangement may be considered for First Nations candidates on reserve or Indigenous candidates that reside further than 125KM from a CMHC office.
Learn more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion

We’ve got the purpose, the people and the perks you need for a fulfilling career. Here’s the comprehensive and generous benefits you get when you’re a contract employee:
- Accrued vacation.
- Annual individual performance bonus.
- Support towards your personal and professional growth with training, mentorship and more.
- While positions at CMHC require some in-office presence, alternative work arrangements may be considered for Indigenous candidates.
About the role
Join the CMHC Surveys team, in the Enumerator position. Bring your research and data collection skills to work as an Enumerator surveying Starts, Completions and Market Absorption Survey for Saint John, New Brunswick and surrounding area.
Hours of work will vary based on survey workload and geographic area. Approximately 30-35 hours per month – the work hours are not guaranteed hours and can vary within your assigned geographic area of Saint John, New Brunswick and surrounding area. The rate of pay is $23.89 per hour.
This is a temporary position with a duration of 6 months, with possibility of renewal.
What you'll do:
- Work with the Enumerator’s team to ensure the ongoing achievement of the survey for collecting high quality survey data within tight deadlines.
- Collect housing market data (via research, computer-assisted and/or telephone survey) in a timely and accurate manner, according to the requirements of CMHC, within your assigned geographic area.
- Visit construction sites and sales offices and communicate with developers, builders, and municipalities to collect the required data.
- Build and maintain professional rapport in all your interactions.
- Organize your work to ensure that you deliver quality work within tight deadlines.
What you should have:
- A High School diploma or higher.
- Strong communications skills (oral and written).
- Demonstrated strong numerical aptitude with a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail.
- Strong computer and typing skills.
- Strong organizational skills with the ability to work independently and achieve strong results with minimum supervision.
- High attention to accuracy and detail; ability to follow very detailed instructions.
- Knowledge of your assigned geographic area, ability to plan routes, ability to read a map and follow directions.
- Proficiency using internet and computer software tools such as research, email, video conference tools, data entry databases, and MS Excel skills are required.
- The ability to work from home with an access to internet (high-speed).
- A valid driver’s license and access to a reliable vehicle and insurance for $2,000,000 public liability and property damage would be required to complete travel for site visits.
It would be great if you also had:
- A related experience in field data collection or survey-based research and/or data entry.
- A previous experience with telephone interviewing, particularly making outbound calls.
- A related experience in property management and/or housing industry.
- Knowledgeable of Saint John, New Brunswick and surrounding area.

- Evaluate business and technical requirements and help select fit-for-purpose monitoring, observability, logging, and security analytics tools such as Zabbix, Dynatrace, SolarWinds, PRTG, Azure Monitor, Azure Log Analytics, Splunk, and Microsoft Sentinel.
- Configure and implement monitoring platforms and capabilities from the ground up, including discovery, agents, collectors, integrations, dashboards, service maps, health checks, log ingestion, alerts, and automated ticket creation.
- Maintain, administer, upgrade, and optimize monitoring tools and integrations to ensure reliable data collection, platform availability, appropriate capacity, security, and sustainable support.
- Define, document, and govern event and alert management processes and procedures, including standards for thresholds, severity, correlation, deduplication, suppression, escalation, ownership, and response.
- Detect, validate, enrich, correlate, and route events and alerts to identify service degradation and incidents before users are affected, reduce alert noise, and accelerate triage.
- Use monitoring data, logs, service-level indicators, and operational trends to identify detection gaps and improve service reliability, operational readiness, mean time to detect (MTTD), and mean time to restore or resolve (MTTR).
- Partner with application, infrastructure, security, service management, and vendor teams to establish monitoring requirements, onboard services, support incidents and post-incident reviews, and provide actionable operational insights.
What you should have:
- An undergraduate degree in Information Systems, Business, or a related field, and a minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in IT operations, including substantial hands-on responsibility for enterprise monitoring, observability, service reliability, or Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) (an equivalent combination of related education and/or experience will be considered).
- A demonstrated experience designing, configuring, and implementing monitoring or observability platforms from the ground up and supporting them through their operational lifecycle.
- A strong knowledge of infrastructure, application, cloud, network, service, log, synthetic, and availability monitoring, including practical experience defining dashboards, health indicators, alerts, and service-level measurements.
- Experience defining and operating event and alert management practices, including threshold design, alert tuning, correlation, deduplication, noise reduction, escalation, and on-call integration.
- The ability to assess monitoring requirements, compare tools, develop selection criteria, conduct proofs of concept, and recommend solutions based on coverage, integration, scalability, usability, security, and total cost of ownership.
- A working knowledge of ITIL and ITSM processes, particularly Incident, Major Incident, Problem, Change, Configuration, and Event Management; an ITIL Foundation certification is required.
- A record of using monitoring and operational data to improve MTTD, reduce MTTR, strengthen operational readiness, and increase service reliability in complex enterprise environments.
- Strong analytical, documentation, facilitation, and communication skills in both official languages (English and French), with the ability to work calmly across technical and business teams during high-pressure situations.
Technologies:
- A hands-on experience with several enterprise monitoring and observability platforms, such as Zabbix, Dynatrace, SolarWinds, PRTG, Azure Monitor, Azure Log Analytics, Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, or comparable tools.
- Experience integrating monitoring platforms with ServiceNow ITSM or comparable service management tools for event ingestion, alert enrichment, incident creation, routing, dashboards, and reporting.
- A familiarity with logs, metrics, traces, APIs, agents, collectors, scripting or automation, cloud and hybrid environments, and technologies that support end-to-end service visibility.
It will be great if you also had:
- Experience with observability engineering, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), service-level objectives, error budgets, or reliability practices in cloud and hybrid environments.
- Experience automating monitoring configuration, alert enrichment, remediation, or operational workflows using APIs, scripts, infrastructure as code, or orchestration tools.
- Experience coordinating vendors and managed service providers, leading monitoring onboarding or modernization initiatives, or developing operational readiness standards for new and changed services.
- Advanced ITIL, monitoring, observability, cloud, security, Splunk, Dynatrace, Microsoft, or SRE-related certifications.
Posting closing date: Note, the competition will remain active until filled.
Standby and Call Back duties are a requirement of this position and will be subject to CMHC policies, including the Standby and Call Back Pay Procedure.
