We know that applying for a new job can be both exciting and daunting, and we appreciate your effort. Learn more about our hiring process . If you are selected for an interview or testing, please advise us if you require an accommodation.
If you applied before and you were not successful don’t worry – we're always posting new positions, so don’t hesitate to give it another shot. We’re excited to see what you bring to the table this time around!

2482012.text: The Publication Officer is the hands-on production and quality gate for PBO publications. As a member of a small and agile team, the incumbent makes sure that every report leaves the PBO accurate in both official languages, consistent between its English and French versions, visually polished, accessible and on time. They revise and format reports, publish them on the PBO website, help analysts present clear charts and tables, and build the style guide and templates that keep PBO products consistent. They have a love of language and a strong eye for design, enjoy tinkering with digital tools to make production faster and more reliable, and are motivated to grow in publishing, web production and accessibility.

2482013.text:
Staffing process 26-PB-18
Position Student, part-time
Pay $18.69 to $38.38 per hour, based on academic level (college, undergraduate, master's or doctoral), in accordance with the Treasury Board student rates of pay
Open to Canadian citizens, permanent residents and holders of a valid work permit who are legally able to work in Canada
Location Ottawa, hybrid
Schedule 15 to 30 hours per week, with flexibility to accommodate academic commitments and operational needs
Term January, 2027 to January, 2028, with the possibility of extension
Language Bilingual imperative (CBC)
Closing date November 26, 12:00 PM Eastern Time
We're looking for a creative, bilingual student with excellent writing skills who can help make complex economic and fiscal information clear, accessible and engaging for Parliamentarians, journalists and Canadians.
From news releases and digital storytelling to videos, animation and social media, this is an opportunity to contribute fresh ideas while gaining valuable experience in a unique parliamentary environment.
The Parliamentary Budget Office (PBO) provides independent economic and financial analysis to the Senate and House of Commons, analyzes the estimates of the government and, if requested, estimates the financial cost of any proposal over which Parliament has jurisdiction. The PBO is committed to serving Parliament with integrity and professionalism by providing independent, credible and non-partisan economic and financial analysis on a timely basis.
What you'll do
Working under the direction of the Director of Corporate Services, you will provide support in the following areas:
- Writing and editing: Draft news releases, website content, backgrounders and other communications materials in English and French. Final versions follow the PBO's translation and revision process.
- Editorial support: Support the plain-language review of reports for clarity, readability and consistency, in collaboration with analysts and the communications team.
- Creative digital content: Develop ideas for social media posts, short videos, animations, infographics and other digital media assets.
- Media and social media monitoring: Review news coverage, commentary and social media discussions relating to the PBO. Identify emerging issues, relevant trends and possible opportunities for engagement for staff review.
- Communications support: Support staff with report releases, the preparation of responses to media inquiries, key messages and other communications activities.
Essential qualifications
- Full-time enrolment in a college, undergraduate or graduate program in journalism, communications, digital media or a related field.
- Bilingual imperative, assessed through House of Commons language testing: Reading comprehension: Superior level (C) Written expression: Intermediate level (B) Oral interaction: Superior level (C)
- Excellent writing, editing and communication skills.
- Creativity, sound judgment and strong attention to detail.
- Familiarity with social media platforms and digital content creation.
- Ability to work collaboratively, manage priorities and respect the PBO's independent, non-partisan mandate.
Asset qualifications
- Experience with video production, animation, graphic design or multimedia storytelling.
Why join the PBO?
You'll work alongside experienced analysts on issues that matter to Canadians, including housing, health care, government spending and the economy. If you have an interest in public affairs, journalism, economics or government, you'll build your editorial and digital communications skills while helping make important research more accessible.
We know that great ideas come from everywhere. The PBO is committed to building a team with varied lived experiences, perspectives, ways of thinking and cultural backgrounds. We welcome applications from students with diverse experiences and creative approaches.
Conditions of employment
- Obtain and maintain reliability status.
- Maintain the confidentiality of embargoed reports and other information obtained in the course of employment.
- Maintain political neutrality consistent with the PBO's non-partisan mandate.
- Remain enrolled in full-time studies for the duration of the appointment.
- Satisfactory references and proof of enrolment.
How to apply
Apply through the PBO careers portal. Create a profile and follow the online instructions to submit your résumé, proof of full-time enrolment (unofficial copies are accepted at this stage) and two samples of your writing or creative digital work by the closing date. You may apply in English or French. For questions about this opportunity, contact pbohr@parl.gc.ca .
If you are currently employed in the federal public service or by a parliamentary entity, please identify your employment status (indeterminate, determinate, student or casual), substantive group and level, and current second language evaluation results in your application.
Accommodation: The PBO is committed to an accessible, barrier-free selection process. If you require accommodation at any stage, please contact pbohr@parl.gc.ca . Information you provide will be treated confidentially.
Privacy: Personal information you provide will be used only for this selection process.
Only those selected for further consideration will be contacted. We thank all those who apply.

The Canadian Air Transport Security Authority (CATSA) has 1 (one) exciting determinate opportunity up to April 23, 2027 within the Technology branch at the CATSA HQ.
This position represents an opportunity for career-driven individuals seeking a position within an organization that inspires growth and promotes excellence to make a difference and contribute to CATSA’s unique culture as it strives to excel in air transport security.
Why is CATSA a great fit for you?
CATSA is a world leader in aviation security, mandated to protect the public by delivering security screening operations at 89 designated airports across Canada. As a Crown corporation, CATSA is accountable to Parliament through the Minister of Transport.
We champion innovation and creativity and offer a welcoming and inclusive workplace where employees can be their true selves and take pride in being part of a mission that matters.
If you are a motivated professional seeking a position within a multifunctional and collaborative environment and you are looking for the next great adventure, CATSA is the place for you!
Summary of responsibilities:
The Data Engineer is responsible for analyzing, developing, implementing, and supporting CATSA’s business data solutions such as data engineering, Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) development, Power platform (Power BI, PowerApps, Power Automate) development, Artificial Intelligence (AIOps)/Machine Learning (MLOps) Operations. The Data Engineer performs all other duties and responsibilities related to the position as required.
Key Tasks and Responsibilities:
- Design and create interactive dashboards and reports using Power BI to provide data-driven insights and facilitate decision-making.
- Develop custom applications using PowerApps to meet specific business requirements.
- Automate business workflows using Power Automate to enhance operational efficiency and reduce manual tasks.
- Design, develop, and maintain scalable and efficient data pipelines support data integration, processing, and analytics.
- Implement and manage ETL ( Extract, Transform, Load ) processes to ensure data quality and reliability across multiple data sources.
What you need to succeed To qualify for the position, you must have:
- Graduation from a recognized university with a specialization in Computer Science, Information Technology/Management, or another specialty relevant to the duties of the position, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Selection process number: 2090-CMN-26-OC-072
Your place at the Museum
We value diversity and believe we benefit from working in a place where everyone feels included and where the unique qualities and strengths inherent in a diverse workforce are combined. We welcome applications from persons who may identify as a member of one or more other equity seeking groups (for e.g. women, visible minorities, Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+, religious or cultural minority).
You have a place at the Museum!
About the position
Under the supervision of the Head, Contracts, Procurement and Risk Management, the Officer, Contracts and Procurement procures goods and services for the Museum while adhering to the Museum’s Delegation of Financial Signing Authorities, policies, procedure, legislative requirements, national and international trade agreements and treaty obligations. They produce and review procurement and financial documents, maintain various electronic/paper databases and files, answer enquiries from staff regarding procurement activities and matters and perform duties assigned related to the production of financial documents and analytical ad-hoc reports.
Working at the museum means :
- Contributing to an engaging mission as well as exciting projects and challenges
- An inclusive, friendly and safe work environment
- A competitive salary established by collective agreements
- Access to federal public service group insurance and pension plans
Eligibility criteria
This position is open to all Employees of the Canadian Museum of Nature and any members of the public who meet the qualifications below. Candidates must be legally entitled to work in Canada.
Education and training:
Completion of a post-secondary education in a field relevant to the position, or an equivalent combination of education, experience and training.
Language requirements:
English and French are essential Bilingual Imperative (BBB/BBB)
Experience:
1-2 years of experience in:
- in providing interpretation and advice or guidance to managers and clients on the procedures, policies and legislation related to the procurement of goods, services or construction;
- n administering procurement processes of a variety of goods and services using electronic tendering (Bonfire, CanadaBuys, Merx.etc.);
- preparing, reviewing, or approving standard contract terms and conditions.
- preparing, reviewing or approving tender documents, statements of work or requirements and evaluation plans;
- overseeing the bid evaluation process, recommendation of bidders for contract award and awarding contracts;
- conducting financial management administrative duties such as entering financial transactions in a system, processing contracts, processing purchase orders, or auditing financial information against financial policies.
And experience in:
- the use of software applications including Adobe and Microsoft 365, with advanced knowledge of Excel and Word;
- providing services to clients in a fast-paced, high-volume, or multi-tasking environment;
- acquiring goods or services or construction using various procurement methodologies within the Canadian federal government or other public Procurement and Contracting environment considered an asset.
Interested? APPLY!
The Canadian Museum of Nature is committed to inclusive and barrier-free selection processes and work environments. If you are invited to participate in the selection process, we encourage you to advise us of any accommodation you may require. This information will be treated as confidential.
The Statement of Qualifications, providing greater detail about the skills, knowledge and aptitudes needed for this role, can be obtained by contacting the Museum at competition@nature.ca.
All candidates must submit a cover letter and curriculum vitae outlining how their experience and training meet the requirements listed above.
Send your application by filling in the application form where you can upload your cover letter, curriculum vitae and any other required documents.
